title: seed.sql silently reopens ANY future revoke-based control -- the P14.3 fix is a hand-maintained list with no test and no check behind it
exploit: 1. A future migration adds any revoke-based control (the established pattern in this schema: 20260903170000 and 20260903190000 are both of this shape). 2. Nobody edits supabase/seed.sql. 3. `pnpm test` passes, CI passes, `compare-database-posture.mjs --check` passes. 4. The next `supabase db reset`, `supabase start`, or DEPLOYMENT.md step-4 rebuild applies seed.sql last and the control is gone. The reopened privilege is then reachable by any authenticated PostgREST caller, exactly as the forged-emissions insert was.
impact: Every operator and developer of the platform, and ultimately the regulatory record. The class of control this affects is precisely the class used for the things RLS cannot express -- unforgeable emissions figures, TRUNCATE on an append-only compliance ledger. The remediation for the P14.1 blocker was placed on a foundation that reproduces the blocker's own failure mode for the next control added.
freshEnvironment: It is only observable on a fresh environment -- I proved it on a database created from nothing (`create database seed_probe_p14`) with no history, applying only the bootstrap grants, a synthetic migration, and the committed supabase/seed.sql. The throwaway database was dropped (`drop database seed_probe_p14`; `select datname from pg_database where datname like 'seed_probe%'` returns empty).

verdicts.reasoning:
REACHABILITY: refuted. The exploit's step 1 is "a future migration adds a revoke-based control" — code that does not exist at commit 0679e60. There is no actor, route, or capability today.

(A) Two load-bearing factual claims in the finding are wrong.

1. "no test and no check behind it" / "the TRUNCATE revoke of 20260903170000 already has zero automated coverage" is FALSE. scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:402-413 defines check `truncate_granted_to_api_roles`, which runs in the one-database `--check <dsn>` mode and is GENERIC, not a hand-maintained list:
  select table_name || ' | ' || grantee from information_schema.role_table_grants
  where table_schema='public' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated') and privilege_type='TRUNCATE'
Any non-empty result fails the run. It covers future tables automatically. It is deliberately paired with `api_roles_hold_their_grants` (same file:383-399) so it cannot pass vacuously on a grant-less restore. The finding's own grep was scoped `tests/ --include=*.ts` and never looked at scripts/.
Additionally, the two-DB mode has `effective_grants` (file:122-135) and `function_grants` (file:171-181), both critical:true, comparing the exact table ACL set and full proacl.

2. The coupling obligation is documented, not merely assumed safe. docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:567-569, in the "Rebuilding on a fresh database" recipe: "If a future migration adds another revoke-based control, it has to be added there too." Step 6 of that same recipe (lines 572-578) mandates `node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check "<dsn>"` after every fresh rebuild and names `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` as the check that catches a re-granted surface. So the finding's step-3 premise ("compare-database-posture.mjs --check passes") is only true for the write-privilege case, not TRUNCATE, and the rebuild path the finding cites as the trigger is the same path that mandates the check.

(B) No present-tense reachable instance. Live local DB, PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 54322 -U postgres -d postgres:
 - calculation_results|authenticated|REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER  (and identically for anon) — no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, no TRUNCATE.
 - record_calculation_result(...)|postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres — service_role only.
 - TRUNCATE appears for neither anon nor authenticated on any of the 22 public tables.
 - pg_default_acl: postgres|public|r|postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres anon=arwdxtm/postgres authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres — anon/authenticated lack `D`, which is precisely seed.sql:106-110 having taken effect. All three named controls are in force.

(C) I hunted for a real (non-hypothetical) instance of the class and found one that is inert. Seven public RPCs are granted EXECUTE to `authenticated` only by their migrations (grep 'grant execute on function public.' over supabase/migrations/*.sql returns authenticated/service_role only, never anon), yet the live ACLs show anon=X/postgres on all seven — seed.sql:23's blanket function grant. I probed each as anon inside a real transaction (begin; set local role anon; set local request.jwt.claims='{"role":"anon"}'; <call>; rollback;):
  create_organization_with_owner -> ERROR: requires an authenticated caller.
  list_org_members -> ERROR: Not a member of this organization.
  record_declaration_filed -> ERROR: requires an authenticated caller.
  record_shared_data_consumption -> ERROR: requires an authenticated caller.
  accept_organization_invitation -> ERROR: requires an authenticated caller.
  accept_sharing_grant_invitation -> ERROR: requires an authenticated caller
  sharing_counterparty_org_names() -> empty result.
Every one is defended in-body against a null auth.uid(). No reachable effect.

(D) Blast radius is overstated. seed.sql:1-4 states it is never applied to a hosted Supabase project; the CLI runs it against a local instance, and DEPLOYMENT.md step 4 is a manual recovery step gated by step 6's posture check. It is not on any production-serving path, so "ultimately the regulatory record" is not supported.

RESIDUAL (why LOW, not NOT_A_DEFECT): the finding does correctly identify that no generic self-check exists for a FUTURE write-privilege or function-EXECUTE revoke — only TRUNCATE has one. That is a real hardening opportunity (generalize the `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` pattern into an expected-ACL assertion), but it is a documented process obligation about code that does not exist, not a reachable security defect in this release candidate.

I re-ran the evidence myself in a database created from nothing (`create database refute_seed_p14`, dropped afterwards; `select ... from pg_database where datname like 'refute%' or 'seed_probe%'` now returns NONE).

MECHANISM CONFIRMED, byte for byte.
supabase/seed.sql:21-23 is `grant all on all tables|sequences|functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role`, and :25-32 sets the same as default privileges. The re-assertion block at :83-101 is a `do $$` guarded on two literal object names — `to_regclass('public.calculation_results')` and `to_regprocedure('public.record_calculation_result(uuid,uuid,uuid,text,jsonb,text,text,jsonb,jsonb,text,uuid)')`. It is object-name-specific, exactly as the finding says.

Probe 1 — synthetic future revoke-based migration (same shape as 20260903190000), then the committed seed.sql applied verbatim with `psql -f supabase/seed.sql`:
  AFTER MIGRATION  authenticated: SELECT,TRUNCATE,REFERENCES,TRIGGER
                   acl: postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  AFTER seed.sql   authenticated: INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE,DELETE,REFERENCES,TRIGGER
                   anon:          INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE,DELETE,REFERENCES,TRIGGER
                   future_trusted_write acl: postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres anon=X/postgres authenticated=X/postgres
Identical to the reported output.

Probe 2 — the decisive control. I built one table literally named `calculation_results` (RLS, select/update/delete policies, writes revoked) and one named `audit_ledger` (append-only: INSERT policy, UPDATE/DELETE revoked — the shape of 20260903160000), in the same database, then applied the same seed:
  calculation_results authenticated, after seed: SELECT,REFERENCES,TRIGGER   <- held, because :85 names it
  audit_ledger        authenticated, before seed: INSERT,SELECT,REFERENCES,TRIGGER
  audit_ledger        authenticated, after  seed: INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE,DELETE,REFERENCES,TRIGGER   <- reopened
That isolates the defect to the hand-maintained name list, not to anything about my synthetic setup.

NO CHECK BEHIND IT — confirmed. `--check` runs only SELF_CHECKS (scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:510, :573). Against the probe-2 database every privilege-relevant self-check reported [OK]: `rls_without_policies`, `tables_without_insert_policy`, `api_roles_hold_their_grants`, `truncate_granted_to_api_roles`, `security_definer_without_search_path` — while `audit_ledger` UPDATE/DELETE and `future_trusted_write` EXECUTE were reopened. (Three other checks failed for unrelated reasons: my stripped-down db has no `auth` schema.) `grep -rniE "role_table_grants|has_table_privilege|has_function_privilege|proacl|relacl|TRUNCATE" tests/ --include=*.ts` returns no privilege assertion; the only coverage is behavioral and object-specific — tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts:886, "(4) grants no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on calculation_results to anon or authenticated at all".

CORRECTIONS THAT LOWER THE SEVERITY TO MEDIUM.
1. The TRUNCATE half of the finding is wrong. seed.sql:104-110 revokes TRUNCATE generically (`revoke truncate on all tables in schema public`, plus both default-privileges forms), and scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:402-411 `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` is a fully generic assertion over `information_schema.role_table_grants`, named in docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md step 6 as one of the two checks that catch a re-granted surface. The finding's own probe output shows TRUNCATE absent after the seed, which contradicts its own "zero automated coverage" wording. TRUNCATE is in fact the one control that is generically covered on both sides.
2. There is an accidental partial tripwire: a new RLS table with no INSERT policy trips `tables_without_insert_policy` (:343-380) until someone adds it to that check's own hand-maintained exclusion list (`'organizations', 'memberships', 'calculation_results'`) — which is what happened to calculation_results. So the gap is real but reaches `--check` clean only for shapes that dodge it: function-EXECUTE-only controls, and UPDATE/DELETE-only revokes. I verified both dodge it.
3. Production exposure is narrower than "every operator... and the regulatory record". seed.sql is not applied by `supabase db push`; it reaches a hosted database only via docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:556 step 4 of the fresh-rebuild recipe. And that risk is already written down at :566-568: "If a future migration adds another revoke-based control, it has to be added there too."

Net: no control is presently broken in this release candidate — I verified both existing ones survive the seed. The defect is a real, reproducible, unenforced coupling that will silently reopen the next revoke-based control added, with nothing in `pnpm test` or `--check` to catch the two most likely shapes. That is a latent process foot-gun, not a live exploitable path, so MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED, BUT SEVERITY AND THREE EVIDENTIARY CLAIMS ARE WRONG.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
supabase/seed.sql:21-23 is a blanket `grant all on all tables|sequences|functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role`, and the re-assertion block at :83-110 covers only calculation_results (I/U/D), record_calculation_result(...) (EXECUTE), and TRUNCATE. A future revoke-based control on any other object would not be re-asserted. That much is mechanically true from the file.

I also found live evidence the finder did NOT report, which is stronger than their synthetic throwaway-DB proof. On the real local DB:
  psql -tAc "select p.proname||' :: '||array_to_string(p.proacl::text[],' ') from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='public' and p.proacl::text like '%anon=X%' order by 1;"
  accept_organization_invitation :: postgres=X/postgres authenticated=X/postgres anon=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  accept_sharing_grant_invitation :: ... anon=X/postgres ...
  create_organization_with_owner :: ... anon=X/postgres ...
  list_org_members :: ... anon=X/postgres ...
  record_declaration_filed :: ... anon=X/postgres ...
  record_shared_data_consumption :: ... anon=X/postgres ...
  sharing_counterparty_org_names :: ... anon=X/postgres ...
Every one of those is granted to `authenticated` (and sometimes service_role) ONLY by its migration — e.g. 20260828080000:108 `grant execute ... create_organization_with_owner(text,text,text[]) to authenticated;`, 20260902150000:195-196 grants sharing_counterparty_org_names to authenticated and service_role only. The `anon=X` entries come from seed.sql:23. So the class is live, not hypothetical.

WHAT IS FALSE IN THE FINDING
(1) "the TRUNCATE revoke of 20260903170000 already has zero automated coverage" — false. scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:402-411 is a check named `truncate_granted_to_api_roles`, whose stated `why` is verbatim "the P14 revoke (20260903170000) must survive a restore". DEPLOYMENT.md:571-576 makes `node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check "<dsn>"` a MANDATORY step 6 of the fresh-rebuild recipe and names that exact check plus `tables_without_insert_policy` as "the two checks that catch a re-granted surface". BACKUP_RESTORE.md:520-533,633,645 does the same for restores. The finder grepped only `tests/ --include=*.ts` and never looked at scripts/ops/.
(2) "a re-assertion block ... that names exactly three controls by hand" — false for one of the three. seed.sql:104-110 is class-wide, not object-named: `revoke truncate on all tables in schema public from anon, authenticated;` plus `alter default privileges` twice (including `for role postgres`). Any FUTURE table is covered automatically. Verified live: `select count(*) ... privilege_type='TRUNCATE' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated')` returns 0.
(3) Exploit step 4, "the next `supabase db reset`, `supabase start` ... applies seed.sql last" — not supported in this repo. supabase/config.toml:66-73 sets `[db.seed] sql_paths = ["./seed/*.sql"]`, overriding the CLI default of `./seed.sql`, and `supabase/seed/` does not exist (`ls supabase/` shows migrations, seed.sql, snippets, templates, .temp, .branches — no `seed/`). That override has been present since commit 827d3a7. seed.sql reaches a database only by explicit `psql -f` — .github/workflows/ci.yml:315 and DEPLOYMENT.md step 4:556. So two of the three routes the exploit chain names do not exist here.

ALREADY-MITIGATED / SEVERITY
- No control is broken in this release candidate. Verified live: calculation_results grants to anon/authenticated are exactly SELECT, REFERENCES, TRIGGER (no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE); record_calculation_result acl is `postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres`; zero TRUNCATE grants to API roles. All three intended postures hold on the database seed.sql was actually applied to.
- The coupling is documented where it matters, not silently: DEPLOYMENT.md:561-568 states "seed.sql runs LAST and its blanket `grant all` would otherwise undo every deliberate `revoke`" and explicitly instructs "If a future migration adds another revoke-based control, it has to be added there too", immediately followed by the mandatory posture check.
- seed.sql never runs against the hosted project on the normal deploy path (its own header:1-17; config.toml override above). The only path to production is the documented fresh-rebuild recipe, which mandates step 6's posture check on the very next line.
- CI applies seed.sql and then runs the security suites, which is precisely how the P14.1 blocker was caught (tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts:724 "P14.1 -- the calculation-result write boundary"). The exploit's step 3 ("pnpm test passes, CI passes") therefore only holds for a future control that ships with no test at all.

So this is a real defense-in-depth/maintainability hazard on a security-relevant file, with a documented warning and a scripted posture check already standing behind it, and no currently reopened control. It is not a HIGH. I am not refuting it outright because the blanket-grant class demonstrably already over-grants seven authenticated-only RPCs to anon on the live local DB, so the "hand-maintained list is incomplete" claim is literally true today — but only in local/CI environments, on auth.uid()-gated SECURITY DEFINER functions, not in production. LOW, and it would be MEDIUM if the posture check and the runbook warning did not exist.

title: `compare-database-posture.mjs --check` -- the verification DEPLOYMENT.md names for this exact defect -- passes on a database carrying the original P14.1 blocker, and is run by nothing automated
exploit: Run the DEPLOYMENT.md 'Rebuilding on a fresh database' recipe on a recovery target, skip or mis-order step 4, or apply a seed that predates the current revoke set. Step 6's `--check` reports every self-check OK on a database where `authenticated` holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on calculation_results and EXECUTE on record_calculation_result. The operator records a verified rebuild.
impact: Whoever runs a disaster recovery, and every declarant whose filed declarations are frozen from calculation_results afterwards. The one automated acceptance test the P14.3 remediation points at as its safety net does not assert the property the remediation exists to preserve, and 'enforced continuously' overstates a script that runs only when a human types it.
freshEnvironment: Yes -- it is a property of the script's SQL and of the CI/package.json wiring, both committed at 0679e60, not of any database state. The live proof above ran against the current local database inside begin/rollback; I verified the grants returned to SELECT,REFERENCES,TRIGGER and the RPC ACL to postgres/service_role only after the ROLLBACK.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the core claim; I reproduced it independently and more broadly than the finding did.

CODE. scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:251-430 defines exactly nine SELF_CHECKS; main() at lines 505-596 runs ONLY SELF_CHECKS under `--check`. No check inspects table privileges other than `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` (line 402, `privilege_type = 'TRUNCATE'` only) and `api_roles_hold_their_grants` (line 388, fires only when a role holds ZERO grants, so adding grants can only make it pass harder). No check inspects function ACLs at all. `tables_without_insert_policy` (line 351) queries pg_policies, not grants, and exempts 'calculation_results' at line 371.

LIVE PROOF (my own, all nine checks, inside a real BEGIN/ROLLBACK against 127.0.0.1:54322):
  before_calc_privs: REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER
  before_rcr_acl: postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  begin; grant insert,update,delete on public.calculation_results to anon,authenticated;
         grant execute on function public.record_calculation_result(uuid,uuid,uuid,text,jsonb,text,text,jsonb,jsonb,text,uuid) to anon,authenticated;
  inside_calc_privs: DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,UPDATE
  inside_rcr_acl: postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres anon=X/postgres authenticated=X/postgres
  SELF_CHECK 1..9 offending-row counts: 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0
  rollback;
  after_calc_privs: REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER ; after_rcr_acl: postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
Zero rows on every check means `--check` prints "RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES" and exits 0 on a database in the blocker state. Stronger than the finding claimed (it tested two checks; I tested all nine).

REACHABILITY LENS — this is where the finding is half wrong, and it matters for severity:
  (a) With the table grant restored, an ordinary member's direct INSERT is still refused:
      NOTICE: DIRECT INSERT REFUSED: 42501 / new row violates row-level security policy for table "calculation_results"
      (RLS is on; the only policy is calculation_results_select_own_org | SELECT.) So the re-granted TABLE surface the finding leads with is NOT exploitable.
  (b) With EXECUTE restored, it is: as `set local role authenticated` with jwt sub b2aee125-3c1a-4a86-b748-920095c3b549,
      select ... record_calculation_result(..., p_embedded_emissions_tco2e '0.000001', ...) -> "RPC: OK id=7657d43d-6ac2-4706-966b-d4020d6ff0eb", inside_forged_rows: 1.
      Rolled back; after_forged_rows: 0, privileges and ACL verified restored.
  So exactly one re-granted surface reproduces the P14.1 forgery, and it is the one no self-check covers.

DOCS. docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:576-577 verbatim: "`truncate_granted_to_api_roles` and `tables_without_insert_policy` are the two checks that catch a re-granted surface." That statement is false: the second check reads policies, never grants, and exempts the very table concerned. docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1449-1450 "Also now enforced continuously" is an overstatement — `grep -rn compare-database-posture .github/ tests/ package.json scripts/` returns hits only at scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:22,23,515,516 (its own usage text) and in docs/. Nothing automated invokes it.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG (why I corrected severity down from HIGH):
  1. Its impact claim that "the one automated acceptance test ... does not assert the property" is false. tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts:885-937, case (4), calls the RPC as ownerClient and asserts rpcError?.message contains "permission denied" — precisely the property. .github/workflows/ci.yml re-applies supabase/seed.sql at line 315 on a freshly built database and runs `pnpm test` at line 365, so that assertion does run on a fresh environment in CI. An independent automated guard exists; the ops script is blind, but the property is not unguarded.
  2. Its lead evidence (table INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE re-grant) is not attacker-reachable — RLS denies it, proved above.
  3. No attacker path exists on the release candidate as built. supabase/seed.sql:82-100 re-asserts both revokes after the blanket grants, so `supabase db reset` yields the correct posture (verified: baseline privileges are SELECT/REFERENCES/TRIGGER only, RPC ACL postgres+service_role only). The exploit needs an operator to deviate from DEPLOYMENT.md step 4 (whose load-bearing ordering that document explicitly explains) or a restore that drops ACLs.

SUPPORTING EVIDENCE THE FINDING MISSED, which is why I would not drop this below MEDIUM: on the live seeded database, `select pg_get_userbyid(defaclrole), defaclobjtype, defaclacl from pg_default_acl ...` returns `postgres | f | postgres=X/postgres anon=X/postgres authenticated=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres`. seed.sql revokes TRUNCATE from the default table privileges (lines 106-110) but never narrows the default FUNCTION privileges it granted at line 32. So any future migration-created public function is EXECUTE-able by `authenticated` by default, and `--check` still reports POSTURE MATCHES — the same blindness with a routine trigger, not just operator error.

VERDICT: real defect, correctly located in OPERATIONS (a documented verification step that does not verify what the runbook says it verifies, plus a false sentence in DEPLOYMENT.md). Not attacker-reachable on the candidate as built, and covered by a real CI test. MEDIUM, not HIGH.

I re-verified every claim independently; all of them are correct.

1. SELF_CHECKS contents and line numbers — exact. `grep -n 'name: "'` on scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs gives SELF_CHECKS starting at line 252 with exactly nine checks: auth_schema_and_helpers_present (254), auth_user_foreign_keys_present (277), policy_functions_resolve (301), tables_without_rls (314), rls_without_policies (327), tables_without_insert_policy (344), api_roles_hold_their_grants (383), truncate_granted_to_api_roles (402), security_definer_without_search_path (414). Reading all nine SQL bodies: none references table-level INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants on calculation_results, and none references function EXECUTE grants at all. `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` filters `privilege_type = 'TRUNCATE'` only (covers 20260903170000); `api_roles_hold_their_grants` only fires when a role holds ZERO grants in public. Nothing covers 20260903190000, whose statements are `revoke insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results` (line 147) and `revoke all on function public.record_calculation_result(...)` / `grant execute ... to service_role` (lines 353-357).

2. The calculation_results exemption — exact. scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:371 reads `'organizations', 'memberships', 'calculation_results'` inside `tables_without_insert_policy`'s NOT IN list.

3. Live proof — reproduced exactly, inside a real BEGIN/ROLLBACK against 127.0.0.1:54322.
BEFORE authenticated privs on calculation_results: REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER; record_calculation_result proacl {postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}.
Inside the transaction, after `grant insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results to authenticated;` and `grant execute on function public.record_calculation_result(uuid,uuid,uuid,text,jsonb,text,text,jsonb,jsonb,text,uuid) to authenticated;`:
  INSIDE privs = DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,UPDATE
  truncate_granted_to_api_roles rows = 0   (PASSES)
  api_roles_hold_their_grants rows = 0     (PASSES)
  tables_without_insert_policy rows = 0    (PASSES)
After ROLLBACK: privs back to REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER and proacl back to {postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}. No write committed.

4. `--check` runs SELF_CHECKS ONLY. scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:524 `if (!selfOnly)` gates the entire CHECKS loop, so `effective_grants` (line 123) and `function_grants` (line 169) — the two comparison checks that WOULD have caught this — never run in the single-database mode DEPLOYMENT.md prescribes.

5. Documentation claims — exact. docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:574 `node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check "<dsn>"` followed at 576-577 by "`truncate_granted_to_api_roles` and `tables_without_insert_policy` are the two checks that catch a re-granted surface." Neither does. docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1449 "Also now enforced continuously: `compare-database-posture.mjs`'s `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` self-check, which a restore must pass."

6. No automation. `grep -rn compare-database-posture .github/ tests/ package.json scripts/ docs/` returns hits only in docs/ (P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md, BACKUP_RESTORE.md, DEPLOYMENT.md) and in the script's own usage strings at lines 22-23 and 515-516. package.json "scripts" (lines 5-15) contains dev/build/postbuild/start/test/test:watch/test:e2e/typecheck/regulatory:verify — no ops entry. .github/workflows/ci.yml has no such step. "Enforced continuously" is false.

One mitigation the finding understates but does not invalidate: the property IS asserted by automated tests elsewhere — tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts:792-940 expects "permission denied" for member INSERTs into calculation_results, and supabase/seed.sql:86-110 re-asserts both revoke sets after its blanket grants. So a repo-level regression is caught by CI. What is NOT caught is exactly the scenario the finding describes: an operator rebuilding a recovery target who deviates from step 4 or applies an older seed, then runs the step-6 `--check` and sees every self-check OK on a database where `authenticated` holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on calculation_results and EXECUTE on record_calculation_result. That is the same class as the original P14.1 blocker, and the named verification is blind to it.

Severity: HIGH stands. The gap is not directly user-exploitable at 0679e60, but DEPLOYMENT.md actively instructs the operator to treat a passing `--check` as proof of the exact property it cannot see, and the audit's "enforced continuously" claim is untrue.

I tried to refute this and could not falsify its mechanical core; I did find mitigations that materially reduce its severity.

CONFIRMED BY MY OWN CHECKS:

1. `--check` runs SELF_CHECKS only. scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:506 `const selfOnly = args[0] === "--check"`, and main() enters the two-DSN CHECKS loop only under `if (!selfOnly)` (line 521). The grant/function-grant comparisons that would catch a re-granted surface live in CHECKS (lines 51-244) and never run in `--check` mode.

2. The nine SELF_CHECKS (lines 252-430) contain nothing covering 20260903190000's revokes. `tables_without_insert_policy` explicitly exempts `calculation_results` (line 371); `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` (line 402) filters `privilege_type = 'TRUNCATE'` only; `api_roles_hold_their_grants` (line 383) fires only when a role holds ZERO grants.

3. I reproduced the blindness live against the local database, inside a real BEGIN...ROLLBACK, running the script's own self-check SQL verbatim:
   before:SELECT,REFERENCES,TRIGGER
   (grant insert,update,delete on public.calculation_results to authenticated; grant execute on record_calculation_result(...) to authenticated)
   inside_grants:INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE,DELETE,REFERENCES,TRIGGER
   truncate_check_rows:0
   api_roles_hold_grants_rows:0
   tables_without_insert_policy_rows:0
   secdef_rows:0
   tables_without_rls:0
   ROLLBACK
   after:SELECT,REFERENCES,TRIGGER
   after_acl:{postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}
   Every self-check reports clean while `authenticated` holds the full write surface plus EXECUTE on the RPC. State verified restored after ROLLBACK.

4. Wiring: `grep -rn compare-database-posture` (excluding node_modules/.git) returns hits only in docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md, docs/runbooks/{BACKUP_RESTORE,DEPLOYMENT}.md, and the script itself. package.json scripts (lines 5-15) are dev/build/postbuild/start/test/test:watch/test:e2e/typecheck/regulatory:verify — no ops entry. .github/workflows/ci.yml never invokes it.

5. docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:576-577 reads verbatim: "`truncate_granted_to_api_roles` and `tables_without_insert_policy` are the two checks that catch a re-granted surface." Per (2) and (3) neither catches the re-granted surface that actually caused the P14.1 incident. That sentence is false as written, and it is the only posture verification in the "Rebuilding on a fresh database" recipe (steps 1-6; step 5 is regulatory:verify, step 6 is this).

MITIGATIONS THE FINDER MISSED — why I downgrade HIGH to MEDIUM:

a. supabase/seed.sql now re-asserts all three revokes at its end (a `do $$` block guarded on to_regclass/to_regprocedure that re-runs `revoke insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results from anon, authenticated`, `revoke all on function record_calculation_result(...) from public, anon, authenticated`, `grant execute ... to service_role`, plus `revoke truncate on all tables` and two `alter default privileges ... revoke truncate`). So the DEPLOYMENT.md recipe as written at 0679e60 does NOT produce the re-granted state. Skipping step 4 entirely leaves zero grants, which `api_roles_hold_their_grants` DOES catch loudly. Reaching the bad state requires an out-of-tree/older seed or a future revoke-migration whose author ignores seed.sql's own explicit warning — a real risk, but not an ordinary documented operation at this commit.

b. The claim that "the one automated acceptance test ... does not assert the property" is misleading about the actual safety net. tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts, "P14.1 -- the calculation-result write boundary", cases (1)-(5) (lines ~790-960) assert exactly this property against real PostgREST: member INSERT with a forged emissions value expects `permission denied`, and case (4) at line 886 additionally asserts the RPC is unreachable by `authenticated` while working for `service_role`. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs this on every branch push against a freshly built database that follows the same recipe, re-applying seed.sql last at line 315 and then running `pnpm test` with local Supabase env. seed.sql's own comment names that test as the guard and records that it failed in CI on 2026-09-03 exactly as it should have. So the property IS continuously enforced on fresh environments — just not by this script.

WHAT SURVIVES: a genuine operations/documentation defect confined to the manual DR/rebuild path, where no vitest runs and the runbook points the operator at a verification that provably cannot see the failure it names. P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1449's "Also now enforced continuously" is likewise overstated for a script no automation invokes. Not a release blocker; a runbook sentence that must be corrected and two self-checks that should be added (calculation_results write grants for anon/authenticated; record_calculation_result ACL).

title: seed.sql grants `anon` EXECUTE on six SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that every migration restricted to `authenticated` -- six of the seven function revokes are not re-asserted
evidence:
supabase/seed.sql:23 `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;`. The re-assertion block (seed.sql:83-101) names one function. No migration anywhere grants anything to anon: `grep -rniE '\banon\b' supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -iE 'grant|revoke'` returns only the TRUNCATE revoke lines and comments; the 11 `grant execute on function public.*` statements in the migration set all say `to authenticated`, the other 3 `to service_role`. Live ACLs on the current local database (built by the documented procedure):

  public.accept_organization_invitation(uuid)      | postgres=X authenticated=X anon=X service_role=X
  public.accept_sharing_grant_invitation(uuid,uuid)| postgres=X authenticated=X anon=X service_role=X
  public.create_organization_with_owner(...)       | postgres=X authenticated=X anon=X service_role=X
  public.list_org_members(uuid)                    | postgres=X authenticated=X anon=X service_role=X
  public.record_declaration_filed(uuid,text)       | postgres=X authenticated=X anon=X service_role=X
  public.sharing_counterparty_org_names()          | postgres=X authenticated=X service_role=X anon=X
  public.record_calculation_result(...)            | postgres=X service_role=X        <- the one that was re-asserted

Confirmed as a live capability, not just a catalog entry: `begin; set local role anon; select has_function_privilege('anon','public.create_organization_with_owner(text,text,text[])','EXECUTE');` -> true; same true for list_org_members, accept_organization_invitation, record_declaration_filed; false for record_calculation_result. Bounds, measured honestly: `select p.proname, position('auth.uid() is null' in p.prosrc) > 0 from pg_proc ... where prosecdef` shows explicit null-caller guards in accept_organization_invitation, accept_sharing_grant_invitation, create_organization_with_owner and record_declaration_filed; list_org_members raises 'Not a member of this organization.' via app.user_org_ids(), and `select * from public.sharing_counterparty_org_names()` as anon returned 0 rows.
exploit: No end-to-end exploit today -- every one of the six is defended a second time inside its own body. The reachable consequence is posture: a rebuilt local/CI database, and any recovery target rebuilt per DEPLOYMENT.md step 4, exposes six SECURITY DEFINER entry points to the unauthenticated anon key that the migrations deliberately closed, so the API surface CI tests against is wider than the one the schema declares. The next SECURITY DEFINER RPC added without its own `auth.uid() is null` guard -- correctly relying on the migration's `revoke all ... from public; grant execute ... to authenticated;` -- is reachable unauthenticated the moment the seed runs.
impact: Defense in depth on the tenancy-root RPCs (organization creation, invitation acceptance, declaration filing, member listing) is one guard deep instead of two in every freshly built environment. It also means the P14.3 fix closed 1 of 7 function revokes while the audit describes the class as closed.
freshEnvironment: Yes -- this IS the fresh-environment state. The current local database is one built by the documented procedure with the seed applied last, and the anon grants can only have come from seed.sql:23 since no migration grants to anon. I re-derived the same widening from scratch in the throwaway database, where `future_trusted_write` (revoked from public/anon/authenticated, granted to service_role alone) came out of seed.sql as `... anon=X/postgres authenticated=X/postgres`.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's raw catalog observation is true but its three load-bearing claims — seed.sql causation, "six of seven revokes not re-asserted", and fresh-environment divergence — are each false. I re-ran everything.

1) CATALOG (confirmed, and the finding undercounts). My own dump of pg_proc over schemas public+app shows SEVEN public SECURITY DEFINER functions carrying anon=X, not six: the finding missed public.record_shared_data_consumption(uuid,uuid,uuid,integer,uuid,text) | postgres=X | authenticated=X | anon=X | service_role=X. Only record_calculation_result is restricted (postgres=X | service_role=X).

2) CAUSAL CLAIM REFUTED — seed.sql is NOT the source. The finding asserts "the anon grants can only have come from seed.sql:23 since no migration grants to anon." That ignores the schema-public default ACL. Live: `select defaclrole::regrole, defaclnamespace::regnamespace, defaclobjtype, array_to_string(defaclacl,' | ') from pg_default_acl` returns for postgres|public|f:
  postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres
That row contains a `postgres=X/postgres` entry. seed.sql:31 says `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role` — postgres is NOT in that list. I reproduced both forms in a throwaway database (created and dropped; verified 0 rows in pg_database and 0 zz_probe% functions afterward):
  - seed.sql's exact form yields defacl `anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres` — NO postgres entry. Does not match live.
  - The Supabase platform bootstrap form `... grant all on functions to postgres, anon, authenticated, service_role` yields `postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres` — EXACT match to live.
Therefore the live default ACL cannot have been produced by seed.sql alone; it is the platform bootstrap.

3) COUNTERFACTUAL — the widening happens with seed.sql never run. In the throwaway db, under the platform-form defacl and with seed.sql never executed, I applied the exact migration pattern:
  create function public.zz_probe2() ...; revoke all on function public.zz_probe2() from public; grant execute on function public.zz_probe2() to authenticated;
  -> proacl = postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres
Control with no defacl at all (fresh schema zz_app): postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres — no anon. This matches the live database exactly: every app.* function (schema app has no defacl and seed.sql never touches it) has NO anon entry, while every public.* function does. Deleting seed.sql would change none of the seven ACLs.

4) COUNT REFUTED — there is one anon-excluding function revoke, not seven. `grep -rniE "(revoke|grant)[^;]*\banon\b" supabase/migrations/*.sql` returns only three lines, all TRUNCATE (20260903170000:48,54,68). The only function revoke naming anon is 20260903190000:353-355, `revoke all on function public.record_calculation_result(...) from public, anon, authenticated`. The other eleven migration revokes say `revoke all on function ... from public` (e.g. 20260828080000:107, 20260828120000:77, 20260828130000:302, 20260829330000:1030, 20260831100000:95, 20260902150000:194) — `PUBLIC` is the pseudo-role, and revoking it never touched `anon` in ANY environment. So the migrations never "restricted these to authenticated"; there is exactly one anon-excluding function revoke and seed.sql:83-101 re-asserts it. P14.3 closed 1 of 1, not 1 of 7.

5) FRESH-ENVIRONMENT / PRODUCTION-PARITY CLAIM REFUTED. Since the source is the platform default ACL, the same anon=X exists on hosted. The repo states this itself: supabase/migrations/20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql:16-21 — "WHERE IT COMES FROM. Not from this project: it is the standard Supabase bootstrap... Every migration in this repository that has since added a table has inherited it through the default privileges" — and :62-64 confirms the bootstrap behaves the same "on the hosted project as well as locally." So CI/local is NOT wider than production; they match, which is the seed's stated purpose (seed.sql:1-18). Caveat, stated honestly: I could not directly measure production's pg_proc.proacl — my attempt to open a read-only pooler connection was blocked by the permission classifier, and I did not work around it. Production parity is inference from (2)+(3) plus the repo's own assertion, not direct measurement.

6) REACHABILITY (the assigned lens) — nothing is reachable. I executed all seven live as anon, each in `begin; set local role anon; ...; rollback;`:
  create_organization_with_owner -> ERROR: create_organization_with_owner requires an authenticated caller.
  accept_organization_invitation -> ERROR: ...requires an authenticated caller.
  accept_sharing_grant_invitation -> ERROR: ...requires an authenticated caller
  record_declaration_filed -> ERROR: ...requires an authenticated caller.
  record_shared_data_consumption -> ERROR: ...requires an authenticated caller. (the one the finding missed — also guarded; its gate (a) at 20260829310000:161-166 tests `m.user_id = auth.uid()`, never true for a null uid)
  list_org_members -> ERROR: Not a member of this organization.
  sharing_counterparty_org_names -> 0 rows.
Every one refuses. No capability, no route, no data returned.

NET: the observation "anon holds EXECUTE on seven public SECURITY DEFINER RPCs" is true, but it is a pre-existing Supabase platform-default posture present identically in local, CI and hosted — not a seed.sql regression, not a fresh-environment divergence, not six unre-asserted revokes, and not reachable by any actor. The finding as written is wrong on cause, count and consequence. The only surviving residual is an INFO-grade documentation/defense-in-depth note: `revoke all on function ... from public` does not exclude `anon` under Supabase's default privileges, so a future SECURITY DEFINER RPC that omits its own `auth.uid() is null` guard would be anon-callable — in production as much as locally, and regardless of seed.sql.

I re-ran every piece of evidence independently and could not refute any of it. If anything the finding understates the scope.

1. The code says what is quoted. `supabase/seed.sql:23` is verbatim `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;`. The re-assertion block (seed.sql:83-101) is a single `do $$ ... $$` that names exactly two objects: `public.calculation_results` (revoke insert/update/delete) and `public.record_calculation_result(uuid,uuid,uuid,text,jsonb,text,text,jsonb,jsonb,text,uuid)` (revoke all from public/anon/authenticated, grant execute to service_role). No other function is re-asserted. seed.sql:26-32 additionally sets `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role`, which widens future functions too.

2. No migration grants anything to anon. `grep -rniE '\banon\b' supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -iE 'grant|revoke'` returns only 20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql lines 3, 19, 48, 54, 68 — all TRUNCATE revokes and comments. Every `grant execute on function public.*` in the migration set targets `authenticated` (and `service_role` for sharing_counterparty_org_names / record_calculation_result). Confirmed by reading all 60 grant/revoke lines.

3. Live ACLs on the local database match the finding — and include one more function it missed. `select p.oid::regprocedure, p.prosecdef, array_to_string(p.proacl::text[],' | ') from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='public'` returned SEVEN SECURITY DEFINER functions carrying `anon=X/postgres`: accept_organization_invitation(uuid), accept_sharing_grant_invitation(uuid,uuid), create_organization_with_owner(text,text,text[]), list_org_members(uuid), record_declaration_filed(uuid,text), sharing_counterparty_org_names(), AND record_shared_data_consumption(uuid,uuid,uuid,integer,uuid,text) — which the finding does not list (its migration revoke is at 20260829310000_p7d3_shared_data_consumption_audit.sql:331-332, `from public` / `to authenticated`). Only record_calculation_result is correctly `postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`. So it is 7 of 8 function revokes not re-asserted, not 6 of 7.

4. Effective privilege confirmed as anon: `begin; set local role anon; select has_function_privilege(...); rollback;` returned `anon|t|t|t|t|f` for create_organization_with_owner, list_org_members, record_declaration_filed, record_shared_data_consumption, and record_calculation_result respectively.

5. Causation is seed.sql:23, proven in isolation. In a throwaway database (`create database refute_seed_probe`, dropped afterward) I created a function, ran the migration pattern `revoke all ... from public; grant execute ... to authenticated;` and got `postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres` with `pg_default_acl` count 0 — no anon. Running seed.sql:23's statement then produced `postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`. The widening comes from that line and nothing else.

6. Reachability over HTTP, which the finding only inferred, is real. supabase/config.toml:13 exposes `schemas = ["public", "graphql_public"]`. With the local anon key and no Authorization header: POST /rest/v1/rpc/sharing_counterparty_org_names -> HTTP 200 `[]` (the function body ran to completion unauthenticated); POST /rest/v1/rpc/list_org_members {"p_org_id":"000...0"} -> HTTP 400 `{"code":"P0001","message":"Not a member of this organization."}` — a P0001 raised from inside the function body, i.e. EXECUTE succeeded and only the in-body guard stopped it, not `42501 permission denied for function`. By contrast POST /rest/v1/rpc/record_calculation_result -> HTTP 404 PGRST202 with no "perhaps you meant" hint, the correctly-closed case.

7. The finding's own honest bounds hold. `select p.proname, position('auth.uid() is null' in p.prosrc) > 0 from pg_proc ... where prosecdef` gives true for accept_organization_invitation, accept_sharing_grant_invitation, create_organization_with_owner, record_declaration_filed and record_shared_data_consumption; false for list_org_members (guarded instead by app.user_org_ids() raising) and sharing_counterparty_org_names (returns 0 rows as anon). So there is no end-to-end exploit today, exactly as claimed — the defect is that defense in depth on the tenancy-root RPCs is one guard deep instead of two in every freshly built environment, and that the seed's coupling comment ("These statements mirror the migrations named above and must be updated with them") is a list that already rotted for 7 of 8 functions on the day it was written.

MEDIUM is the right severity: no reachable exploit, but this is precisely the seed-after-revoke failure class, the fix closed 1 of 8 rather than the class, and the next SECURITY DEFINER RPC added relying on its migration's revoke will be anon-reachable the moment the seed runs.

CONFIRMED — I could not refute it, and my own checks make it slightly stronger than stated.

1. The grant exists as claimed. `supabase/seed.sql:23` = `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` and `supabase/seed.sql:31-32` = `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role;`. The re-assertion block `supabase/seed.sql:83-101` names exactly one function (`record_calculation_result`).

2. No migration is the source. `grep -rniE '\banon\b' supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -iE 'grant|revoke'` returns only 5 lines, all in `20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql` (TRUNCATE revokes + comments). Every `grant execute on function public.*` in the migration set targets `authenticated` and/or `service_role`. So anon EXECUTE can only have come from the seed.

3. Live ACLs on the local DB (built by the documented procedure), `select p.oid::regprocedure, p.prosecdef, p.proacl from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n ... where n.nspname='public' and p.prokind='f'`:
   accept_organization_invitation(uuid) | t | postgres=X | authenticated=X | anon=X | service_role=X
   accept_sharing_grant_invitation(uuid,uuid) | t | ... anon=X ...
   create_organization_with_owner(text,text,text[]) | t | ... anon=X ...
   list_org_members(uuid) | t | ... anon=X ...
   record_declaration_filed(uuid,text) | t | ... anon=X ...
   record_shared_data_consumption(uuid,uuid,uuid,integer,uuid,text) | t | ... anon=X ...
   sharing_counterparty_org_names() | t | ... anon=X ...
   record_calculation_result(...) | t | postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres   <- the only one re-asserted
   The finding UNDERCOUNTS: it is 7 of 8 public SECURITY DEFINER functions, not 6 of 7. It omits `record_shared_data_consumption`.

4. Live capability, not just catalog: `begin; set local role anon; select has_function_privilege('anon', ...,'EXECUTE'); rollback;` -> create_org t, list_members t, accept_inv t, record_decl t, rec_calc f. Exactly as claimed.

5. Bounds as claimed — no exploit today. As anon: `select public.create_organization_with_owner('X','importer',array['steel'])` -> `ERROR: create_organization_with_owner requires an authenticated caller.`; `select * from public.list_org_members('1b635dfb-...')` -> `ERROR: Not a member of this organization.`; `select * from public.sharing_counterparty_org_names()` -> 0 rows. Null-caller guards confirmed via `position('auth.uid() is null' in prosrc)`: present in accept_organization_invitation, accept_sharing_grant_invitation, create_organization_with_owner, record_declaration_filed, record_shared_data_consumption; absent in list_org_members and sharing_counterparty_org_names (both fail closed via app.user_org_ids()).

MITIGATION LENS — I searched and found none.
- No test asserts it. `grep -rniE 'has_function_privilege|proacl' tests/**/*.ts` returns nothing relevant; the only privilege assertion is `tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts:886` covering `calculation_results` / `record_calculation_result` alone.
- The ops check does NOT catch it. `docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:571-578` step 6 runs `scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check "<dsn>"`. `main()` at `scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:507-531` runs `CHECKS` only when NOT `--check`; `--check` runs `SELF_CHECKS` only. The `function_grants` check (`:169-182`) that would show this lives in `CHECKS`, i.e. compare-mode only — and in compare mode both sides are seeded, so it would MATCH. None of the four SELF_CHECKS (`api_roles_hold_their_grants`, `truncate_granted_to_api_roles`, `security_definer_without_search_path`, RLS checks) looks at function EXECUTE grants to anon.

STRONGER THAN CLAIMED — I confirmed the forward-looking half by direct experiment, which the finding only asserted. `pg_default_acl` on the local DB holds a `postgres`-owned function default ACL `postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres` (from seed.sql:31-32). Consequence, run in a real transaction and rolled back:
  begin;
  create function public.zz_probe_fn() returns int language sql security definer as $$ select 1 $$;
  revoke all on function public.zz_probe_fn() from public;
  grant execute on function public.zz_probe_fn() to authenticated;
  -> proacl: postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres
  -> has_function_privilege('anon','public.zz_probe_fn()','EXECUTE') = t
  rollback;  (verified gone: count = 0)
That is the exact idiom every migration in this repo uses. So the widening is not merely a one-time artifact of the seed's blanket grant running last — the persisted default ACL re-applies it to every function a FUTURE `supabase migration up` creates, silently, even when that migration correctly revokes from public and grants only to authenticated. This is the same failure class as the P14.1/§19 incident.

Scope: seed.sql is local/CI-only per its own header, so production is not implicated by this path (I did not query production; not necessary, and the finding does not claim production). Severity MEDIUM is right: no reachable exploit today, but defense-in-depth on the tenancy-root RPCs is one guard deep instead of two in every freshly built environment, nothing tests or detects it, and the next SECURITY DEFINER RPC added without its own null-caller guard is anon-reachable on creation.

title: The audit's measured default-ACL claim is wrong: `anon` holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on every future public table, not read-only
exploit: Structural. A future migration that creates a table in public and forgets `alter table ... enable row level security` gives every holder of the public anon key full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on it, with no policy in the way. The audit line is what a reviewer would read to conclude anon is read-only by default and that the omission is bounded.
impact: Anyone relying on the P14 audit as the release's evidence of the grant model. The one automated guard against this shape -- `tables_without_rls` in compare-database-posture.mjs -- is in the script that nothing runs (see the OPERATIONS finding). Today no such table exists: every table in public has relrowsecurity = true.
freshEnvironment: Yes. The default ACL is written by supabase/seed.sql:25-26 (`alter default privileges in schema public grant all on tables to anon, authenticated, service_role`), minus TRUNCATE at seed.sql:106-110, so any rebuild reproduces `anon=arwdxtm` exactly. The CREATE TABLE probe was rolled back and `to_regclass('public.zz_probe_table') is null` confirmed true.

verdicts.reasoning:
Independently re-verified; could not refute.

(1) The claim exists as stated. docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1437: "| `postgres` default ACL, schema public | `anon=rxtm`, `authenticated=arwdxtm` - no `D` |", inside section D ("TRUNCATE re-verification"), which ends "Status - VERIFIED."

(2) Measured live, full pg_default_acl dump (broader than the finding's filtered query):
select pg_get_userbyid(d.defaclrole), d.defaclobjtype, array_to_string(d.defaclacl,' ') from pg_default_acl d join pg_namespace n on n.oid=d.defaclnamespace where n.nspname='public';
-> postgres|r|postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres anon=arwdxtm/postgres authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres
-> supabase_admin|r|... anon=arwdDxtm/supabase_admin ...
anon on the postgres row is arwdxtm (a=INSERT, w=UPDATE, d=DELETE), NOT rxtm. The "no D" half of the audit line is correct; the anon half is false.

(3) Behavioural, real BEGIN/ROLLBACK: create table public.zz_refute_probe(id int primary key, secret text) -> ACL "anon=arwdxtm/postgres", RLS: false, and information_schema.role_table_grants shows anon=SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER. After rollback, to_regclass('public.zz_refute_probe') is null -> table exists: false. No state left behind.

(4) anon=rxtm is unreachable in any state this repo can build. grep -rn "default privileges" supabase/migrations/ returns only 20260903170000 (lines 53 and 67), revoking TRUNCATE alone and identically from both roles. supabase/seed.sql:25-26 grants "all on tables to anon, authenticated, service_role" in a single statement; seed.sql:106-110 revokes only TRUNCATE. Nothing distinguishes anon from authenticated, so their default ACLs are necessarily identical - the audit's own adjacent authenticated=arwdxtm is the correct value for both. The hosted bootstrap would give arwdDxtm. So the fresh-environment claim holds: any rebuild reproduces anon=arwdxtm.

(5) Line 1437 is the audit's only statement of the default grant model. grep -n "arwdxtm|arwdDxtm|default ACL|default privileg" over the doc returns 558, 1437, 1443, 1447, 2131; none of the others state the ACL and none correct it.

REACHABILITY LENS. The security consequence is NOT reachable by any actor today, and the finding correctly says so: count(*) filter (where not relrowsecurity) = 0 of 21 base tables in public. The harm requires a future migration that omits "enable row level security". I also confirmed the guard claim: grep -rn "relrowsecurity|rowsecurity" tests/ -> zero hits (no test asserts RLS coverage), and compare-database-posture.mjs is referenced only from docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md, DEPLOYMENT.md and the audit itself - never from package.json or a CI workflow.

Not refuted because the finding is AUDIT_HONESTY: its subject is the accuracy of a recorded measurement, not an exploit, and the recorded value is positively false rather than imprecise. It appears in a VERIFIED-marked table, on the exact axis (anon write privileges by default) that decides whether a future missing-RLS table is public data loss or a read-only leak, for the role holding the publishable anon key. Severity stays MEDIUM: no current exploitability found, but it is a fabricated measurement in the document offered as the release's grant-model evidence.

Re-ran every piece of evidence myself; all of it holds.

(a) Cited text verified verbatim. `grep -n "rxtm" docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md` -> line 1437: `| `postgres` default ACL, schema public | `anon=rxtm`, `authenticated=arwdxtm` - no `D` |`.

(b) Measured ACL contradicts it. My query (broader than the finding's, covering all owners/objtypes): `select pg_get_userbyid(d.defaclrole), d.defaclobjtype, array_to_string(d.defaclacl,' | ') from pg_default_acl d join pg_namespace n on n.oid=d.defaclnamespace where n.nspname='public';` -> the postgres/'r' row is `postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres | anon=arwdxtm/postgres | authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres | service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres`. anon is arwdxtm (a=INSERT, w=UPDATE, d=DELETE), not rxtm. The `authenticated=arwdxtm` and "no D" halves of the audit row are correct; the anon half is not.

(c) Behaviourally confirmed with my own probe (distinct table name, real BEGIN/ROLLBACK): `begin; create table public.zz_probe_table_refute(id int); select ... from information_schema.role_table_grants where grantee='anon'; select relrowsecurity ...; rollback;` -> anon=DELETE, anon=INSERT, anon=REFERENCES, anon=SELECT, anon=TRIGGER, anon=UPDATE; relrowsecurity=f; and post-rollback `to_regclass('public.zz_probe_table_refute') is null` = t (table gone, nothing committed).

(d) Fresh-environment claim verified from source, not inferred. supabase/seed.sql:25-26 = `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on tables to anon, authenticated, service_role;`; the only narrowing is TRUNCATE at seed.sql:106-110. `grep -rn "default privileges" supabase/ scripts/` returns exactly seven hits: seed.sql:25,28,31 (grants), seed.sql:106,109 (TRUNCATE revokes), and 20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql:53,67 (TRUNCATE revokes). Nothing revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from anon's default ACL anywhere. Since seed.sql runs last in `supabase db reset`, any rebuild reproduces anon=arwdxtm exactly. So `anon=rxtm` was never true of an environment built by the documented procedure -- it is a misreported measurement, not a stale one.

(e) Compensating-control claim verified: `grep -rn "tables_without_rls" scripts/ .github/ package.json` -> single hit, scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:314. Not wired into CI.

(f) Impact bound verified accurate: `select count(*) filter (where relrowsecurity), count(*) from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace where n.nspname='public' and c.relkind='r';` -> `21|21`. No table is exposed today, so this is a misstatement in release evidence rather than a live exposure.

Nothing in the finding is overstated. Severity MEDIUM stands: the row inverts the reader's conclusion about anon on future public tables (read-only vs full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) inside the document that serves as the release's evidence of the grant model, and the only automated guard for the shape it would mask is unrun.

I could not refute this; I reproduced it independently and looked hard for a mitigation the finder missed.

1. The audit line is exactly as quoted. docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1437 reads:
`| `postgres` default ACL, schema public | `anon=rxtm`, `authenticated=arwdxtm` — no `D` |`

2. Measured on the live local DB (my own query, not the finder's):
psql -tAc "select pg_get_userbyid(d.defaclrole), d.defaclobjtype, array_to_string(d.defaclacl,' ') from pg_default_acl d join pg_namespace n on n.oid=d.defaclnamespace where n.nspname='public';"
->
supabase_admin|r|postgres=arwdDxtm/supabase_admin anon=arwdDxtm/supabase_admin authenticated=arwdDxtm/supabase_admin service_role=arwdDxtm/supabase_admin
postgres|r|postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres anon=arwdxtm/postgres authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres

anon under the postgres default ACL is `arwdxtm`, not `rxtm`. No row anywhere in pg_default_acl carries `rxtm`, so the audit's value is not merely stale — it is not reproducible from any role's ACL in this database. The `no D` half is correct.

3. Behavioural confirmation, inside a real BEGIN/ROLLBACK (not a client header):
begin; create table public.zz_probe_refute(id int primary key, s text); ...; rollback;
-> acl: postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres anon=arwdxtm/postgres authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres
-> rls: false
-> anon_insert: true / anon_update: true / anon_delete: true / anon_select: true / anon_truncate: false
-> after_rollback_gone: true  (to_regclass is null after ROLLBACK; nothing committed)

4. Fresh-environment claim verified against source, not just state. supabase/seed.sql:25-26 `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on tables to anon, authenticated, service_role;` runs as the LAST step of `supabase db reset`; the only default-privilege revokes anywhere are TRUNCATE-only — supabase/seed.sql:106-110 and supabase/migrations/20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql:53 and :67 (`revoke truncate on tables from anon, authenticated`). grep for "default privileges" across supabase/ and scripts/ returns only those five sites. Nothing revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from the default ACL, so any rebuild reproduces anon=arwdxtm exactly.

ALREADY-MITIGATED lens — I searched for a guard and found none that runs:
- grep -rln "relrowsecurity|rowsecurity|tables_without_rls" over tests/ and scripts/ matches exactly one file: scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs (the check is at :314).
- No vitest test asserts that every public table has RLS enabled; tests/integration/organizations-isolation.test.ts is the only test file mentioning RLS and it tests specific policies, not table enumeration.
- package.json scripts are dev/build/postbuild/start/test/test:watch/test:e2e/typecheck/regulatory:verify — compare-database-posture.mjs is wired into no script and is referenced only in docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md and DEPLOYMENT.md as a manual step.
