title: emission_data's activation and verification gates are BEFORE UPDATE only -- a plain MEMBER can INSERT a fully forged ACTIVE + VERIFIED record, and every grantee org reads it as operator-attested verified data
evidence:
Both gates are UPDATE-only. supabase/migrations/20260829230000_p7b_emission_data_schema.sql:373-376 -- `create trigger emission_data_verification_gate_trg before update on public.emission_data`. supabase/migrations/20260829480000_p13_review_emission_data_verification_and_evidence_integrity_fix.sql:305-308 -- `create trigger emission_data_activation_gate_trg before update on public.emission_data`. Confirmed live: `select pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid) ...` returns `BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data` for both. The INSERT policy (supabase/migrations/20260829230000_p7b_emission_data_schema.sql:399-409) checks only org membership and installation ownership -- nothing about status, verification_status, verifier_user_id or evidence_file_ids: `with check (entered_by_org_id in (select app.user_org_ids()) and exists (select 1 from public.installations i where i.id = emission_data.installation_id and i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id))`. The evidence-integrity anti-join exists ONLY on emission_data_update_own_org, never on insert. Live probe, inside `begin; ... rollback;`, attacker = a MEMBER (app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of returned f):

  insert into emission_data (installation_id, entered_by_org_id, cn_scope, reporting_period_kind, reporting_period_year, direct_specific, indirect_specific, emission_unit, methodology, status, verification_status, verifier_user_id, evidence_file_ids)
  values ('a2000000-...-00000000000a','a0000000-...-00000000000a','{7206}','ANNUAL',2026,'0.000001','0','tCO2e/t','EU_METHOD','ACTIVE','VERIFIED','bbbbbbbb-...-000000000002','{"deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-00000000dead"}');

  -> INSERT 0 1, returning status=ACTIVE, verification_status=VERIFIED, verifier_user_id=bbbbbbbb-... (a user of a DIFFERENT organization), evidence_file_ids={deadbeef-...} (no evidence_files row exists).

Switching to the grantee importer's claims in the same transaction:
  select id, entered_by_org_id, direct_specific, verification_status, status from emission_data;
  -> 1 row: the forged record, direct_specific 0.000001, VERIFIED, ACTIVE.

And the determination validator accepts it:
  select app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record(<ACTUAL snapshot naming that row>, '<importer org>','72061000','CN',null);
  -> t

The repo's own test for this invariant is UPDATE-only: tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts:441 "Finding 1b: a plain MEMBER cannot set status='ACTIVE' directly on a DRAFT+UNVERIFIED+no-evidence row, bypassing the verify workflow" -- its body is `.update({status: "ACTIVE"})`. Every one of the ~12 cases in that suite drives UPDATE; none drives INSERT.
exploit: 1. Attacker is an ordinary MEMBER (no ADMIN/OWNER) of a producer org that has at least one installation. 2. One raw PostgREST call: POST /rest/v1/emission_data with body {installation_id: <own installation>, entered_by_org_id: <own org>, cn_scope:[...], reporting_period_*, direct_specific:"0.000001", indirect_specific:"0", emission_unit, methodology, status:"ACTIVE", verification_status:"VERIFIED", verifier_user_id:<any uuid, including a user in the counterparty's org>, evidence_file_ids:["<any uuid>"]}. The row is admitted -- the three walls that would have stopped the equivalent UPDATE (ADMIN+-only verify, DRAFT->ACTIVE-requires-VERIFIED-plus-evidence, evidence-must-name-real-files) are all on the UPDATE side. 3. Every org holding an ACTIVE sharing grant on that installation now reads the row, because emission_data_select_own_org admits shared rows on exactly `status='ACTIVE' and verification_status='VERIFIED'`. 4. The importer freezes it as an ACTUAL determination; app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record accepts (verified: t), so it persists onto a shipment_line and flows into record_calculation_result and a FILED_RECORDED declaration snapshot.
impact: The cross-org trust boundary this product is built on -- 'ACTIVE + VERIFIED means an ADMIN of the operating installation verified it against real evidence' -- can be manufactured from nothing by the lowest-privileged member of the producer org. The importer on the other side of the sharing grant, a different tenant, cannot tell the forgery from a real record: it carries a verifier_user_id (which can name one of the importer's own users, so the audit trail implicates the victim), a non-empty evidence list, OPERATOR_PROVIDED provenance, and it survives the P14 D2 provenance wall and the full determination validator. It reaches a filed CBAM declaration as understated embedded emissions. Bounds, honestly: the forger must be a member of an org that owns the installation (not a stranger), the numbers are their own org's to state, and the exploit needs raw PostgREST rather than the UI -- but that is precisely the threat model 20260903120000's own header names ('a member posting raw PostgREST could freeze ... and every surface reading the snapshot would repeat the claim'), and the harmed party is a different tenant.
freshEnvironment: Yes. Both trigger definitions and the INSERT policy are migration DDL (20260829230000, 20260829480000), applied identically by `supabase db reset`, by a hosted `db push`, and by any restore of a schema dump. supabase/seed.sql touches only grants and cannot change a trigger's event list or a policy's WITH CHECK. I verified against the migration source files as well as the live catalog, so the finding does not depend on this database's history.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by my own independent reproduction. I did not reuse the finding's environment or evidence.

Setup note: the main local `postgres` database currently has an EMPTY public schema (`select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> 0 rows; `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` does not exist), so I built my own throwaway database `advrev_insgate` (created from another agent's fully-migrated `advrev_expiry`, verified to carry the P14 v2 gate: `position('P14 v2' in pg_get_functiondef(...)) > 0` -> t), seeded my own fixtures, and dropped it afterwards. Every mutation was inside a real `begin; ... rollback;`.

1. STRUCTURE (source + live catalog agree). All four triggers on emission_data are BEFORE UPDATE, none BEFORE INSERT:
   pg_get_triggerdef -> emission_data_prevent_fact_change_trg / emission_data_verification_gate_trg / emission_data_touch_updated_at_trg / emission_data_activation_gate_trg, all "BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data".
   I also read the two newest P14 migrations that rewrite the gate — supabase/migrations/20260903140000_p14_emission_data_verification_downgrade_gate.sql and supabase/migrations/20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql — both are `create or replace function app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate()`, i.e. they harden the UPDATE body only and add no INSERT trigger.
   Live policy dump: emission_data_insert_own_org WITH CHECK is exactly `entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids()) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE i.id = emission_data.installation_id AND i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)` — no status, verification_status, verifier_user_id or evidence clause. The evidence anti-join exists only on emission_data_update_own_org's WITH CHECK. Check constraints (all 9, dumped live) contain nothing gating status/verification_status at insert time; emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck only requires verifier_user_id to be non-null, which the attacker supplies.

2. REACHABILITY (the lens I was asked to apply) — the path is real end to end:
   - Privilege: `information_schema.role_table_grants` for emission_data shows `authenticated | INSERT` (intended — members record emission data; not a seed artifact).
   - Transport: supabase/config.toml `[api] enabled = true`, `schemas = ["public", "graphql_public"]`, and src/infrastructure/supabase/browser-client.ts:28-31 uses NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, so a logged-in member holds a valid JWT plus a public anon key and can POST /rest/v1/emission_data directly. The repo's own migration header (20260903120000, quoted inside app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record) names exactly this actor: "a member posting raw PostgREST could freeze ...".
   - Capability: plain MEMBER, no ADMIN/OWNER needed — verified in-session: `select app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of('a0000000-...-00000000000a')` -> f.

3. LIVE EXPLOIT (fixtures: producer org a0000000-…, MEMBER 11111111-…-0001, OWNER 11111111-…-0002, importer org b0000000-… with user 22222222-…-0001, installation d0000000-… provenance OPERATOR_PROVIDED, ACTIVE sharing_grant producer->importer).
   As the MEMBER, inside begin/rollback:
     insert into public.emission_data (installation_id, entered_by_org_id, cn_scope, reporting_period_kind, reporting_period_year, direct_specific, indirect_specific, emission_unit, methodology, status, verification_status, verifier_user_id, evidence_file_ids) values ('d0000000-…','a0000000-…','{7206}','ANNUAL',2026,'0.000001','0','tCO2e/t','EU_METHOD','ACTIVE','VERIFIED','22222222-0000-4000-8000-000000000001','{"deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-00000000dead"}') returning …;
   -> INSERT 0 1, returning status=ACTIVE | verification_status=VERIFIED | verifier_user_id=22222222-… (a user of the OTHER tenant) | evidence_file_ids={deadbeef-…} (no evidence_files row exists) | direct_specific=0.000001.

4. CROSS-TENANT READ, same transaction, after switching request.jwt.claims to the grantee importer's user:
     select id, entered_by_org_id, direct_specific, verification_status, status, verifier_user_id from public.emission_data;
   -> 1 row: the forged record, VERIFIED, ACTIVE, 0.000001. (Live SELECT policy: `... OR (installation_id IN (SELECT app.user_shared_installation_ids()) AND status='ACTIVE' AND verification_status='VERIFIED')`.)

5. DOWNSTREAM VALIDATOR ACCEPTS IT. As the importer's user, same transaction:
     select app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record('{"method":"ACTUAL","snapshot":{…emission_data_id, installation_id, methodology EU_METHOD, record_provenance OPERATOR_PROVIDED, emission_data_version 1, resolved_at, sharing_grant_id, evidence_file_ids ["deadbeef-…"], emission_unit, values, verification{status VERIFIED, verifier_user_id}}}'::jsonb,'b0000000-…','72061000','CN',null);
   -> t
   Reading the function body: it requires evidence_file_ids to be non-empty and byte-equal to the live array, but never checks that those ids name real evidence_files rows — so the forged evidence list passes, and the P14 D2 provenance wall passes too because the installation genuinely is OPERATOR_PROVIDED.

6. TEST-COVERAGE CLAIM VERIFIED. tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts: every `.insert(` (lines 157, 194, 222, 271, 300, 322) is a fixture written through `serviceClient` (see insertDraftEmissionData at line 148, which hardcodes status "DRAFT"/verification_status "UNVERIFIED"); every member-driven adversarial probe, including line 441's "Finding 1b … cannot set status='ACTIVE' directly", is `.update(`. No test drives a member INSERT.

Refutation attempts that failed: no BEFORE INSERT trigger anywhere in supabase/migrations (grep of every `create trigger … emission_data`); no INSERT-side revoke on emission_data (20260903170000 revokes TRUNCATE only; 20260903190000's trusted-write-only revokes target calculation_results); no check constraint pins insert-time status; PostgREST exposure and the authenticated INSERT grant are both intended and present. Severity stands at BLOCKER: it manufactures, from the lowest privilege level, exactly the cross-tenant attestation ("ACTIVE+VERIFIED means an ADMIN verified against real evidence") that three separate migrations (20260829480000, 20260903140000, 20260903150000) were written to protect on the UPDATE side, and it survives into a filed determination.

I tried to refute this on the CORRECTNESS lens and could not. Every cited artifact says what the finding quotes, and I re-reproduced the exploit end-to-end in a database I built myself.

1. TRIGGER EVENT LISTS — confirmed in source. `supabase/migrations/20260829230000_p7b_emission_data_schema.sql:373-376` reads `create trigger emission_data_verification_gate_trg / before update on public.emission_data`. `supabase/migrations/20260829480000_p13_review_emission_data_verification_and_evidence_integrity_fix.sql:305-308` reads `create trigger emission_data_activation_gate_trg / before update on public.emission_data`. Verbatim as quoted.

2. I HUNTED FOR A LATER FIX AND FOUND NONE. Two migrations postdate the ones cited: `20260903140000_p14_emission_data_verification_downgrade_gate.sql` and `20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql`. Both are `create or replace function app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate()` ONLY — neither issues a `create trigger`, so the trigger stays BEFORE UPDATE. `grep -n "create trigger|before insert|for insert" supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep emission_data` returns exactly four triggers, all `before update` (activation_gate, prevent_fact_change, touch_updated_at, verification_gate), and one `for insert` policy. There is no INSERT-side trigger anywhere in the migration set.

3. INSERT POLICY — confirmed, both in source (`20260829230000...:399-409`) and live: `select polname, polcmd, pg_get_expr(polwithcheck,polrelid) from pg_policy where polrelid='public.emission_data'::regclass` returns for `emission_data_insert_own_org|a`: `((entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE ((i.id = emission_data.installation_id) AND (i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)))))` — nothing about status, verification_status, verifier_user_id or evidence_file_ids. The evidence anti-join (`NOT EXISTS ... unnest(evidence_file_ids) ... evidence_files ef`) appears ONLY on `emission_data_update_own_org|w`, as claimed.

4. NO TABLE CONSTRAINT SAVES IT. `pg_get_constraintdef` for all 14 constraints on emission_data: the only verification-related one is `emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck CHECK ((verification_status <> 'VERIFIED') OR (verifier_user_id IS NOT NULL))` — which the forgery satisfies by supplying a uuid, and `verifier_user_id` is only FK-constrained to `auth.users(id)`, so any real user (including the victim org's) is accepted.

5. LIVE REPRODUCTION — I re-ran it myself. The shared `postgres` DB was empty when I started (another agent's reset in flight), so I built an INDEPENDENT throwaway (`create database advrev_edins`), seeded a producer org, a MEMBER, an installation and an ACTIVE sharing grant to an importer org, and ran inside a real `begin; ... rollback;`:
  - `select app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of('a0000000-...-0000000000a')` -> `f`, `current_user` -> `authenticated`. Attacker is a plain MEMBER.
  - The forged `insert into emission_data (... status, verification_status, verifier_user_id, evidence_file_ids) values (...,'ACTIVE','VERIFIED','22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222','{"deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-00000000dead"}')` returned `INSERT 0 1` with `status=ACTIVE | verification_status=VERIFIED | verifier_user_id=22222222-... | evidence_file_ids={deadbeef-...} | direct_specific=0.000001`. The verifier named is a user of the IMPORTER org, not the producer's.
  - `select count(*) from evidence_files where id='deadbeef-...'` -> `0`. The evidence id names nothing.
  - Switching to the grantee importer's claims in the same transaction, `select id, entered_by_org_id, direct_specific, verification_status, status from emission_data` returned the forged row. Cross-tenant read confirmed.
  - Rollback verified: `emission_rows_before=0`, `emission_rows_after=0`. Nothing committed. Throwaway DB dropped afterward (`DROP DATABASE`).

6. VALIDATOR — corroborated. `pg_get_functiondef` for `app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record` gates on exactly the fields the forgery sets: line 66 `if v_ed.status <> 'ACTIVE' or v_ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED' then`, line 70 `if coalesce(array_length(v_ed.evidence_file_ids,1),0) = 0 then`, line 97 snapshot `verification.status = 'VERIFIED'`, line 176 snapshot-evidence vs live-evidence equality. It never checks that evidence_file_ids name real `evidence_files` rows, so a fabricated-but-non-empty array passes every one of them.

7. TEST GAP — confirmed and worse than stated. `tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts:441` is the quoted "Finding 1b" title and its body is `.update({ status: "ACTIVE" })`. The file has 26 `.update(` calls and 6 `.insert(` calls; I checked the client on all six — the only `emission_data` insert is at line 157 via `serviceClient` (a fixture helper), and the rest are evidence_files/organizations/memberships/operators/installations. Not one test drives an `emission_data` INSERT as a member client, so the INSERT path has zero coverage.

8. FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CLAIM — holds, and I strengthened it. This is migration DDL, not a grant, so `supabase/seed.sql`'s blanket `grant all` is irrelevant to it (a grant cannot change a trigger's event list or a policy's WITH CHECK). More directly: I proved it in a database with no shared history with the one the implementer probed.

Severity: I hold BLOCKER. It defeats, on the INSERT side, the exact three controls that migrations 20260829230000, 20260829480000, 20260903140000 and 20260903150000 were each written to enforce on the UPDATE side; the forged attestation is indistinguishable from a genuine one to the counterparty; and the harmed party is a different tenant. The honest bound the finding itself states — the forger must be a member of the org owning the installation — is real but does not reduce it below BLOCKER, since the whole point of ACTIVE+VERIFIED is that an ADMIN attested it against evidence, and a MEMBER can now manufacture that from nothing.

I tried to refute this via the already-mitigated lens and failed.

Note first that the local `postgres` database is currently EMPTY (`select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='public'` -> 0; no `app` schema), so I did NOT trust the finder's live evidence. I built my own database from scratch: `create database advrev_ins_refute`, bootstrapped auth/storage/extensions, applied all 74 files in supabase/migrations/ in order, then applied supabase/seed.sql. That is a stronger fresh-environment test than the finder ran. I dropped the database afterward.

MITIGATIONS I SEARCHED FOR AND DID NOT FIND:

(1) Later migrations. The finder cited only 20260829230000 and 20260829480000, but two later ones exist that they did not mention: supabase/migrations/20260903140000_p14_emission_data_verification_downgrade_gate.sql and 20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql. Both are `create or replace function app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate()` ONLY -- neither issues a `create trigger`, so neither changes the event list. Confirmed on my fresh DB: the v2 body is present (`position('cannot be removed from an ACTIVE' in pg_get_functiondef(...))` -> t) and all four triggers are still UPDATE-only:
  emission_data_prevent_fact_change_trg | BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data
  emission_data_verification_gate_trg   | BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data
  emission_data_touch_updated_at_trg    | BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data
  emission_data_activation_gate_trg     | BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data
`grep -rn "emission_data" supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -i "create trigger"` returns exactly those four. There is no BEFORE INSERT trigger anywhere in the repo.

(2) A CHECK constraint. All 14 constraints on emission_data are row-local; none couples status/verification_status to caller role or to evidence existence. `emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck` only requires verifier_user_id NOT NULL when VERIFIED -- the forgery supplies one. `emission_data_verifier_user_id_fkey` only requires the uuid exist in auth.users -- a user of the VICTIM org satisfies it.

(3) The INSERT policy. Live on my fresh DB, `emission_data_insert_own_org` (polcmd 'a') WITH CHECK is exactly `((entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE i.id = emission_data.installation_id AND i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)))` -- no status, no verification_status, no verifier, no evidence anti-join. The evidence anti-join exists only on `emission_data_update_own_org`.

(4) Column-level or seed-level revoke. `select privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_name='emission_data' and grantee='authenticated'` after seed.sql -> INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER. supabase/seed.sql revokes only on calculation_results and record_calculation_result. public is exposed to PostgREST (supabase/config.toml:13 `schemas = ["public", "graphql_public"]`).

(5) An existing test. tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts has 26 `.update(` calls and 6 `.insert(` calls; every insert goes through `serviceClient` (RLS-bypassing seed helper `insertDraftEmissionData`, lines 148-184) and hardcodes status DRAFT / verification_status UNVERIFIED. No test drives a member-role INSERT. The finder's coverage claim is accurate.

MY OWN REPRODUCTION (real `begin; ... rollback;`; rows before = 0, rows after = 0, both verified in the same script).

Control -- same MEMBER, the UPDATE route, correctly BLOCKED:
  begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims='{"sub":"11111111-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","role":"authenticated"}';
  insert ... (DRAFT/UNVERIFIED);
  update emission_data set status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id='22222222-...', evidence_file_ids=array['deadbeef-...'] where id='c0000000-...c1';
  -> ERROR:  emission_data: only an ADMIN or OWNER of the owning organization may verify or reject a record
     CONTEXT:  PL/pgSQL function app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate() line 7 at RAISE

Exploit -- SAME member (`app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of('a0000000-...')` -> f), identical end state, ONE INSERT, ADMITTED:
  insert into public.emission_data (installation_id, entered_by_org_id, cn_scope, reporting_period_kind, reporting_period_year, direct_specific, indirect_specific, emission_unit, methodology, status, verification_status, verifier_user_id, evidence_file_ids) values ('a2000000-...','a0000000-...',array['7206'],'ANNUAL',2026,'0.000001','0','tCO2e/t','EU_METHOD','ACTIVE','VERIFIED','22222222-0000-4000-8000-000000000001',array['deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-00000000dead']);
  -> INSERT 0 1; returning status=ACTIVE, verification_status=VERIFIED, verifier_user_id=22222222-... (a user of the IMPORTER org), direct_specific=0.000001, evidence_file_ids={deadbeef-...}
  -> select count(*) from evidence_files where id='deadbeef-...' -> 0 (no backing file exists)

Cross-tenant read, same transaction, switching claims to the grantee importer (22222222-...):
  select id, entered_by_org_id, direct_specific, status, verification_status from emission_data;
  -> 1 row: the forged record, 0.000001, ACTIVE, VERIFIED. (emission_data_select_own_org admits shared rows on exactly `status='ACTIVE' and verification_status='VERIFIED'`.)

Downstream, as the importer:
  select app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record(<honest ACTUAL snapshot of the forged row, record_provenance='OPERATOR_PROVIDED', sharing_grant_id=a3000000-...>, 'b0000000-...' /* importer org */, '72061000','IN', null);
  -> t
The validator tests `coalesce(array_length(v_ed.evidence_file_ids,1),0) = 0` and compares the snapshot array byte-for-byte against the live array, but never checks that any evidence_file_ids entry names a real evidence_files row -- so the phantom id passes, and so does the P14 D2 provenance wall.

CONCLUSION. Every gate that stops the UPDATE (ADMIN+-only verify; DRAFT->ACTIVE-requires-VERIFIED-plus-evidence via app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate, whose body is `new.status is distinct from old.status` and is structurally UPDATE-shaped; and the evidence anti-join on the UPDATE policy) is absent on the INSERT. This is migration DDL, identical after `supabase db reset`, a hosted `db push`, or a schema-dump restore, and seed.sql cannot change a trigger's event list or a policy's WITH CHECK -- so it is not an artifact of this database's history. BLOCKER stands: an ordinary MEMBER manufactures the cross-tenant "ACTIVE + VERIFIED means an ADMIN verified it against real evidence" claim from nothing, with fabricated verifier attribution that can name one of the victim tenant's own users.

title: Global emission_data_predecessor_id_uq lets any org that knows a victim's emission_data id permanently block that producer from ever recording a corrected version
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260829290000_p7_review_version_lineage_hardening.sql:52-54 -- `create unique index emission_data_predecessor_id_uq on public.emission_data (predecessor_id) where predecessor_id is not null;`. The index is global; nothing scopes it to entered_by_org_id, and emission_data_predecessor_id_fkey is an ordinary FK, so referential integrity is checked with RLS bypassed. Live probe inside `begin; ... rollback;`:

(a) attacker (org A) confirms it cannot see the victim row: `select count(*) from emission_data where id='b3000000-...-00000000000b'` -> 0.
(b) attacker squats the slot with a row entirely inside its OWN org and on its OWN installation:
    insert into emission_data (installation_id, entered_by_org_id, ..., predecessor_id) values ('a2000000-...','a0000000-...', ..., 'b3000000-...-00000000000b');
    -> INSERT 0 1, returning predecessor_id = b3000000-...-00000000000b
(c) switching to the victim owner's claims, the ordinary product operation:
    insert into emission_data (installation_id, entered_by_org_id, ..., predecessor_id, version) values ('b2000000-...','b0000000-...', ..., 'b3000000-...-00000000000b', 2);
    -> ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "emission_data_predecessor_id_uq"

The application always sets predecessor_id to the latest version's id, so there is no alternate path: src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:304-307 (`const predecessorId = latestRecord ? latestRecord.id : null`) and :321 (`predecessor_id: predecessorId`). Corrections cannot go through UPDATE either -- app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change pins direct_specific, indirect_specific, methodology, cn_scope, version and predecessor_id.

The same FK is a cross-tenant existence oracle: predecessor_id pointing at a nonexistent uuid returns `ERROR: insert or update on table "emission_data" violates foreign key constraint "emission_data_predecessor_id_fkey" DETAIL: Key is not present in table "emission_data".`, while a real id succeeds.
exploit: 1. Attacker's org holds an ACTIVE sharing grant on the victim producer's installation -- the ordinary importer/producer relationship. Reading shared emission_data through emission_data_select_own_org returns the row's `id` (I confirmed this in the finding above: the grantee's SELECT returned the id column). 2. The attacker POSTs one emission_data row into their OWN org, on their OWN installation, with predecessor_id set to that id. It passes emission_data_insert_own_org because every column the policy inspects is the attacker's own. 3. From that moment the victim's `recordEmissionData` for that (installation, period) fails permanently with a unique-violation on a row the victim cannot see, cannot query, and cannot delete (no DELETE policy on emission_data, and the squatting row is in another tenant). The victim's only visible symptom is an opaque PERSIST_FAILED.
impact: A cross-tenant, permanent, and invisible denial of the single most compliance-critical write in the producer half of the product: correcting a declared emissions figure. Because emission_data facts are immutable by trigger, superseding is the ONLY correction mechanism, and this removes it for the targeted (installation, reporting period). The victim gets no attribution -- the blocking row lives in the attacker's tenancy and is unreadable to them, so the failure looks like a platform bug. It is also a cross-tenant row-existence oracle for emission_data ids. Bounds: the attacker needs the victim's emission_data UUID, so this is not blind mass abuse -- but every grantee importer is handed exactly that UUID by design, and importer/producer counterparties have genuinely adversarial commercial interests. Not exploitable against a producer who has shared with nobody.
freshEnvironment: Yes. The unique index is migration DDL from 20260829290000 and is recreated identically by `supabase db reset`, `db push`, and any pg_dump/restore. Nothing in supabase/seed.sql affects index definitions. Verified in the migration file, not only in the live catalog.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced independently, not taken on trust. The shared local `postgres` DB currently has 0 public tables, so I built my own throwaway DB (`create database advrev_pred_refute template advrev_insgate`), verified its objects against the repo migration DDL, confirmed it is at release-candidate level (app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate contains the P14 v2 body from 20260903150000), then dropped it.

Schema: live catalog shows `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX emission_data_predecessor_id_uq ON public.emission_data USING btree (predecessor_id) WHERE (predecessor_id IS NOT NULL)` — global, matching supabase/migrations/20260829290000_p7_review_version_lineage_hardening.sql:52-54. `emission_data_insert_own_org` WITH CHECK constrains only entered_by_org_id and installation ownership; nothing constrains predecessor_id (contrast declarations, which scopes its predecessor via app.declaration_predecessor_matches(), 20260829340000). No BEFORE INSERT trigger on emission_data (only 4 BEFORE UPDATE), and no DELETE policy at all (pg_policy has no polcmd='d' row), so the squatting row is unremovable by the victim. emission_data_select_own_org (20260829260000:537-545) hands a grantee the full ACTIVE+VERIFIED row including its id.

Live repro, one transaction, real ROLLBACK, state verified before/after (1 emission_data row -> 1 row):
(a) attacker (importer org b0000000..., user 22222222-...-0001) SELECT emission_data -> returns victim row e1000000-...-0001 (org a0000000..., ACTIVE/VERIFIED).
(b) same authenticated session inserted its OWN operators + installations rows in its own org — an IMPORTER_DECLARANT-only org passed RLS with no capability gate.
(c) insert into emission_data (... predecessor_id) values (..., 'e1000000-...-0001') -> INSERT 0 1, returning predecessor_id = e1000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.
(d) switching claims to the victim producer's member and running exactly what recordEmissionData computes (latest lineage row e1..., version 2, predecessor e1...) -> ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "emission_data_predecessor_id_uq".
Oracle variant also confirmed: nonexistent predecessor uuid -> ERROR: ... violates foreign key constraint "emission_data_predecessor_id_fkey" DETAIL: Key is not present in table "emission_data."

Reachability lens passes. src/infrastructure/supabase/browser-client.ts:14-20 documents that the anon/publishable key is inlined into the client bundle, so every authenticated user holds a JWT and can POST arbitrary emission_data payloads directly to PostgREST; role `authenticated` holds INSERT on the table and RLS is the only control — the same threat model the repo's own shipment_line_determination_forgery_fix v2..v10 series exists for. Permanence confirmed in code: src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:304-307 and :321 always set predecessor_id to the latest lineage row's id with no status filter (so discarding v1 does not free the victim), UPDATE corrections are blocked by app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change (pins version and predecessor_id), and the victim sees only an opaque PERSIST_FAILED (manage-emission-data.ts:330-336).

Fresh-environment claim holds: this is migration DDL, unaffected by supabase/seed.sql's blanket grants. Severity HIGH stands: cross-tenant, permanent, unattributable denial of the only correction mechanism for a declared emissions figure, with no in-product remediation; bounded only by the attacker needing an ACTIVE sharing grant, which is the ordinary importer/producer relationship.

NO CONTROL BLOCKS THE SQUAT: emission_data_insert_own_org WITH CHECK is `((entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE i.id = emission_data.installation_id AND i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)))` -- predecessor_id is not inspected. pg_trigger shows no INSERT trigger on emission_data (only 4 BEFORE UPDATE triggers). pg_constraint shows emission_data_predecessor_id_fkey is an ordinary `FOREIGN KEY (predecessor_id) REFERENCES emission_data(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`.

LIVE PROBE, inside `begin; set local role authenticated; ... rollback;`:
(a) attacker claims sub=aa000000-...-00000000000a: `select count(*) from emission_data where id='b3000000-...-00000000000b'` -> "(a) attacker visible count of victim row = 0"
(b) attacker inserts into its OWN org/installation with predecessor_id = victim's id -> "(b) SQUAT OK id=fc705513-81d8-4b83-b19c-f7705cf4ccd1 predecessor_id=b3000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000b" / INSERT 0 1

NO ESCAPE PATH: app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change (prosrc read from pg_proc) raises if `new.predecessor_id is distinct from old.predecessor_id`, so UPDATE cannot correct. `select count(*) from pg_policy where polrelid='public.emission_data'::regclass and polcmd='d'` -> 0, so no DELETE policy: the victim cannot remove the squatting row (which is in the attacker's tenancy anyway). Permanence also survives discarding v1: manage-emission-data.ts:252 states the lineage lookup is "Deliberately NOT filtered to status='ACTIVE'", so latest-by-version stays v1 and the collision repeats forever.

EXISTENCE ORACLE VERIFIED: predecessor_id='deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-000000000000' -> "ERROR: insert or update on table \"emission_data\" violates foreign key constraint \"emission_data_predecessor_id_fkey\" DETAIL: Key is not present in table \"emission_data\"", versus the real cross-tenant id which was accepted in probe (b).

REACHABILITY: recordEmissionData computes predecessorId server-side, but src/infrastructure/supabase/browser-client.ts:28-35 plus NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (.env.example:35-36) means an authenticated member POSTs an arbitrary column payload directly to PostgREST; RLS + grants are the only boundary, and neither constrains predecessor_id. This is the same threat model under which every other P7-P13 finding in this repo was reproduced.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING, neither refuting it:
1. Line-number cite is off by two: `const predecessorId =` is at src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:302 (block 302-305), not 304-307. The `predecessor_id: predecessorId` cite at :321 is exact.
2. The finding understates the precondition. emission_data_select_own_org's shared branch is `((installation_id IN (SELECT app.user_shared_installation_ids())) AND (status = 'ACTIVE') AND (verification_status = 'VERIFIED'))` -- a grantee learns the victim's id only for rows that are ACTIVE *and* VERIFIED, not ACTIVE alone. This narrows the attack surface (my fixture row was ACTIVE/UNVERIFIED and would not have been grantee-readable) but does not close it: verified, shared figures are exactly the ones a producer subsequently needs to correct.

Severity HIGH is defensible and I am leaving it: permanent, cross-tenant, unattributable denial of the only correction mechanism for a declared emissions figure, surfacing to the victim only as an opaque PERSIST_FAILED (manage-emission-data.ts returns {status:"REJECTED", reason:"PERSIST_FAILED"} on insert error). It is availability/integrity of the compliance correction path rather than disclosure of numbers, and it needs an existing sharing relationship, which is what keeps it below BLOCKER.

title: record_shared_data_consumption lets a grantee write unverifiable claims into the grantor's append-only audit log, and the release certification never carried the gap forward
evidence: The gap is documented in the function body itself (live `pg_get_functiondef(public.record_shared_data_consumption)`, and supabase/migrations/20260829310000_p7d3_shared_data_consumption_audit.sql): "KNOWN GAP, WORTH-TRACKING, NOT FIXED HERE (mandatory review, 2026-08-29, live-reproduced): this check does not read sl.emission_determination at all, so it never confirms the line was actually determined from p_emission_data_id/p_emission_data_version via p_sharing_grant_id ... There is also no uniqueness constraint, CAS, or rate limit on this RPC. Confirmed live: three identical calls against a shipment_line with NO emission_determination at all each returned a distinct OK + a new audit_events row." The function is SECURITY DEFINER (prosecdef=true) and its INSERT targets `v_grant.grantor_org_id` -- i.e. it writes into a DIFFERENT tenant's audit stream, which has no UPDATE or DELETE policy by design. The grantor cannot read the grantee's side to disprove the claim (I confirmed the reciprocal: audit_events_select_own_org is `org_id IN (select app.user_org_ids())`, so neither party can see the other's stream). The honesty half: `grep -n "data_consumed\|shared_data_consumption" docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md` returns nothing, and section 15 "High-risk accepted items" (lines 369-393) lists nine items, none of them this one -- so a live-reproduced cross-tenant write gap, explicitly flagged in a migration as needing owner attention, is absent from the document that certifies the release.
exploit: A member of an org holding one ACTIVE, unexpired sharing grant calls POST /rest/v1/rpc/record_shared_data_consumption repeatedly with any shipment_line_id belonging to their own org -- including lines with no emission_determination at all -- and any valid (emission_data_id, version) under the granted installation. Each call returns OK and appends a `sharing_grant.data_consumed` audit_events row to the GRANTOR org's log, unbounded and unretractable.
impact: Cross-tenant append-only write into another organization's compliance audit trail, with no rate limit and no idempotency key. The grantor's audit log -- the record they would rely on in a dispute about who consumed their emissions data and when -- can be filled with fabricated entries by a counterparty, and there is no mechanism to remove them. Bounds, stated plainly: only a genuine member of an ACTIVE, unexpired grant can do this, not a stranger, and the events are additive noise rather than data disclosure. The severity here is as much about the certification document omitting a known, reproduced gap as about the gap itself.

title: seed.sql hands anon EXECUTE on seven SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that every migration explicitly revoked -- the same blanket-grant-after-narrow-revoke pattern, re-asserted for only one of the eight
evidence: Each RPC's migration ends with `revoke all on function public.<fn>(...) from public;` followed by a grant to `authenticated` ONLY -- confirmed by grepping the migrations: accept_organization_invitation, accept_sharing_grant_invitation, create_organization_with_owner, list_org_members, record_declaration_filed, record_shared_data_consumption and sharing_counterparty_org_names are each granted `to authenticated` (sharing_counterparty_org_names additionally `to service_role`). No migration grants any of them to anon. But supabase/seed.sql:22 runs `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` as the LAST step of `supabase db reset`, and its remediation block (seed.sql:83-101) re-asserts the revoke for record_calculation_result ALONE. Live catalog on this reset database: `select p.proname, has_function_privilege('anon', p.oid,'EXECUTE') from pg_proc p ...` -> accept_organization_invitation t, accept_sharing_grant_invitation t, create_organization_with_owner t, list_org_members t, record_declaration_filed t, record_shared_data_consumption t, sharing_counterparty_org_names t, record_calculation_result f. Seven `t` where the migrations say there should be none. seed.sql:66-70 states the coupling rule the file itself relies on -- "Anywhere a broad grant runs after a narrow revoke, the revoke has to be re-asserted" -- and it was applied to exactly one function.
exploit: None that discloses data, and I tested rather than assumed. As role anon with {"role":"anon"} claims: list_org_members('91f720bb-...') raises 'Not a member of this organization.'; record_declaration_filed, accept_organization_invitation, accept_sharing_grant_invitation and record_shared_data_consumption all raise 'requires an authenticated caller'; sharing_counterparty_org_names() returns 0 rows; create_organization_with_owner raises on the auth.uid()/confirmed-email guard. Every one of the seven is saved by its own auth.uid() precondition, not by the ACL.
impact: Today: a defence-in-depth layer that the migrations deliberately built is silently absent in every locally-reset and CI-built environment, so the pre-authentication attack surface those environments test is wider than production's. Tomorrow: this is the identical mechanism that the P14.3 CI failure exposed for calculation_results, and the seed's own remediation comment describes it as a coupling that "must be updated with" the migrations. Any future RPC added with a `revoke ... from public` inherits the same silent restoration, and any future RPC whose auth.uid() guard is forgotten or moved becomes anon-reachable in dev/CI while looking correct in the migration source. The right fix is the same shape as the one already there: re-assert the function revokes in the seed tail, or narrow the blanket grant.
freshEnvironment: This IS the fresh-environment state -- it is what `supabase db reset` produces, which is how the repo documents building a local or CI database, and I read it off exactly such a database. It does NOT exist on hosted Supabase, where seed.sql never runs and the migration revokes stand. So the divergence runs the opposite way to the P14.3 incident: dev/CI is more permissive than production, which means CI cannot catch a regression in these seven functions' ACLs.

THE SEED ORDERING, FROM SOURCE. supabase/seed.sql:23 is `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` (the finding said :22 -- off by one, immaterial; :21 is tables, :22 sequences, :23 functions). supabase/seed.sql:83-101 is the remediation `do $$` block, and it names exactly one function: `record_calculation_result(uuid,uuid,uuid,text,jsonb,text,text,jsonb,jsonb,text,uuid)`, revoked `from public, anon, authenticated` and re-granted `to service_role`. Nothing after line 101 touches function ACLs (lines 104-110 are TRUNCATE-on-tables only). Confirmed by reading the whole file.

2. THE SEVEN MIGRATIONS, FROM SOURCE. `grep -rn "revoke all on function\|grant execute on function" supabase/migrations/` -- every public RPC except record_calculation_result uses the weak pattern `revoke all on function public.<fn>(...) from public;` followed by `grant execute ... to authenticated;`:

 - 20260828120000:77-78 and 20260829360000:320-321 list_org_members(uuid)
 - 20260828130000:302-303 and 20260829380000:348-349 accept_organization_invitation(uuid)
 - 20260829300000:627-628 and 20260829390000:282-283 accept_sharing_grant_invitation(uuid,uuid)
 - 20260829310000:331-332 record_shared_data_consumption(uuid,uuid,uuid,integer,uuid,text)
 - 20260829330000:1030-1031 record_declaration_filed(uuid,text)
 - 20260831100000:95-97 and 20260902150000:194-196 sharing_counterparty_org_names() (also to service_role)
Only 20260903190000:353-357 revokes `from public, anon, authenticated`. `grep -rn "to anon" supabase/migrations/*.sql` returns two hits, both COMMENT text (20260829230000:299, 20260903170000:19) -- no migration grants anything to anon. The finding's list of seven and its "no migration grants any of them to anon" are both exact.

3. LIVE MECHANISM PROOF. In a throwaway DB (`create database advrev_anonexec_refute`, dropped afterward) I replicated both patterns verbatim and then ran seed.sql:23 verbatim:
  AFTER MIGRATIONS   fn_seven anon=false fn_rcr anon=false
  AFTER SEED BLANKET fn_seven anon=true  fn_rcr anon=true
  AFTER SEED REMEDY  fn_seven anon=true  fn_rcr anon=false
`revoke ... from public` does not survive `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon`; only the explicitly-named record_calculation_result is restored. This is deterministic ACL semantics, so it holds for any freshly built environment, not just one snapshot -- which is precisely the failure class under hunt.

4. THIS IS THE CI STATE, NOT A LOCAL ACCIDENT. .github/workflows/ci.yml:315 runs `psql ... -f supabase/seed.sql` explicitly AFTER `pnpm exec supabase migration up --local` (ci.yml:304), on top of `supabase start` (ci.yml:289) which already runs it. So CI's database provably ends in the permissive state.

5. CI CANNOT CATCH IT. The only ACL assertion in the suite is tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts (the "P14.1 -- the calculation-result write boundary" block, ~:735-790), which covers record_calculation_result alone. No test asserts anon-denial for the other seven. The finding's impact claim holds.

REACHABILITY LENS (the lens I was told to apply). anon IS a real reachable principal here -- PostgREST exposes schema public and seed.sql:19 grants anon USAGE, so an unauthenticated POST /rest/v1/rpc/<fn> reaches the function body in any locally-reset or CI environment. But every one of the seven is saved by its own in-body guard, which I verified in source rather than trusting: six raise explicitly (`create_organization_with_owner requires an authenticated caller.` 20260828080000:68; `Not a member of this organization.` 20260828120000:52 / 20260829360000:288; `accept_organization_invitation requires an authenticated caller.` 20260828130000:190; `accept_sharing_grant_invitation requires an authenticated caller.` 20260829300000:482; `record_shared_data_consumption requires an authenticated caller.` 20260829310000:130; `record_declaration_filed requires an authenticated caller.` 20260829330000:630), and the seventh, sharing_counterparty_org_names(), filters its entire result through `sg.grantee_org_id in (select app.user_org_ids())` / `sg.grantor_org_id in (select app.user_org_ids())`, where app.user_org_ids() is `select org_id from public.memberships where user_id = auth.uid()` (20260828070000) -- null auth.uid() yields zero rows. So NO data or state is reachable. The ACL is the outer of two layers and the inner one holds. That is exactly what the finding itself claims, and it is why LOW/OPERATIONS is the correct severity: an environment-fidelity and defence-in-depth defect, not an exploitable vulnerability.

ONE CLAIM IN THE FINDING I WOULD NOT ENDORSE (partially evidenced, unverified). Its "fresh-environment" paragraph asserts the divergence runs dev-more-permissive-than-production because "seed.sql never runs and the migration revokes stand" on hosted. That may be wrong in the finding's own favour: hosted Supabase provisions `alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role`, so a function created by a migration on hosted receives an EXPLICIT anon grant at CREATE time, which `revoke ... from public` does not remove. The repo's own author appears to know this -- 20260903190000:350-352 comments "Stated as an explicit revoke-then-grant rather than relying on defaults, so a future `alter default privileges` cannot quietly widen it," and that migration alone revokes from anon by name. If so, production carries the same seven anon EXECUTE grants and the fix belongs in the migrations, not only the seed. I did NOT verify this against production (I ran no production queries), so I report it as an unverified nuance. It would make the finding broader, never narrower -- so it is no basis for refutation.

Net: every material assertion checked out under my own re-derivation. Severity stands at LOW.
