title: create_organization_with_owner leaks a cross-tenant organization-existence oracle by slug, and permits slug squatting
exploit: Any authenticated user calls POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_organization_with_owner with a guessed slug (slugs are derived from organization names, so 'acme-steel', 'thyssenkrupp-gmbh' etc. are guessable). A 23505 with the slug echoed means that organization exists on the platform; success means it does not. The successful branch also permanently claims the slug, so an attacker can pre-register the slugs of prospective customers.
impact: Discloses the existence of other tenants on the platform to any signed-up user -- customer-list enumeration for a compliance product where the tenant roster is itself commercially sensitive. Also enables denial-of-registration by squatting a target's natural slug. It leaks only existence, never any row content, and each probe costs a real organization row (so it is noisy and self-limiting), which is why this is LOW rather than higher. Related and weaker: emission_data_predecessor_id_fkey and suppliers_linked_operator_id_fk return 'Key is not present in table X' for a nonexistent id versus success for a real one, giving the same existence oracle over emission_data.id and operators.id -- but those need a UUID rather than a guessable name.
freshEnvironment: Yes. The unique constraint and the RPC are both migration DDL (20260828070000 and 20260828080000); no seed, reset or restore step changes either. Verified against the migration sources as well as live behaviour.

verdicts.reasoning:
I rebuilt a fresh environment myself rather than trusting the reporter's DB. The main local `postgres` DB had no public schema at all (`select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> empty), so I created throwaway db `advrev_slugoracle_x9`, loaded the `auth` schema via pg_dump, applied all 74 migrations in order (only storage/regulatory-dataset migrations failed, none relevant), then applied supabase/seed.sql, then dropped the DB.

MECHANISM: confirmed, exactly as claimed.
- `select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) ... contype='u'` -> `organizations_slug_uq|UNIQUE (slug)` (source: supabase/migrations/20260828070000_create_organizations_foundation.sql:88-89).
- proacl before seed: `postgres=X/postgres|authenticated=X/postgres`; after seed also `anon=X/postgres|service_role=X/postgres`.
- Probe A (unrelated confirmed user 2222..., existing slug), inside `begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims=...; rollback;`:
  ERROR:  duplicate key value violates unique constraint "organizations_slug_uq"
  DETAIL:  Key (slug)=(victim-steel-gmbh) already exists.
- Probe B (same user, unused slug): returned `d8f5cb82-0a75-478c-94c0-a7df39529ddc`. Post-state `select slug from public.organizations` -> only `victim-steel-gmbh`, so both rollbacks held.
So the two branches are distinguishable and the DETAIL echoes the probed slug. The reporter's evidence is accurate.

WHY IT IS NOT A DEFECT:
1. It is the feature, deliberately surfaced. app/onboarding/actions.ts:155-161 explicitly maps `error.code === "23505"` to the user-facing string "That organization URL is already taken -- try a different one." The product MUST tell a user their chosen slug is taken or onboarding is unusable. The "oracle" is a first-class designed response, not an accidental leak; suppressing the DB DETAIL would not remove it, because the app already tells the caller "taken" in plain English. There is no fix that keeps a globally unique, user-chosen slug and removes the signal.
2. Already identified and reasoned about in-repo as accepted risk. app/onboarding/actions.ts:27-33 names this exact property verbatim ("organizations has no DELETE policy, and organizations_slug_uq is a GLOBAL unique constraint, so a squatted slug can never be reclaimed") as the stated justification for the 5-per-10-minutes rate limiter. This is a documented tradeoff, not an undiscovered defect.
3. The claimed impact does not hold up. The slug is NOT a routing key: `find app -type d -name "*slug*"` returns nothing; the only dynamic segments are `[id]` (declarations, shipments, api/evidence). Slug appears only as a display field in app/organization/danger-zone.tsx:84 and app/organization/page.tsx:96. So "denial-of-registration by squatting" squats a cosmetic display string, not a URL, subdomain or namespace. And slugs are client-side slugify() output that the user may freely override (app/onboarding/onboarding-form.tsx:138-172, `slugEditedManually`), so name->slug is not a reliable mapping and a hit does not identify a company.
4. Zero row content is disclosed. organizations RLS is tight -- the four SELECT policies are membership-scoped or invitation/grant-scoped (`organizations_select_own_org` = `id IN (select app.user_org_ids())`, etc.). A collision reveals only that some string is taken.
5. The actor bar is higher than "any authenticated user". Live: as `anon` -> `ERROR: create_organization_with_owner requires an authenticated caller.`; as an authenticated user with `email_confirmed_at IS NULL` -> `ERROR: Confirm your email address before creating an organization.` (the check at 20260829460000 runs BEFORE the insert, so an unconfirmed caller never reaches the slug). Every successful probe writes an `organization.created` audit_events row under the attacker's own user id (20260829460000 body), so enumeration is self-incriminating.

FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CLASS CHECK (the class this review is hunting): I did verify the constraint and the RPC survive a fresh migrate+seed build, and they do -- but that cuts the other way here, since it means the behavior is stable and intended rather than an artifact of ordering. The only thing seed.sql changes is adding `anon`/`service_role` EXECUTE on the function, and anon is still stopped by the `auth.uid() is null` guard.

RESIDUAL (not enough to sustain the finding): the rate limiter cited in app/onboarding/actions.ts is in the Server Action only, so a direct POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_organization_with_owner is unrated. That is a real gap in mitigation coverage, but it does not create the oracle -- it only affects the speed of an already-designed, content-free, audit-logged signal. Worth an accepted-risk note at most, not a release finding.

I could not refute it — every technical claim checks out, and I re-derived them in a database I built from the migration sources alone.

Environment note: the shared local `postgres` database currently has an EMPTY public schema (`select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='public'` -> 0; `pg_proc` in public -> 0), so the finding's original evidence is not re-runnable there. I therefore built a genuinely fresh environment: `create database advrev_slug_refute`, restored a schema-only pg_dump of the auth/storage/extensions schemas, then applied every file in supabase/migrations/ in filename order (only 4 storage-bucket / regulatory-dataset migrations failed, none touching organizations). Dropped it afterwards (`DROP DATABASE`).

1) Constraint is global and real (supabase/migrations/20260828070000_create_organizations_foundation.sql:88-89):
select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid='public.organizations'::regclass and conname like '%slug%';
-> organizations_slug_format_ck|CHECK ((slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$'::text))
-> organizations_slug_uq|UNIQUE (slug)
No org_id/tenant scoping. Confirmed.

2) RPC is SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE to authenticated, exposed via PostgREST:
select p.oid::regprocedure, p.prosecdef, p.proacl from pg_proc ... where proname='create_organization_with_owner';
-> create_organization_with_owner(text,text,text[])|t|{postgres=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres}
supabase/config.toml:13 -> schemas = ["public", "graphql_public"], so /rest/v1/rpc/create_organization_with_owner is reachable. Confirmed.

3) No pre-check, no error translation. pg_get_functiondef of the live (post-hardening) body shows only an auth.uid() null check and an app.user_confirmed_email() check, then a bare `insert into public.organizations (name, slug, capabilities) values (p_name, p_slug, p_capabilities) returning * into v_org;` with no exception handler. Confirmed.

4) Live oracle, reproduced in the fresh DB. Victim (11111111-…) created slug 'acme-steel' (committed in the throwaway DB). Then as an unrelated authenticated user (22222222-…), each inside `begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims=...; ...; rollback;`:
  A) select (public.create_organization_with_owner('X','acme-steel','{IMPORTER_DECLARANT}')).id;
     -> ERROR:  duplicate key value violates unique constraint "organizations_slug_uq"
        DETAIL:  Key (slug)=(acme-steel) already exists.
  B) select (public.create_organization_with_owner('X','definitely-unused-slug-zzz','{IMPORTER_DECLARANT}')).id;
     -> e5c0b561-5c62-4b8f-a627-c22208776f32 (succeeds)
Post-state verified after both rollbacks: select count(*), string_agg(slug,',') from public.organizations; -> 1|acme-steel. Two cleanly distinguishable responses; the error echoes the probed value.

5) Squatting is permanent: pg_policies on organizations lists only SELECT policies plus organizations_update_owner — there is no DELETE policy, so a squatted slug cannot be reclaimed by any authenticated user. The repo itself already states this in app/onboarding/actions.ts:28-31 ("organizations has no DELETE policy, and organizations_slug_uq is a GLOBAL unique constraint, so a squatted slug can never be reclaimed").

6) Fresh-environment claim holds, and is in fact worse than stated: both the constraint and the RPC come from migration DDL only; supabase/seed.sql does not touch them narrowly — but seed.sql:23 (`grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role`) re-grants EXECUTE broadly after reset, so nothing closes this on a rebuild.

Two refinements the finding omitted, neither of which refutes it:
- The current live body (post 20260829460000) additionally requires app.user_confirmed_email() to be non-null. An ordinary signed-up user satisfies this trivially, so the "any authenticated user" premise stands.
- There IS an existing mitigation, but only in the Next.js Server Action: app/onboarding/actions.ts:41-51 defines an IP-keyed 5-per-10-minutes createOrganizationLimiter. It is entirely bypassed by calling POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_organization_with_owner directly with the user's JWT, since the limiter lives in application code and there is no database-level equivalent. This slightly strengthens the finding rather than refuting it (the documented mitigation does not cover the documented attack path), though the per-probe cost of a real, undeletable organization row still keeps the practical severity at LOW.

Confirmed by my own source review and an isolated live reproduction; I could not find a mitigation.

SOURCE (release-candidate tree):
1. supabase/migrations/20260828070000_create_organizations_foundation.sql:88-89 — `constraint organizations_slug_uq unique (slug)`. Global. Grepping all 60 migrations for slug + unique/drop constraint/add constraint returns no later migration that drops or rescopes it.
2. The current definition of the RPC is supabase/migrations/20260829460000_p13_review_onboarding_email_confirmation_hardening.sql:63-145 (not 20260828080000 as the finding says — it was redefined twice, by 20260828090000 and 20260829460000). The body inserts p_slug directly into public.organizations with NO pre-check and NO `exception when unique_violation` handler.
3. supabase/migrations/20260828080000_organization_onboarding_rpc.sql:107-108 — `revoke all on function ... from public; grant execute on function ... to authenticated;`. Grep of every migration for `create_organization_with_owner` combined with grant|revoke returns ONLY these two lines; nothing later narrows it.

LIVE REPRODUCTION. The shared local postgres DB was mid-`supabase db reset` for my entire run (`select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> 0, and `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` did not exist), so I created an isolated throwaway DB `advrev_slug_refute`, loaded the organizations DDL plus the VERBATIM function body from lines 63-145 of 20260829460000, and dropped the DB afterwards (`drop database advrev_slug_refute` -> DROP DATABASE; scratch files removed).

  insert into public.organizations (name, slug, capabilities) values ('Victim Co','acme-steel','{IMPORTER_DECLARANT}');  -- INSERT 0 1

  begin; select (public.create_organization_with_owner('Attacker','acme-steel','{IMPORTER_DECLARANT}')).id; rollback;
  -> ERROR:  duplicate key value violates unique constraint "organizations_slug_uq"
     DETAIL:  Key (slug)=(acme-steel) already exists.
     CONTEXT: ... PL/pgSQL function create_organization_with_owner(text,text,text[]) line 26 at SQL statement

  begin; select (public.create_organization_with_owner('Attacker','definitely-unused-slug-zzz','{IMPORTER_DECLARANT}')).id; rollback;
  ->                  id
     101a571c-a8b5-4c93-bb1a-75bded95dde7
     ROLLBACK

Two cleanly distinguishable branches; the error echoes the probed slug. Matches the finder's reported output exactly.

MITIGATIONS SEARCHED FOR AND NOT FOUND (already-mitigated lens):
- Email-confirmation gate added by 20260829460000 (`if app.user_confirmed_email() is null then raise`) fires BEFORE the insert. It narrows the attacker to a confirmed account; it does not touch the oracle. The finder omitted this precondition — a real inaccuracy in their "any authenticated user" phrasing, but not one that changes the outcome.
- The IP-keyed rate limiter (5 per 10 minutes) lives only in app/onboarding/actions.ts (createOrganizationLimiter). supabase/config.toml:13 exposes `public` to PostgREST, so a direct POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_organization_with_owner with the publishable anon key plus a user JWT bypasses the Server Action and its limiter entirely.
- The only trigger on organizations is `organizations_capabilities_append_only` (20260903160000:77-79), declared `before update on public.organizations` — it cannot affect an INSERT.
- No DELETE policy on organizations exists in any migration (`grep -rn "for delete" supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -i organizations` -> empty; `select count(*) from pg_policies where tablename='organizations' and cmd='DELETE'` -> 0). The squatting half of the finding is therefore also correct: a claimed slug is unreclaimable. The implementer states this themselves at 20260829460000:26-30.

FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CHECK: both the constraint and the grant are plain migration DDL. supabase/seed.sql:23 (`grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role`) only WIDENS this on every reset — it re-grants EXECUTE to anon as well. That does not create an anon oracle, because the `auth.uid() is null` check raises first and returns the same message for every slug. So the finding's fresh-environment claim holds, and is if anything understated.

SEVERITY: I would keep LOW, not raise it. A globally unique slug is an approved master-plan requirement (docs/plans/MASTER_PLAN.md:80 "slug unique") and app/onboarding/actions.ts deliberately surfaces "That organization URL is already taken -- try a different one." to the user, so slug-collision disclosure is intended product UX rather than an implementation slip. What is genuinely new and unmitigated is (a) the direct-REST path skipping the rate limiter, (b) the raw 23505 echoing the probed slug back, and (c) each negative probe permanently claiming an unreclaimable slug. No row content ever leaks, and a hit proves only that some org holds that string, not that it is the named company.

title: anon and authenticated hold TRIGGER, REFERENCES and MAINTAIN on every table in public, and authenticated can create functions in pg_temp
evidence:
Live ACLs: every table shows `anon=arwdxtm/postgres authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres` (the `t` is TRIGGER, `x` is REFERENCES, `m` is MAINTAIN); the P14.1 fix removed only `D` (TRUNCATE). Live confirmation inside `begin; ... rollback;` as role authenticated with real JWT claims:
  select has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.organizations','TRIGGER'); -> t
  create function pg_temp.leak() returns trigger language plpgsql as $f$ begin return new; end $f$;  -> CREATE FUNCTION
  create trigger zz_leak_trg before insert on public.organizations for each row execute function pg_temp.leak();  -> CREATE TRIGGER
Both statements succeeded as `authenticated` on a table it does not own. Countervailing facts I checked rather than assumed: `select rolname, rolcanlogin from pg_roles` shows authenticated and anon are both NOLOGIN, and has_schema_privilege('authenticated','public','CREATE') is false.
exploit: NONE reachable. The DDL above requires a direct SQL session as role authenticated. That role is NOLOGIN and is only ever entered via PostgREST's SET ROLE, and PostgREST has no verb that issues DDL -- the same reasoning the P14 audit correctly applied to the TRUNCATE finding at section 19.D. A REFERENCES-based FK oracle from a temp table is separately impossible: Postgres refuses foreign keys between temporary and permanent tables.
impact: None today. Recorded because if an attacker or a future feature ever obtains a direct connection able to SET ROLE authenticated (a leaked pooler credential, a debugging path, an admin tool), TRIGGER on every public table combined with pg_temp function creation is a full cross-tenant exfiltration primitive: a trigger installed on organizations or memberships executes inside the victim's own session with the victim's privileges and can copy their rows into a table the attacker can read. That is a materially larger consequence than the TRUNCATE the same grant line carried, and the same one-line fix (`revoke trigger, references on all tables in schema public from anon, authenticated`, plus the default privileges) closes it.
freshEnvironment: Yes, and it is worse in a fresh one. The grants come from supabase/seed.sql:22-24's `grant all on all tables` plus `alter default privileges ... grant all on tables`, so every reset re-establishes them and every future table inherits them automatically. Hosted Supabase's own bootstrap grant has the same shape, so this is not a local-only artifact -- I confirmed the seed's revoke tail (seed.sql:104-111) removes only TRUNCATE.

verdicts.reasoning:
I re-ran the finding's own evidence. It is factually accurate, but its reachability and impact reasoning do not survive checking.

WHAT IS TRUE (verified, not trusted). D:\projects\snowkap-cbam\supabase\seed.sql:22-31 does `grant all on all tables in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role` plus `alter default privileges ... grant all on tables`; the revoke tail at seed.sql:104-111 removes only TRUNCATE (plus the calculation_results DML / record_calculation_result EXECUTE in the DO block, seed.sql:84-102). I reproduced that exact sequence in a fresh throwaway db (`create database advrev_trigger_refute`; the local `postgres` db currently has ZERO tables in public -- other agents have it mid-rebuild, so I could not use it):
  relacl -> {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,anon=arwdxtm/postgres,authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}
t=TRIGGER, x=REFERENCES, m=MAINTAIN do survive the P14.1 TRUNCATE revoke in a freshly built environment. Inside `begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims=...; ... rollback;`:
  has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.organizations','TRIGGER') -> t ; REFERENCES -> t ; has_schema_privilege(...,'public','CREATE') -> f
  create function pg_temp.leak() ... -> CREATE FUNCTION
  create trigger zz_leak_trg before insert on public.organizations ... -> CREATE TRIGGER
  post-ROLLBACK re-check of pg_trigger -> 0 rows (nothing stuck).

WHY IT IS STILL NOT A DEFECT.

1. The precondition already implies a strictly greater compromise. The DDL needs a direct SQL session as `authenticated`. `select rolname, rolcanlogin, rolbypassrls from pg_roles` -> anon/authenticated/service_role all NOLOGIN; the only login role holding them is `authenticator`:
  select r.rolname, g.rolname from pg_auth_members m join pg_roles r on r.oid=m.member join pg_roles g on g.oid=m.roleid -> authenticator|anon, authenticator|authenticated, authenticator|service_role
So the hypothesised attacker ("a leaked pooler credential, a debugging path, an admin tool" able to SET ROLE authenticated) can equally `set role service_role`, which is rolbypassrls=t and holds arwdDxtm on every table: read/write/truncate of every tenant's rows with no RLS at all. TRIGGER/REFERENCES/MAINTAIN on `authenticated` add zero marginal capability to anyone who can meet the precondition. No PostgREST-reachable DDL path exists either: grepping every migration for dynamic SQL (`execute format(` / `execute '`, excluding `execute function|procedure` and `grant/revoke execute`) returns zero hits across supabase/migrations/*.sql, so no SECURITY DEFINER RPC relays attacker text into DDL.

2. The claimed impact ("a full cross-tenant exfiltration primitive") is empirically false even granting the precondition. A pg_temp trigger function is dropped when the creating session ends, cascading the trigger away. Committed in session A, then a new session B:
  session A: create pg_temp.leak(); create trigger zz_leak_trg ...; select tgfoid::regprocedure -> pg_temp_9.leak()
  session B: insert into public.organizations(name) values ('victim-row'); -> INSERT 0 1
             select tgname from pg_trigger where tgrelid='public.organizations'::regclass and not tgisinternal -> (0 rows)
The trigger never fires in a victim's session; it is already gone. A persistent trigger needs a persistent function, and `authenticated` has CREATE on no schema in the cluster: has_schema_privilege('authenticated', nspname, 'CREATE') is f for all 12 non-system schemas (public, auth, storage, extensions, vault, realtime, graphql, graphql_public, supabase_functions, supabase_migrations, pgbouncer, _realtime). The REFERENCES/FK-oracle route dies for the same reason (no table creatable anywhere), as the finding itself concedes. MAINTAIN (VACUUM/ANALYZE/REINDEX/REFRESH MATVIEW) likewise has no HTTP verb.

Net: the ACL observation is correct and the one-line hardening would be harmless, but no actor, route or capability turns it into anything, and in the only scenario meeting its precondition the attacker already has service_role. Refuted on reachability; the recorded impact rationale is additionally disproved by test. (Throwaway db dropped afterwards; no repo file touched, no write outside my own temporary database.)

I re-ran the evidence rather than trusting it, and every element reproduced.

SOURCE FILE CHECK. `grep -n` on D:/projects/snowkap-cbam/supabase/seed.sql returns exactly what the finding quotes: line 21 `grant all on all tables in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;`, lines 25-26 `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on tables to anon, authenticated, service_role;`, and the revoke tail at 104-110 which removes ONLY TRUNCATE (`revoke truncate on all tables in schema public from anon, authenticated;` plus the two matching `alter default privileges ... revoke truncate on tables`). A repo-wide `grep -rniE "revoke +(all +)?(trigger|references|maintain)"` across *.sql/*.ts/*.md returned zero matches — nothing anywhere revokes TRIGGER or REFERENCES. Since seed.sql runs last in `supabase db reset`, the grant is authoritative in any freshly built environment. The finding's fresh-environment claim is correct.

LIVE CHECK, complication worth recording. The main local `postgres` database currently has ZERO tables in `public` (`select count(*) ... relkind='r'` -> 0; `public.organizations` errors with "relation does not exist"), so I could not re-run the finding's literal SQL there. I instead created a throwaway database `advrev_trg_opus2` and replayed seed.sql's grant/revoke statements verbatim against a postgres-owned, RLS-enabled `public.organizations`. Resulting ACL:
  {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,anon=arwdxtm/postgres,authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}
That is character-for-character the `anon=arwdxtm/postgres authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres` the finding reported — D (TRUNCATE) gone, t (TRIGGER), x (REFERENCES), m (MAINTAIN) present.

MUTATION PROBE, inside a real `begin; ... rollback;` as role authenticated with the stated JWT claims:
  select current_user, has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.organizations','TRIGGER'), ...REFERENCES -> authenticated | t | t
  create function pg_temp.leak() returns trigger language plpgsql as $f$ begin return new; end $f$;  -> CREATE FUNCTION
  create trigger zz_leak_trg before insert on public.organizations for each row execute function pg_temp.leak();  -> CREATE TRIGGER
  select tgname from pg_trigger where tgrelid='public.organizations'::regclass and not tgisinternal;  -> zz_leak_trg
Post-ROLLBACK verification in a separate session: leftover_triggers -> 0. The throwaway database was then dropped (`drop database advrev_trg_opus2` -> DROP DATABASE, confirmed absent from pg_database). No repo file was touched.

COUNTERVAILING FACTS RE-CHECKED, not assumed. `select rolname, rolcanlogin from pg_roles` -> authenticated|f, anon|f (both NOLOGIN); authenticator|t and postgres|t are the only login roles. `has_schema_privilege('authenticated','public','CREATE')` -> f. The claimed impossibility of a REFERENCES-based FK oracle also holds: `create temp table t_att (org_id uuid references public.organizations(id))` as authenticated -> ERROR: constraints on temporary tables may reference only temporary tables. So the finding did not overstate reachability — its own "NONE reachable" caveat is itself accurate, and PostgREST exposes no DDL verb, matching the reasoning the P14 audit applied to the TRUNCATE case.

CONCLUSION. Nothing in the finding is technically wrong. The ACL string, the two DDL statements, the seed line numbers, and all three limiting facts reproduce exactly. INFO is the right severity: real and durable across resets, but with no exploit path from the app's actual surface today. I am not refuting it.

CONFIRMED by independent reproduction in a fresh throwaway database (created and dropped by me: `advrev_trig_opus2`), not by trusting the finder's evidence.

1) Fresh-environment mechanism, verified. `supabase/seed.sql:22-24` (`grant all on all tables/sequences/functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role`) and `seed.sql:26-33` (`alter default privileges ... grant all on tables`) run as the LAST step of `supabase db reset`, and the deliberate-revoke tail only removes TRUNCATE (`revoke truncate on all tables ...`, `alter default privileges ... revoke truncate on tables`, seed.sql end). I replicated exactly that sequence on a table created before the grants:
  relacl -> {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,anon=arwdxtm/postgres,authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}
  has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.orgs','TRIGGER')=t, 'REFERENCES'=t, 'TRUNCATE'=f, has_schema_privilege('authenticated','public','CREATE')=f, has_database_privilege('authenticated',db,'TEMP')=t
So `t` (TRIGGER), `x` (REFERENCES) and `m` (MAINTAIN) survive; only `D` was removed. Exactly as claimed.

2) ALREADY-MITIGATED lens applied and came back empty. `grep -rniE "revoke" supabase/migrations/*.sql` shows the only privilege revokes are: `revoke all on function ... from public` (five RPCs), `revoke truncate on all tables ... from anon, authenticated` (20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql:48,54,68) and `revoke insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results` (20260903190000:147). No migration, trigger, CHECK, policy or test revokes TRIGGER or REFERENCES. No `grant create on schema` anywhere; in a fully migrated db (advrev_slug_refute) has_schema_privilege('authenticated', nsp,'CREATE') is false for public, auth and app.

3) DDL as `authenticated`, verified inside a real `begin; ... rollback;` with before/after state checks (before_rows=1, after_triggers=0, after_rows=1):
  set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims='{"sub":"...","role":"authenticated"}'; current_user -> authenticated
  create function pg_temp.leak() ... -> CREATE FUNCTION
  create trigger zz_leak_trg before insert on public.orgs ... -> CREATE TRIGGER (pg_trigger shows it on orgs)
  rollback -> trigger gone, row count unchanged.

4) I attempted to refute the IMPACT narrative and failed. My hypothesis was that a pg_temp trigger function is session-local and therefore useless against a victim session. Half of that is true and worth recording as a refinement: after the attacker's session ends the trigger is dropped with the temp function (new-session `select tgname from pg_trigger where tgname='zz_leak_trg'` -> empty; a later insert by another session succeeded and stole nothing). But while the attacker's session is alive the primitive DOES work cross-session: attacker session installed `pg_temp.leak()` that does `insert into public.stolen values (new.secret)` plus a BEFORE INSERT trigger on public.orgs, then held the session with pg_sleep(12); a separate session's `insert into public.orgs values (3,'tenant-c-secret')` returned INSERT 0 1 and `select * from public.stolen` -> `tenant-c-secret`. So the exfiltration claim stands, non-persistently.

5) Reachability, checked rather than assumed, and it agrees with the finding's own "NONE reachable": anon/authenticated are NOLOGIN and are only entered via PostgREST's SET ROLE; PostgREST has no DDL verb; `grep -rniE "execute format\(|execute '" supabase/migrations/*.sql` returns no dynamic SQL outside seed.sql's own do-block; package.json declares no direct Postgres driver (`pg`/`postgres`/`slonik`), so the app has no non-PostgREST SQL path.

6) The hosted-environment sub-claim is corroborated without touching production: 20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql:18 states the hosted Supabase bootstrap itself does `grant all on all tables in schema public`, and docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1437 records `authenticated=arwdxtm`. I did not connect to production.

Conclusion: every factual and fresh-environment claim reproduces; nothing mitigates it; no reachable exploit exists today, which is exactly what the finding says. INFO is the correct severity — the same defence-in-depth argument the repo already accepted for TRUNCATE one line earlier in the same grant.

title: The "evidence may grow but never shrink" invariant is fully bypassed by a DISCARDED -> DRAFT detour: evidence behind an ACTIVE+VERIFIED record can be destroyed and swapped, and the record restored to ACTIVE+VERIFIED with the same id
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql:125-129 blocks only `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and new.status = 'DRAFT'`; :141-156 keys the evidence-shrink gate on `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED'`; :106-113 keys the un-verify gate on `old.status = 'ACTIVE'`. Nothing blocks ACTIVE -> DISCARDED -> DRAFT. supabase/migrations/20260829560000_...evidence_files_verified_delete_lock.sql:43 keys the evidence_files DELETE lock on `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'` alone, so un-verifying first unlocks it.

Live, against 127.0.0.1:54322, as role `authenticated` with jwt sub = 36d33703-00e9-4b0f-8695-d1f73046b326 (OWNER of org 754c5a85-9ab9-4772-a6df-ecf8a4a1ea4c), target emission_data 2210a59a-a767-4c4b-ad96-61b94fd85398 (ACTIVE / VERIFIED / evidence {2e5cd514-21f4-4204-b663-515143c9d8bf}), all inside `begin; ... rollback;`:

  CONTROL first: update emission_data set evidence_file_ids='{}'  -> ERROR: "evidence cannot be removed from an ACTIVE, VERIFIED record" (gate confirmed in force)

  step 1 update emission_data set status='DISCARDED'            -> UPDATE 1
  step 2 update emission_data set status='DRAFT'                -> UPDATE 1
  step 3 update emission_data set verification_status='VERIFICATION_PENDING' -> UPDATE 1
  step 4 insert into evidence_files (... id 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111, sha256 bbbb...) -> INSERT 0 1
  step 5 update emission_data set evidence_file_ids=array['11111111-...'] -> UPDATE 1
  step 6 delete from evidence_files where id='2e5cd514-...'      -> DELETE 1
  step 7 update emission_data set verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id=<self> -> UPDATE 1
  step 8 update emission_data set status='ACTIVE'               -> UPDATE 1

  in-transaction result: 2210a59a-... | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | {11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111}
                         evidence_files for that record: only 11111111-... (storage_path .../swapped-evidence.pdf, sha256 bbbb...)
  post-ROLLBACK verification: 2210a59a-... | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | {2e5cd514-...}, evidence_files row 2e5cd514-... present. Nothing committed.

A PLAIN MEMBER variant (membership inserted inside the same rolled-back transaction, role MEMBER, user a4ef3f67-c353-4d71-9285-22a4ab5af0b9) needs only 4 statements and no ADMIN/OWNER: status='DISCARDED' -> UPDATE 1; verification_status='VERIFICATION_PENDING' -> UPDATE 1; delete from evidence_files where id='2e5cd514-...' -> DELETE 1; evidence_file_ids='{}' -> UPDATE 1. In-transaction state DISCARDED / VERIFICATION_PENDING / {} with 0 evidence rows. Post-rollback state restored and the injected membership gone (count 0).
exploit: Any member of the producer organization, over PostgREST with their own JWT (authenticated holds a,r,w,d on both tables per pg_class.relacl; emission_data_update_own_org requires only org membership, no ADMIN/OWNER), issues: PATCH emission_data {status:DISCARDED}; PATCH {status:DRAFT}; PATCH {verification_status:VERIFICATION_PENDING}; DELETE evidence_files?id=eq.<the file the importer froze>; PATCH emission_data {evidence_file_ids:[<a new file>]}. An ADMIN/OWNER then adds PATCH {verification_status:VERIFIED} and PATCH {status:ACTIVE} to put the record back to ACTIVE+VERIFIED carrying different evidence under the same row id and version. No UI affordance exists for DISCARDED->DRAFT; this is raw-API reachable, which is the same threat model 20260829310000 explicitly writes for ("directly callable via supabase.rpc() by any authenticated client").
impact: Own-tenant actor, cross-tenant harm -- the party damaged is the importer, who has no way to see it. The importer's frozen ActualEmissionSnapshot compares its evidence set byte-for-byte against the live array (20260902140000 lines 194-207), so after the swap the frozen determination silently stops validating and the importer's error says only "locked or void". Worse than the array-emptying defect this migration was written to close: the underlying evidence_files rows are destroyed, so a filed CBAM declaration's provenance chain points at rows that no longer exist anywhere, and the verifier's own basis for the VERIFIED stamp is gone -- precisely the harm 20260829560000's header names. There is no DB-level audit trigger on emission_data (only prevent_fact_change, verification_gate, touch_updated_at, activation_gate), the raw path writes no audit_events, and audit_events RLS is own-org, so the importer cannot observe any of it. If the record is left DISCARDED (the member-only variant), the importer additionally loses read access entirely via emission_data_select_own_org's ACTIVE+VERIFIED clause.
freshEnvironment: Yes. The exploit depends only on trigger logic created by migrations, not on any grant, so the seed.sql blanket-grant hazard is irrelevant to it. I read the migration file text (20260903150000 lines 106-156) as well as the deployed pg_proc body of app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate() and they agree: the only status guard is `old.status='ACTIVE' and new.status='DRAFT'`, with no DISCARDED/SUPERSEDED -> DRAFT branch. CI applies this same file (.github/workflows/ci.yml runs the full migration set then seed.sql), so any db reset / CI build / hosted push reproduces it identically. The repo's own regression suite confirms the gap is untested: tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts:665 asserts only "an ACTIVE record cannot be walked back to DRAFT" and :622 only the same-statement variant -- no test routes through DISCARDED.

verdicts.reasoning:
I re-ran everything myself against 127.0.0.1:54322; I did not rely on the finding's evidence.

CODE / DEPLOYED-OBJECT CHECK
- `select prosrc from pg_proc where proname='enforce_emission_data_verification_gate'` returns exactly the migration text of supabase/migrations/20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql. The only status guard in it is `if old.status = 'ACTIVE' and new.status = 'DRAFT'`. There is no DISCARDED->DRAFT or SUPERSEDED->DRAFT branch. The un-verify gate is keyed `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED'`; the evidence-shrink gate likewise `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED'`. Once the row is parked at DISCARDED, all three stop applying.
- `pg_get_constraintdef` over public.emission_data: `emission_data_status_check` is a bare membership CHECK. No status-transition constraint exists.
- Triggers on emission_data: prevent_fact_change, verification_gate, touch_updated_at, activation_gate. `enforce_emission_data_activation_gate` only requires `old.status='DRAFT' and new.verification_status='VERIFIED' and evidence_file_ids non-empty` for ACTIVE, so the walk-back re-activates cleanly. No audit trigger, confirming the "invisible to the importer" part.
- evidence_files_delete_own_org (20260829560000_p13_review_evidence_files_verified_delete_lock.sql:43) is keyed on `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'` alone, so un-verifying first unlocks the DELETE.

LIVE REPRODUCTION (real BEGIN ... ROLLBACK, state verified before and after; nothing committed)
Control, as OWNER 36d33703-00e9-4b0f-8695-d1f73046b326 on emission_data 2210a59a-a767-4c4b-ad96-61b94fd85398 (ACTIVE/VERIFIED/{2e5cd514-...}):
  update emission_data set evidence_file_ids='{}' -> ERROR: "emission_data: evidence cannot be removed from an ACTIVE, VERIFIED record..." (gate in force).
Full detour, same session:
  status='DISCARDED' -> UPDATE 1
  status='DRAFT' -> UPDATE 1
  verification_status='VERIFICATION_PENDING' -> UPDATE 1
  insert evidence_files 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 (sha256 bbbb...) -> INSERT 0 1
  evidence_file_ids=array['11111111-...'] -> UPDATE 1
  delete from evidence_files where id='2e5cd514-...' -> DELETE 1
  verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id=self -> UPDATE 1
  status='ACTIVE' -> UPDATE 1
  in-transaction: 2210a59a-... | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | {11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111} | version 1; only evidence row is the swapped one.
  post-ROLLBACK: ACTIVE | VERIFIED | {2e5cd514-...}, evidence row 2e5cd514-... present, sha256 aaaa.... Nothing committed.

PLAIN-MEMBER VARIANT (membership inserted and rolled back in the same tx; `select app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of('754c5a85-...')` returned `f` for that user):
  status='DISCARDED' -> UPDATE 1; verification_status='VERIFICATION_PENDING' -> UPDATE 1; delete evidence_files 2e5cd514 -> DELETE 1; evidence_file_ids='{}' -> UPDATE 1. End state DISCARDED/VERIFICATION_PENDING/{} with 0 evidence rows, achieved with no ADMIN/OWNER. Post-rollback: ACTIVE/VERIFIED/{2e5cd514-...}, 1 evidence row, membership count 0.

REACHABILITY LENS (the lens I was told to apply) — it passes, it does not refute:
- Privilege: `select relacl from pg_class` gives `authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres` on BOTH emission_data and evidence_files, i.e. UPDATE and DELETE are granted to the end-user role.
- RLS: emission_data_update_own_org USING/WITH CHECK is only `entered_by_org_id in (select app.user_org_ids())` plus an evidence-ownership check on the claimed ids — no role predicate. The un-verify admin gate only fires for new.verification_status in ('VERIFIED','REJECTED'), so VERIFICATION_PENDING is ungated for a MEMBER.
- Transport: supabase/config.toml [api] enabled=true, schemas=["public"]. I confirmed the local REST API is live and exposes the table: `curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1/emission_data?select=id&limit=1` -> 200, and /rest/v1/ returns the "standard public schema" swagger. src/infrastructure/supabase/browser-client.ts hands a real user session JWT to the browser with the anon key, so every logged-in member holds the credential needed to issue these PATCH/DELETE calls directly. This is the project's own declared threat model ("two walls, always both"; 20260829310000's "directly callable ... by any authenticated client"), so absence of a UI affordance for DISCARDED->DRAFT does not refute it.

IMPACT AND FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CLAIMS ALSO CHECK OUT
- supabase/migrations/20260902140000_p13_review_shipment_line_determination_validator_v10.sql compares the frozen snapshot's evidence_file_ids against the live array with `if v_snapshot_evidence is distinct from v_real_evidence then return false`, so the swap silently invalidates the importer's frozen determination.
- No guard anywhere blocks ACTIVE -> DISCARDED (grepped every migration mentioning DISCARDED; 20260829230000:431 explicitly makes DISCARD the sanctioned path and adds no transition guard).
- The defect is in trigger logic created by migrations, not in any grant, so the seed.sql blanket-grant hazard is irrelevant and any db reset / CI run reproduces it identically.
- Regression gap is real: tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts covers only the same-statement variant (~line 622) and the direct ACTIVE->DRAFT walk-back (~line 665); grep for DISCARDED in that file hits only lines 916, 1248, 1268, none of which route the un-verify/evidence-strip chain through DISCARDED.

Severity stays BLOCKER: it fully defeats the invariant the release-hardening migration was written to establish, is reachable by an ordinary MEMBER with no elevated role, destroys the underlying evidence_files rows (not merely the array), leaves the row at ACTIVE+VERIFIED with the same id and version so nothing downstream signals a change, and writes no audit trail the damaged counterparty can see.

Independently re-verified every citation and re-ran both live reproductions; could not refute.

CODE. supabase/migrations/20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql: the status guard is exactly `if old.status = 'ACTIVE' and new.status = 'DRAFT'`; the un-verify guard `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED' and new.verification_status is distinct from old.verification_status`; the evidence-shrink guard `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED' and exists (... previous_id <> all (new...))`. LIVE, 127.0.0.1:54322, all inside real `begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims=...; ... rollback;`.
