TEST-GAP CLAIM CONFIRMED: `grep -n DISCARDED tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts` returns only 916, 1248, 1268 — the two "DISCARD still works" legitimate-flow assertions. Nothing routes DISCARDED -> DRAFT. The two P14/F11 v2 tests assert only the same-statement bypass and the direct ACTIVE -> DRAFT walk-back.

FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CLAIM CONFIRMED: the chain turns entirely on trigger predicates created by migrations, not on any grant, so the seed.sql blanket-grant hazard neither creates nor hides it; any db reset / CI run applying this migration set reproduces it identically.

SEVERITY: I keep BLOCKER. This fully reopens precisely the invariant the 20260903140000/150000 pair was written to close, and does so more destructively: the underlying evidence_files rows are deleted, the record returns to ACTIVE+VERIFIED under the same id and version carrying different evidence, no audit_events are written on the raw path, and the harmed party (the importer whose declaration froze that evidence set) has no read path to observe it.

CONFIRMED by my own independent re-check. I searched for a mitigation the finder missed and found none.

1. Code, as deployed. `supabase/migrations/20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql` lines 106-113 key the un-verify gate on `old.status = 'ACTIVE'`; lines 125-131 block only `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and new.status = 'DRAFT'`; lines 141-158 key the evidence-shrink gate on `old.status = 'ACTIVE' and old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED'`. I dumped the live function body (`select prosrc from pg_proc where proname='enforce_emission_data_verification_gate'`) and it is byte-identical to the file: no DISCARDED/SUPERSEDED -> DRAFT branch exists.

2. Mitigation search (the ALREADY-MITIGATED lens), all negative:
- Triggers on public.emission_data are exactly four (pg_trigger): prevent_fact_change, verification_gate, touch_updated_at, activation_gate. `app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change` deliberately permits status/verification_status/evidence_file_ids to change. `app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate` only constrains transitions INTO ACTIVE (`old.status='DRAFT' and new.verification_status='VERIFIED' and evidence non-empty`) — it does not constrain DISCARDED -> DRAFT, and its own conditions are satisfiable by the chain.
- RLS: `emission_data_update_own_org` USING/WITH CHECK requires only org membership plus that each claimed evidence id resolve to a real evidence_files row (which is why the chain inserts the replacement before swapping the array). No role gate, no status gate.
- `evidence_files_delete_own_org` (pg_policy, matching 20260829560000:37-45) is `org_id in user_org_ids AND exists(... ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED')` — un-verifying first genuinely unlocks the DELETE.
- Grants: pg_class.relacl shows `authenticated=arwdxtm` on both emission_data and evidence_files, so the path is PostgREST-reachable.
- Regression suite: tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts covers only the one-statement (status+verification in one UPDATE) and the direct ACTIVE->DRAFT cases; no test routes through DISCARDED. Gap is untested, as claimed.

3. Live reproduction (127.0.0.1:54322, role authenticated, jwt sub 36d33703-00e9-4b0f-8695-d1f73046b326 = OWNER of org 754c5a85-9ab9-4772-a6df-ecf8a4a1ea4c, target emission_data 2210a59a-a767-4c4b-ad96-61b94fd85398, pre-state ACTIVE/VERIFIED/{2e5cd514-21f4-4204-b663-515143c9d8bf}).
CONTROL — `update emission_data set evidence_file_ids='{}'` -> ERROR: "evidence cannot be removed from an ACTIVE, VERIFIED record" (gate in force).
CHAIN — step1 status='DISCARDED' UPDATE 1; step2 status='DRAFT' UPDATE 1; step3 verification_status='VERIFICATION_PENDING' UPDATE 1; step4 insert evidence_files 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 (sha bbbb…) INSERT 0 1; step5 evidence_file_ids=array['11111111-…'] UPDATE 1; step6 delete from evidence_files where id='2e5cd514-…' DELETE 1; step7 verification_status='VERIFIED' UPDATE 1; step8 status='ACTIVE' UPDATE 1.
In-transaction result: `2210a59a-… | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | {11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111} | version 1`, and the only evidence_files row for it is 11111111-… (storage_path .../swapped-evidence.pdf, sha bbbb…). Same id, same version, different evidence, original evidence row destroyed.
PLAIN-MEMBER variant (membership row for a4ef3f67-c353-4d71-9285-22a4ab5af0b9 role MEMBER inserted inside the same rolled-back tx): status='DISCARDED' UPDATE 1; verification_status='VERIFICATION_PENDING' UPDATE 1 (not admin-gated, because the admin check only fires for new.verification_status in ('VERIFIED','REJECTED')); delete evidence row DELETE 1; evidence_file_ids='{}' UPDATE 1 -> DISCARDED / VERIFICATION_PENDING / {} with 0 evidence rows. No ADMIN/OWNER needed to destroy the evidence.
POST-ROLLBACK for both runs: record back to ACTIVE / VERIFIED / {2e5cd514-…}, evidence row 2e5cd514-… present, stray row 11111111-… count 0, injected membership count 0. Nothing committed.

4. Impact claim verified: supabase/migrations/20260902140000…:193-208 compares the frozen snapshot's evidence_file_ids array against `unnest(v_ed.evidence_file_ids)` and returns false on any difference, so the importer's frozen determination silently stops validating after the swap while the record still reads ACTIVE+VERIFIED to them.

5. Fresh-environment claim verified: the exploit rides on trigger logic only, not on the seed.sql blanket grant, so `supabase db reset` / CI reproduces it identically. The grants it needs (UPDATE on emission_data, DELETE on evidence_files for authenticated) are the intended ones — matching DELETE/UPDATE RLS policies exist for `authenticated`.

Severity: BLOCKER stands. It is strictly worse than the defect 20260903150000 was written to close (that one only emptied an array; this destroys the underlying evidence_files rows behind an ACTIVE+VERIFIED record and restores it under the same id and version), and the repo itself treated that sibling defect as a P14 release blocker.

title: The evidence storage.objects DELETE policy carries no verification gate, so the actual evidence document can be deleted from behind an intact, locked, VERIFIED record
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260829410000_p11_review_evidence_storage_path_and_uuid_cast_hardening.sql:136-142 --
  create policy evidence_storage_delete_own_org on storage.objects for delete to authenticated
    using (bucket_id = 'evidence' and app.try_cast_uuid((storage.foldername(name))[1]) in (select app.user_org_ids()));
The predicate is org membership and nothing else. Contrast supabase/migrations/20260829560000_p13_review_evidence_files_verified_delete_lock.sql:43, which added `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'` to the *metadata row* delete policy for exactly this reason ("Deleting evidence out from under a VERIFIED record silently invalidates the verifier's own basis for approving it, for a record that may already be consumed cross-org via an active sharing grant"). No corresponding condition was ever added to the storage side; grep of every storage-touching migration (20260829240000, 20260829410000, 20260829490000, 20260829510000) shows the three storage.objects policies were never revisited after 20260829410000.
exploit: PARTIALLY EVIDENCED -- policy text only. Any member of the producing org calls supabase.storage.from('evidence').remove(['<their-org-id>/<emission-data-id>/<file>.pdf']) against a VERIFIED, ACTIVE record. The evidence_files row survives (locked by 20260829560000), emission_data.evidence_file_ids is unchanged, and the v10 determination validator therefore still returns true -- the importer's determination keeps validating while the document it attests to no longer exists.
impact: The single control the whole evidence model rests on -- that a verified figure has a retrievable supporting document -- is bypassable without touching Postgres. Unlike finding 1 this leaves no visible trace at all in the database: every DB-level check still passes. For a CBAM declaration under audit, the cited evidence simply 404s. Bounded to the owning org's own objects (the path-prefix check is sound), so not cross-tenant read; the harm is to the importer relying on it and to the regulator.
freshEnvironment: Almost certainly yes, but I could NOT test it. Storage is disabled in the committed supabase/config.toml ([storage] enabled = false, with a long comment recording three failed re-enable attempts), and this local instance has zero tables in the storage schema -- I confirmed directly: `select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='storage'` returns 0, and `insert into storage.buckets (...)` inside a rolled-back transaction returns ERROR: relation "storage.buckets" does not exist. So the HTTP Storage layer was not exercised and I am reasoning from the policy SQL alone. CI does enable storage and asserts the bucket exists (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines ~274, ~341), so these policies do apply for real there and in the hosted project; nothing in CI attacks this particular case (the P14 audit's §C.2 storage probes cover cross-org read/delete, not same-org delete behind a VERIFIED record).

verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed independently, not taken on trust.

POLICY TEXT (re-read, verbatim): supabase/migrations/20260829410000_p11_review_evidence_storage_path_and_uuid_cast_hardening.sql:134-142 -- `create policy evidence_storage_delete_own_org on storage.objects for delete to authenticated using (bucket_id = 'evidence' and app.try_cast_uuid((storage.foldername(name))[1]) in (select app.user_org_ids()));`. Org membership is the entire predicate. Contrast confirmed at 20260829560000_p13_review_evidence_files_verified_delete_lock.sql:37-45 (`and exists (select 1 from public.emission_data ed where ed.id = evidence_files.emission_data_id and ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED')`) and 20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql:139-156 (blocks shrinking evidence_file_ids on ACTIVE+VERIFIED). Both metadata layers gated; the storage-object layer never was.

NO OTHER GATE: `grep -rn "restrictive" supabase/migrations/` returns zero matches, so every policy is permissive and nothing can subtract from the DELETE grant. Only two migrations ever define storage.objects policies (20260829240000 Part 5, 20260829410000); no triggers, no additional predicate.

REACHABILITY (the lens I was asked to apply -- I expected to refute here and could not): the exploit requires (a) role `authenticated` to hold DELETE on storage.objects and (b) a route bypassing the app. Both hold. app/(producer)/emission-data/actions.ts:548-559 calls removeEvidenceFile(setup.supabase, ...) where setup.supabase is the USER-SESSION client from src/infrastructure/supabase/server-client (anon key + user JWT => role authenticated), and that function does .storage.from('evidence').remove(...). The app's own ordinary removal therefore proves `authenticated` can DELETE these objects in a real deployment; the identical DELETE is issuable straight to /storage/v1/object/evidence/<org_id>/<emission_data_id>/<file>. The anon key is public by design (src/infrastructure/supabase/browser-client.ts:16-19: "inlined into the client bundle by Next.js at build time, safe for browser exposure"). The direct-Storage-API-with-public-anon-key path is this repo's OWN accepted threat path, not my invention: 20260829510000_p13_review_evidence_bucket_size_mime_limits.sql:11-22 exists solely to close that same bypass on the INSERT side, and docs/plans/P13_RELEASE_READINESS_REPORT.md:594 records the analogous anon-key bypass of the sign-in rate limiter. The path string is org-readable (storage_path is in EVIDENCE_FILES_COLUMNS, src/application/evidence/evidence-mapper.ts:25). The PRODUCER_OPERATOR capability check (src/application/evidence/upload-evidence.ts:494) and the fail-closed VERIFIED guard (upload-evidence.ts:525-546) are Wall 1 only and are simply not on the direct-Storage path -- so this control has one wall where the codebase's stated posture is "two walls, always both" (20260829560000's own header).

NO COVERAGE: `grep -rn "evidence_storage_delete\|remove(\[" tests/ src/ app/ scripts/ docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md` returns nothing. docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1475 states `| Storage, storage path probing | **not re-attacked** -- local Storage returns 503 |`.

WHAT I COULD NOT DO (same limit the finder declared): I re-ran their check -- `PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 54322 -U postgres -d postgres -tAc "select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='storage'"` returns `0`, and supabase/config.toml:169-170 ships `[storage] enabled = false`. There is no HTTP Storage layer locally to fire the DELETE at, so the final step is inferred rather than executed. The inference is tight (the app's own remove path establishes the privilege) rather than speculative, and CI does enable storage and asserts the bucket exists (.github/workflows/ci.yml:274, 341), so the policies are in force there and in the hosted project. Confidence "likely" rather than "certain" reflects only that unexecuted HTTP step.

SEVERITY: HIGH sustained. The exactly-analogous metadata-row gap was treated as a P13 release blocker (finding S6) and the evidence_file_ids variant got its own P14 migration; this is the third face of the same control and is the only one still open. Bounded to the owning org's own objects (the path-prefix check is sound, so no cross-tenant exposure), and the evidence_files row plus its sha256 survive -- so the deletion is detectable on the next download attempt, though the document itself is unrecoverable.

I re-ran every piece of the finding's evidence rather than trusting it, and it survives.

1. The quoted policy is verbatim correct at the exact cited lines. `awk 'NR>=134&&NR<=143'` on supabase/migrations/20260829410000_p11_review_evidence_storage_path_and_uuid_cast_hardening.sql returns:
136: create policy evidence_storage_delete_own_org
137:     on storage.objects
138:     for delete
139:     to authenticated
140:     using (
141:         bucket_id = 'evidence'
142:         and app.try_cast_uuid((storage.foldername(name))[1]) in (select app.user_org_ids())
143:     );
The USING predicate is bucket + org membership and nothing else. No verification_status term, no emission_data lookup.

2. The contrast is also verbatim correct. supabase/migrations/20260829560000_p13_review_evidence_files_verified_delete_lock.sql:33-45 shows the *metadata row* policy carries `and exists (select 1 from public.emission_data ed where ed.id = evidence_files.emission_data_id and ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED')` — line 43 is exactly the cited conjunct. Its header comment gives exactly the rationale the finding quotes.

3. The "never revisited" claim checks out. `grep -rn "storage.objects|storage.buckets|evidence_storage" supabase/ --include=*.sql` returns storage.objects policy DDL only in 20260829240000 (original three) and 20260829410000 (drop+recreate of the same three). 20260829490000 mentions storage.objects only in a comment; 20260829510000 touches `storage.buckets` (size/MIME limits) only. The newest evidence migration, 20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql, closes the `evidence_file_ids` array hole on public.emission_data and does not touch storage at all. So exactly three permissive policies exist on storage.objects (select/insert/delete) and there is no UPDATE policy; nothing adds a gate and nothing restrictive overlays it.

4. Decisive corroboration from the codebase itself. src/application/evidence/upload-evidence.ts:582-585, in a comment written during the P13 final round, states outright:
  "Without this the function returned OK for a row it never deleted -- and because the storage delete above has no verification clause in its own policy, the object was already gone by then."
The implementation confirms the gap in its own words. removeEvidenceFile does reject with `EMISSION_DATA_VERIFIED` at line 554-558 (Wall 1), and the storage `.remove()` at 561-566 runs before the metadata delete — so on this path only the application guard stands between a VERIFIED record and its object being deleted. That is Wall 1 without Wall 2, against this codebase's own stated "two walls, always both" rule (20260829560000 header). A member calling the Storage API directly with their own session skips Wall 1 entirely; the path shape the exploit needs is confirmed at upload-evidence.ts:306-307, `${orgId}/${input.emissionDataId}/${randomUUID()}${extension}`, whose first segment is the caller's own org id and therefore satisfies the policy.

5. The finding's own caveat about testability is honest and I reproduced it. PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 54322 -tAc "select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='storage'" -> 0, and "select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname='storage'" -> 0, while all five evidence migrations (20260829240000, 410000, 490000, 510000, 560000) appear in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations. So locally the migrations are recorded applied but the storage objects never existed (config.toml [storage] enabled = false, plus `migration repair` per .github/workflows/ci.yml:253-274). I therefore could not execute an HTTP delete, exactly as the finding said. CI does enable storage and hard-fails if the evidence bucket is absent (ci.yml:332-343), so the policies are genuinely in force there and in the hosted project.

Two calibrations, neither refuting: (a) "leaves no visible trace at all in the database" is slightly overstated — the evidence_files row and emission_data.evidence_file_ids survive, leaving a storage_path that no longer resolves, i.e. a detectable-by-reconciliation dangling pointer (though no evidence.removed audit event is written, so there is no audit trail); (b) the exploit is bounded to an authenticated member of the owning org, so it is insider integrity/audit harm, not cross-tenant — which the finding already states. Severity HIGH stands: it is the same defect class the project itself treated as a release blocker for the metadata row (finding S6), left open on the object the row points at.

I tried to refute this under the ALREADY-MITIGATED lens and failed; every mitigation candidate I checked is absent.

1. Policy text re-read directly, not taken on trust. `sed -n 134,143p supabase/migrations/20260829410000_p11_review_evidence_storage_path_and_uuid_cast_hardening.sql` (file lines 134-143):
   drop policy evidence_storage_delete_own_org on storage.objects;
   create policy evidence_storage_delete_own_org on storage.objects for delete to authenticated
     using (bucket_id = 'evidence' and app.try_cast_uuid((storage.foldername(name))[1]) in (select app.user_org_ids()));
   Two conjuncts, neither referencing emission_data or verification_status. `grep -n verification_status` on that migration returns nothing (exit 1).

2. No later migration revisits it. `grep -rn "storage.objects" supabase/migrations/` and `grep -rln "storage" supabase/migrations/` both show the last storage.objects DDL is 20260829410000; 20260829490000 and 20260829510000 mention storage only in comments/bucket limits, and 20260903150000_p14_emission_data_evidence_integrity_v2.sql does not match the "storage" grep at all. `grep -rn "revoke" supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -i storage` returns nothing (exit 1), and supabase/seed.sql contains no storage references — so there is no grant-level mitigation either (Supabase's own bootstrap grants ALL on storage.objects to authenticated).

3. The asymmetry with the metadata side is real and live in the local DB. `psql ... "\d public.evidence_files"` shows the DELETE policy now carries `AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM emission_data ed WHERE ed.id = evidence_files.emission_data_id AND ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED')` — i.e. 20260829560000 is in force for the metadata row while the storage object is left ungated.

4. No FK or trigger mitigates it: `\d public.evidence_files` shows FKs only to organizations, emission_data and auth.users — nothing referencing storage.objects, so deleting the object cannot cascade or be RESTRICTed.

5. No role gate narrows the actor. `pg_get_functiondef` for app.user_org_ids(): `select org_id from public.memberships where user_id = auth.uid() and deactivated_at is null` — any active member of the producing org, of any role, satisfies the storage delete policy. The application-layer guard is stricter (removeEvidenceFile requires PRODUCER_OPERATOR and rejects with EMISSION_DATA_VERIFIED, src/application/evidence/upload-evidence.ts:489-560), but that is Wall 1 only and a direct Storage API call bypasses it.

6. Decisive corroboration from the implementer's own code, which the finder did not cite: src/application/evidence/upload-evidence.ts:583 — "and because the storage delete above has no verification clause in its own policy, the object was already gone by then." The codebase already knows the storage delete is ungated; it only ever fixed the ordering consequence, never the policy.

7. Downstream checks cannot detect it: src/domain/emissions/snapshot-completeness.ts's checkEmissionDataEvidenceCompleteness tests only `record.evidence_file_ids.length === 0`, and determine-from-actual-data.ts:333-341 re-derives from that array — neither looks at storage, so the determination keeps validating.

8. Fresh-environment/coverage: I reproduced the finder's constraint — `select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='storage'` returns 0 locally (schema exists, tables do not; config.toml [storage] enabled = false), so I likewise could not exercise the HTTP Storage layer. But .github/workflows/ci.yml:274-276 rewrites [storage] to enabled = true and lines 332-343 hard-fail unless GET /storage/v1/bucket is healthy and `select count(*) from storage.buckets where id='evidence'` = 1 — so the policies do apply in CI and in any freshly built/hosted environment. docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1475 records "Storage, storage path probing | not re-attacked", and tests/ contains no storage.objects reference at all, so nothing in the suite covers same-org delete behind a VERIFIED record.

Residual uncertainty (why "likely", not "certain"): the policy gap itself is certain, but the end-to-end exploit depends on two links I could not execute here — that authenticated retains DELETE on storage.objects in the hosted project (Supabase default; no revoke in this repo) and that storage-api enforces RLS as the caller's role on delete (it does, by design). Severity: I keep HIGH rather than lowering it, because the identical harm on the metadata side (20260829560000, finding S6) was treated as a P13 release blocker; I do note the finder overstates "no visible trace" — the evidence_files row, its storage_path and sha256 survive, so a storage-vs-DB diff would reveal the dangling reference, though nothing in the product performs one.

title: seed.sql's blanket function grant re-grants EXECUTE to anon on every public RPC the migrations deliberately revoked; harmless today only because each function guards itself
evidence: supabase/seed.sql:23 `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` and :32 the matching alter-default-privileges. Its re-asserted revokes (lines 86-110) cover only calculation_results and TRUNCATE. Live pg_proc.proacl consequently shows anon=X/postgres on accept_sharing_grant_invitation, accept_organization_invitation, create_organization_with_owner, list_org_members, record_declaration_filed, record_shared_data_consumption and sharing_counterparty_org_names -- none of which any migration granted to anon (e.g. 20260902150000:194-196 grants only authenticated and service_role). Probed as `set local role anon`: sharing_counterparty_org_names() 0 rows; organizations/sharing_grants/evidence_files 0 rows each; list_org_members('754c5a85-...') raised 'Not a member of this organization.'
exploit: NONE reachable. Every affected function either raises on `auth.uid() is null` or routes through app.user_org_ids(), which returns nothing for anon.
impact: No present harm. It is reported because it is the identical undone-revoke pattern that produced the §19 failure, still live in the same file, and the file's own header claims the coupling is 'covered by tests that already caught it once' -- that coverage exists for calculation_results only. Any future public RPC that relies on its migration-time grant list rather than an internal auth check will be anon-callable on every freshly built environment, with nothing to catch it.
freshEnvironment: Yes, and it is specifically a fresh-environment property: seed.sql runs last on `supabase db reset` and is run explicitly as the last step in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml ~line 315), so every rebuilt database has these anon grants. I confirmed the resulting ACLs live and confirmed the migrations' own grant statements by grepping `grant execute on function public.` across supabase/migrations/.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's ACL facts are accurate, but it describes no reachable defect, and its own claimed exploit is "NONE". Under the reachability lens it does not survive.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (so the refutation is not a hand-wave):
- supabase/seed.sql:23 `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` and :31-32 the default-privileges equivalent. Its re-asserted revokes (lines 83-110) cover only calculation_results / record_calculation_result / TRUNCATE.
- The migrations genuinely close PUBLIC, so my first refutation angle (Postgres' default EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC would give anon access anyway) FAILS: e.g. 20260828080000:107-108, 20260828120000:77-78, 20260829380000:348-349, 20260829390000:282-283, 20260829310000:331-332, 20260829330000:1030-1031, 20260902150000:194-196 each pair `revoke all ... from public` with `grant execute ... to authenticated`.
- Live proacl (psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 54322): all seven show an explicit `anon=X/postgres`; record_calculation_result correctly shows only `postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`.

WHY IT IS STILL NOT A DEFECT — I re-ran the probes myself, each inside a real `begin; set local role anon; set local request.jwt.claims='{"role":"anon"}'; <call>; rollback;`:
  accept_organization_invitation('954e2869-...') -> ERROR: "accept_organization_invitation requires an authenticated caller." (line 8 RAISE)
  accept_sharing_grant_invitation('0e33f489-...','1b635dfb-...') -> ERROR: "...requires an authenticated caller" (line 7 RAISE)
  record_declaration_filed('c5c352c3-...','FORGED-REF') -> ERROR: "record_declaration_filed requires an authenticated caller." (line 12 RAISE) — this one has no guard in the 20260829330000 body I first read, but the terminal definition at 20260903110000_p14_filing_requires_calculation_quantity_to_match_line.sql:87-91 adds it
  record_shared_data_consumption(...) -> ERROR: "...requires an authenticated caller." (line 7 RAISE)
  list_org_members('1b635dfb-...') -> ERROR: "Not a member of this organization." (line 17 RAISE)
  create_organization_with_owner('anon-forge','anon-forge-slug','{DECLARANT}') -> ERROR: "...requires an authenticated caller." (line 6 RAISE)
  sharing_counterparty_org_names() -> 0 rows
Post-state verification (separate read-only query, after the probes): `anon-forge orgs|0`, `inv status|ACCEPTED` (unchanged), `decl status|DRAFT` (unchanged), `grant status|ACTIVE` (unchanged). Nothing was written.

THREE FURTHER REACHABILITY REBUTTALS:
1. The anon role confers nothing an attacker could not already have. supabase/config.toml:251 `enable_signup = true` — anyone holding the public anon key can self-register into `authenticated` in one step. Every one of these seven functions then still refuses a non-member (via auth.uid()/app.user_org_ids()/memberships), so the anon grant crosses no boundary that signing up does not already cross legitimately.
2. Blast radius is local/CI, not the deployed product. `grep -rn "seed.sql"` outside node_modules returns only .github/workflows/ci.yml:315, docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:556-566, docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md, one doc citation and one test comment. The file's own header (seed.sql:2-4) states the CLI applies it exclusively to a local instance. The one non-local path is DEPLOYMENT.md's "Rebuilding on a fresh database" step 4 — and even there the outcome is the same anon-can-execute-but-gets-refused posture probed above. (I did not query production; the conclusion does not depend on it, since no path yields harm in either case.)
3. The finding's "with nothing to catch it" is wrong as stated. scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:168-180 has a `function_grants` check, `critical: true`, whose SQL emits `array_to_string(p.proacl::text[], ' ')` for every function in `public` and `app` — an anon EXECUTE grant appearing on any public RPC is exactly what that diff surfaces. (Fair caveat: that is a two-database diff check, so DEPLOYMENT.md step 6's single-DSN `--check` run would not exercise it; the coverage exists but is not wired into the fresh-rebuild recipe.)

RESIDUE: what actually remains is a hypothetical about code that does not exist — "any FUTURE public RPC that relies on its migration-time grant list rather than an internal auth check." Every RPC in this release candidate carries the internal check. A conditional about unwritten code has no failure scenario in this commit and is a hygiene note for seed.sql's header, not a finding against the release.

I re-ran every piece of evidence independently; all of it holds.

1. FILE QUOTES ARE EXACT. supabase/seed.sql:23 is `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` and :31-32 is `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role;`. The re-asserted revokes are the `do $$ ... $$` block at :83-101 (calculation_results INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and record_calculation_result EXECUTE only) plus :104-110 (TRUNCATE only). Nothing else is re-revoked. The header's coverage claim is at :68-76 and names exactly one test, tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts case (4).

2. LIVE ACLs CONFIRMED. `select p.proname, array_to_string(p.proacl,' | ') from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='public'` returns anon=X/postgres on accept_organization_invitation, accept_sharing_grant_invitation, create_organization_with_owner, list_org_members, record_declaration_filed, record_shared_data_consumption and sharing_counterparty_org_names. Only record_calculation_result is clean (`postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`) -- i.e. exactly the one function the seed re-revokes.

3. NO MIGRATION GRANTS anon. `grep -rn "grant execute" supabase/migrations/` shows every public RPC uses the pattern `revoke all on function public.X from public;` then `grant execute ... to authenticated` (+ service_role). 20260902150000:194-196 is verbatim as cited. No `to anon` anywhere.

4. CAUSATION PROVED, not assumed. I created a throwaway db (`create database probe_acl_tmp`), which had zero pg_default_acl rows, and replayed the migrations' own pattern: `create function public.probe_fn()...; revoke all on function public.probe_fn() from public; grant execute ... to authenticated; grant execute ... to service_role;`. Resulting proacl: `postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres` -- no anon. So the anon entry in the real database can only come from seed.sql:23. Dropped the throwaway db afterwards.

5. FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CLAIM CONFIRMED. .github/workflows/ci.yml:315 runs `psql ... -f supabase/seed.sql` explicitly as a post-migration step, and seed.sql:1-4 documents that the CLI runs it last on `db reset`/`start`.

6. HARMLESSNESS CLAIM CONFIRMED (I tried to break it). All eight public functions are prosecdef=t with `search_path=public`. Probed inside `begin; set local role anon; ... rollback;`: `select * from public.create_organization_with_owner('X','x-anon-probe',array['IMPORTER'])` returned `ERROR: create_organization_with_owner requires an authenticated caller.` -- note this is the function's own `if auth.uid() is null` guard (pg_get_functiondef line 6), NOT `permission denied for function`, which is itself independent proof the anon EXECUTE grant is live and reachable. `sharing_counterparty_org_names()` returned 0 rows; `organizations`, `sharing_grants`, `calculation_results` returned 0 rows each. No exploit.

7. THE "NOTHING TO CATCH IT" CLAIM IS ALSO TRUE. `grep -rn "proacl|has_function_privilege|has_table_privilege" tests/` returns nothing. No test anywhere asserts anon's EXECUTE on any public RPC; the only anon assertions are in regulatory-authenticated-read.test.ts (regulatory table reads) and calculation-reproduction.test.ts (calculation_results writes).

ONE PRECISION CAVEAT, not a refutation: the title says the seed re-grants what "the migrations deliberately revoked", but the migrations revoke from PUBLIC, never from anon, and revoking from PUBLIC would not strip an explicit anon grant. On hosted Supabase the platform's own provisioning-time `alter default privileges ... grant all on functions to anon,...` plausibly produces the same anon=X there, so seed.sql may be faithfully replicating hosted state rather than diverging from it. I did not query production to check (production writes forbidden, and a read was not necessary to settle the local/CI facts). This affects the framing only -- every factual and causal claim about the repo and the local/CI database is correct.

INFO is the right severity: verified real, verified currently unexploitable, and correctly reported as a latent instance of the same undone-revoke pattern that produced the section 19 failure.

I tried to refute this on three fronts (mis-stated ACLs, migrations that never revoked from anon in the first place, and an existing mitigation the finder missed) and all three failed. Everything checks out.

1) The file text is as claimed. D:\projects\snowkap-cbam\supabase\seed.sql:23 `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` and :31-32 `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role;`. Its re-asserted revokes (:83-110) cover only `record_calculation_result` (by exact 11-arg signature), `calculation_results` INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and TRUNCATE. Nothing else.

2) Live local ACLs match the finding exactly. `select p.proname, array_to_string(p.proacl,' | ') from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='public'` returns anon=X/postgres on accept_organization_invitation, accept_sharing_grant_invitation, create_organization_with_owner, list_org_members, record_declaration_filed, record_shared_data_consumption, sharing_counterparty_org_names; and `record_calculation_result | postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres` (correctly excluded). `has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE')` = t for all seven, f for record_calculation_result.

3) My first refutation attempt was that Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default, so the migrations never revoked anything from anon. That is wrong here: every one of these migrations does `revoke all on function ... from public` before granting, e.g. supabase/migrations/20260828120000_list_org_members_rpc.sql:77-78, 20260829330000_p9_declarations_schema.sql:1030-1031, 20260902150000...:194-196 (authenticated + service_role only). No migration names anon anywhere.

4) I proved causality rather than inferring it, in a throwaway database (created and dropped): `create database refute_probe_tmp`, then as postgres: create f_probe(); `revoke all on function public.f_probe() from public`; `grant execute ... to authenticated`. Output: `AFTER-MIGRATION acl: postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres` / `anon has execute: false`. Then the seed's own line: `grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` → `AFTER-SEED acl: ... | anon=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres` / `anon has execute: true`. So the blanket grant, not the platform default, is what puts anon on the ACL. `drop database refute_probe_tmp` confirmed DROP DATABASE.

5) Fresh-environment claim confirmed independently: .github/workflows/ci.yml:315 runs `psql ... -f supabase/seed.sql` as the final step after `supabase migration up --local` (comment at :307-314 says so explicitly). Every CI-built and every `db reset` database carries these anon grants.

6) No exploit, as the finding says. Function bodies from pg_proc.prosrc: record_declaration_filed, record_shared_data_consumption, accept_sharing_grant_invitation, accept_organization_invitation and create_organization_with_owner each open with `if auth.uid() is null then raise exception ...`; list_org_members raises 'Not a member of this organization.' off app.user_org_ids(); sharing_counterparty_org_names filters on app.user_org_ids(). Live probe: `begin; set local role anon; select * from public.record_declaration_filed('00000000-...-0001','X'); rollback;` → `ERROR: record_declaration_filed requires an authenticated caller.` (the guard, not permission denied — which itself proves anon holds EXECUTE). INFO is the right severity.

7) ALREADY-MITIGATED lens, searched and came up empty. No test asserts an anon EXECUTE boundary: `grep -rln "proacl|has_function_privilege|has_table_privilege|information_schema.role_" tests/ scripts/` matches only scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs. That script's `function_grants` check (lines ~163-176) is a source-vs-target diff, not an absolute assertion — it cannot fail on a single fresh database — and its SELF_CHECKS list (lines ~248-430) covers auth helpers, RLS, INSERT policies, api_roles_hold_their_grants and truncate_granted_to_api_roles, with nothing about function EXECUTE for anon. tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts's "P14.1 write boundary" block (lines ~735-830) is scoped to calculation_results/record_calculation_result only, exactly as the finding states, so seed.sql's header claim that the coupling "is covered by tests that already caught it once" is true only for that one table.

One caveat, marked as such: I did not query production, so whether the hosted project shows the same anon=X (via hosted default privileges for role postgres) is unverified. If it does, the "fresh-environment-specific" framing is weaker than stated — but the seed-level causality in (4) and the CI ordering in (5) hold regardless, and neither affects the INFO severity.

title: record_declaration_filed never checks that member shipments belong to the declaration's reporting period -- a filed snapshot can be stamped ANNUAL 2029 while containing only a 2035 shipment
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260903110000_p14_filing_requires_calculation_quantity_to_match_line.sql -- whole body read. The only membership test is:

    select count(*) into v_lockable_count
    from public.shipments s
    where s.id = any(v_member_ids)
      and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id
      and s.status in ('READY', 'LOCKED');

There is no comparison anywhere in the function between s.reporting_period_kind/_year/_quarter and v_decl.reporting_period_kind/_year/_quarter. Those column names appear in the body only inside jsonb_build_object, i.e. only to STAMP the period onto filed_snapshot, never to verify it. Live body confirmed to be this version: `select prosrc from pg_proc ... where proname='record_declaration_filed'` contains 'quantity_unit is distinct from' (1 match).

LIVE (begin;...rollback;, state re-read after rollback): a 2035 shipment + line + calculation (999 tCO2e) and a DRAFT ANNUAL-2029 declaration; then as role authenticated with jwt sub = an OWNER of the org:
  update public.declarations set member_shipment_ids = array['aaaaaaaa-1111-1111-1111-111111111111']::uuid[], completeness_report = '{"blockers":[],"forged":true}'::jsonb, status = 'READY' where id='44444444-...';  -> UPDATE 1
  select * from public.record_declaration_filed('44444444-...','REF-CROSS-PERIOD');
    result_status | result_declaration_id
    OK            | 44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444
Resulting filed row:
    period_claimed     | {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2029, "quarter": null}
    total              | 999
    ship_ref           | ADV-D-2035
    ship_actual_period | 2035
exploit: Any ADMIN/OWNER of an importer org using only the public anon key against PostgREST: PATCH /rest/v1/declarations?id=eq.<draft> with {"member_shipment_ids":[<any own-org shipment ids>],"completeness_report":{...},"status":"READY"} -- the freeze trigger only fires when old.status <> 'DRAFT', and declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing permits DRAFT->READY with arbitrary column values -- then POST /rest/v1/rpc/record_declaration_filed. A second path needs no raw member-set edit at all: a plain MEMBER moves a READY member shipment into another period between markDeclarationReady and filing (see the companion finding), and the gate still freezes it.
impact: filed_snapshot is the archived, immutable, legally meaningful artifact the product exists to produce, and it can attribute a reporting period's emissions to goods released in an entirely different period, with a fully consistent audit trail (declaration.filed, provenance.calculation_result_ids, shipment.locked) and nothing in the payload a later reader could use to detect it. Bounded to the acting organization's own data -- RLS pins every id and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id is enforced -- so this is not cross-tenant. It is a self-inflicted misstatement of the declarant's own CBAM record, and it is the same class of gap (a wall that checks the number but not what the number is a number OF) that 20260903110000 itself was written to close for quantity.
freshEnvironment: Yes. This is a missing clause in the SQL body installed by 20260903110000, which grep across supabase/migrations/*.sql confirms is the last create-or-replace of record_declaration_filed. No grant, seed, default-privilege or ordering effect is involved, so db reset, a restore and a hosted push all reproduce it identically. I also confirmed the live body is the 20260903110000 one, so the probe measured release-candidate code, not an older definition.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-verified independently on a database I built myself (throwaway `advrev_period_o5`, all supabase/migrations applied in order + supabase/seed.sql; the shared local `postgres` DB was found with an empty public schema, 0 tables, so it could not be used). CODE: supabase/migrations/20260903110000_p14_filing_requires_calculation_quantity_to_match_line.sql is the last create-or-replace of record_declaration_filed; its only membership test is `where s.id = any(v_member_ids) and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id and s.status in ('READY','LOCKED')`. In the INSTALLED body (`select prosrc from pg_proc ... proname='record_declaration_filed'`), the string `reporting_period` occurs at exactly 6 lines (prosrc 326-329 and 506-508), all inside jsonb_build_object — stamping only, never comparing. No trigger on public.shipments freezes reporting_period_* (pg_trigger on shipment_lines/shipments shows only prevent_org_id_change and prevent_shipment_line_reparent); shipments_update_own_org_not_terminal (20260828150000:253, re-created 20260829090000:144) lets ANY org member update a non-LOCKED/VOID shipment. src/domain/declarations/completeness.ts:71 buildCompletenessReport receives shipments already filtered by period (src/application/declarations/compute-declaration-draft-facts.ts:104-134) and never re-checks period; src/application/declarations/record-declaration-filed.ts only calls supabase.rpc (line 158) with no re-derivation. No test or migration anywhere enforces period membership (grep for OUT_OF_PERIOD / NOT_IN_PERIOD: no hits). PATH 1 REPRODUCED (begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims sub=OWNER; ... rollback;): `update public.declarations set member_shipment_ids=array['aaaaaaaa-1111-...'], completeness_report='{"complete":true,"blockers":[],"forged":true}', status='READY' where id='44444444-...'` -> UPDATE 1; `select * from public.record_declaration_filed('44444444-...','REF-CROSS-PERIOD')` -> OK | 44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444; filed row: period_claimed {"kind":"ANNUAL","year":2029,"quarter":null}, total 999, ship_ref ADV-D-2035, shipment row reporting_period_year 2035 status LOCKED. After ROLLBACK re-read: DRAFT | {} | snap_null t (clean). PATH 2 REPRODUCED (the one that carries the severity, no member-set forgery): OWNER sets member_shipment_ids to the LEGITIMATE in-period 2029 shipment and status READY; then a PLAIN MEMBER (same tx, `select app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of('2222...')` -> f) runs `update public.shipments set release_date='2035-07-01', reporting_period_year=2035 where id='aaaaaaaa-2222-...'` -> UPDATE 1; then the OWNER's ordinary `record_declaration_filed('44444444-...','REF-DRIFT')` -> OK, filed_snapshot period_claimed {"kind":"ANNUAL","year":2029}, ship_ref ADV-D-2029 whose row now says 2035. After ROLLBACK: declaration DRAFT/{}, shipment 2029/READY (clean). Both probes ran as role `authenticated` with only a jwt claim, so the post-seed grants make this PostgREST-reachable with the public anon key; no grant/ordering/seed artifact is involved, so a fresh `db reset`, a restore and a hosted push all reproduce it. TRIMS TO THE FINDING: (a) "nothing a later reader could use to detect it" is overstated — filed_snapshot.member_shipment_ids plus the now-LOCKED (hence immutable) shipments.reporting_period_* columns make the mismatch discoverable by a join; (b) path 1 alone is weak, since an admin who wants a wrong 2029 total can simply insert a shipment already stamped 2029 (shipments_insert_own_org pins only org_id), so it adds little capability. Path 2 is the real gap: a non-admin member, via raw PostgREST, silently causes an honest admin's filed, immutable CBAM record to attribute one period's emissions to goods recorded as released in another — the same class (a wall that checks the number but not what the number is a number OF) that 20260903110000 was written to close for quantity, and reachable by a strictly lower-privileged actor than that one was.

CONFIRMED — I could not refute it on any of the three axes I attacked (wrong code quote, a period check living elsewhere, or an environment-specific probe).

1) STATIC: the quote is accurate. supabase/migrations/20260903110000_p14_filing_requires_calculation_quantity_to_match_line.sql:186-195 is exactly the membership test the finding quotes (org_id + status only). `grep -n "reporting_period" ` on that file returns ONLY lines 403-406 and 583-585, all inside jsonb_build_object — stamping, never comparing. I also grepped reporting_period across all 74 files in supabase/migrations/: the only period-to-period comparisons anywhere are declaration-vs-prior-declaration amendment lineage (20260829330000:511-514, 20260829340000:111-114). No migration compares a shipment's period to a declaration's. `grep -rn "member_shipment_ids" supabase/migrations/*.sql` shows no validating trigger or CHECK on that array's contents.

2) The gap is documented as deliberate, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding: 20260829330000:583-588 states "Two things are deliberately NOT re-derived in SQL and stay the application layer's job ... (a) which shipments belong to the period at all". The TypeScript gate is bypassable by a bare PostgREST client, which is the finding's whole point.

3) LIVE — and note the main local `postgres` DB currently has ZERO public tables (another agent's cleanup), so the finding could NOT have been measured against a stale/lucky database. I built my own from scratch: created `advrev_xperiod_k9`, stubbed auth/storage, applied all 74 migrations in order, then applied supabase/seed.sql for the base-table grants. Verified the installed function is the release-candidate one: `select l from pg_proc, lateral unnest(string_to_array(prosrc,E'\n')) l where proname='record_declaration_filed' and l ilike '%reporting_period%'` returned only the eight jsonb_build_object lines — no comparison in the live body.

PATH A (finding's path, ADMIN/OWNER, inside begin;...rollback;): 2035 shipment + line + calculation('999') + DRAFT ANNUAL-2029 declaration; then as role authenticated with jwt sub = the OWNER:
  update public.declarations set member_shipment_ids = array['aaaaaaaa-...']::uuid[], completeness_report='{"blockers":[],"forged":true}', status='READY' where id='44444444-...';  -> UPDATE 1
  select * from public.record_declaration_filed('44444444-...','REF-CROSS-PERIOD');  -> OK | 44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444
  filed row: status=FILED_RECORDED, period_claimed={"kind":"ANNUAL","year":2029,"quarter":null}, totals.embedded_emissions_tco2e=999, filed_snapshot.shipments=[{"reference":"ADV-D-2035","line_count":1,"status_at_filing":"READY","embedded_emissions_tco2e":"999"}], while the shipment's real reporting_period_year=2035.

PATH B (the companion path — I confirmed this too, and it is STRONGER than the finding's own framing): pg_policies shows shipments_update_own_org_not_terminal USING (org_id in user_org_ids AND status not in ('LOCKED','VOID')) with NO role gate and NO immutability trigger on reporting_period_* (only shipments_prevent_org_id_change_trg exists). So with a fully legitimate READY ANNUAL-2029 declaration whose member set was frozen honestly, a PLAIN MEMBER ran `update public.shipments set reporting_period_year=2035, reference='ADV-MOVED-2035' where id='aaaaaaaa-...'` -> UPDATE 1, and the OWNER's ordinary filing then returned OK, producing period_claimed 2029 / total 15 over a shipment whose actual period is 2035, and LOCKing it there. No member_shipment_ids forgery, no admin privilege required.

Both probes ran inside real `begin; ... rollback;` transactions; post-rollback state verified: 0 declarations, 0 shipments, 0 orgs. Throwaway DB dropped.

FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CLAIM ALSO CONFIRMED: my database was built from migrations + seed.sql only, so no grant/seed/ordering artifact is involved — the gap is a missing clause in the SQL body and reproduces on any fresh build. (Separately noted: before seed.sql, `authenticated` had no grant on public.declarations at all — the P14.1 seed hardening is what makes the exploit reachable, and it reproduces once the seed runs, i.e. in every real environment.)

Severity: I hold HIGH rather than downgrading. Path A alone is self-inflicted admin misstatement, which would argue for MEDIUM; Path B is a low-privilege MEMBER silently re-attributing a locked, archived, legally meaningful CBAM figure to the wrong reporting period, with a fully self-consistent audit trail and nothing in filed_snapshot a later reader could use to detect it.

One disclosure: early on I ran an auth-stub bootstrap (create table if not exists auth.users; create or replace auth.uid()/auth.jwt()) against a database named advrev_period_opus, which I had believed I was creating but which a concurrent agent had just created. Definitions were Supabase-equivalent; that database has since been dropped by its owner, so there is no residual state. No writes were made to the repo or to production.

CONFIRMED by independent rebuild, not by trusting the finder. The shared local postgres DB currently has zero objects in public schema, so I built a fresh DB (create database advrev_period_opus), restored auth/extensions/storage structure, applied all 74 repo migrations in order plus supabase/seed.sql, and verified the installed function is the release candidate: select prosrc like '%quantity_unit is distinct from%' from pg_proc where proname='record_declaration_filed' -> t.

(1) Static: in the live prosrc from that fresh DB, 'reporting_period' occurs only at lines 326-329 and 506-508, both inside jsonb_build_object (stamping filed_snapshot and the audit payload). The only membership test is `where s.id = any(v_member_ids) and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id and s.status in ('READY','LOCKED')` (supabase/migrations/20260903110000_p14_filing_requires_calculation_quantity_to_match_line.sql:186-192). No comparison of shipment period to declaration period exists.

(2) Mitigation search (ALREADY-MITIGATED lens) found nothing. Triggers on public.declarations are only declarations_prevent_fact_change_trg and declarations_touch_updated_at_trg; app.prevent_declaration_fact_change freezes member_shipment_ids/completeness_report only under `if old.status <> 'DRAFT'`, so DRAFT->READY with an arbitrary member set is permitted. RLS declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing: USING (app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(org_id) AND status = ANY(ARRAY['DRAFT','READY'])), WITH CHECK the same plus 'VOID' — no column pinning. Query `select n.nspname||'.'||p.proname from pg_proc ... where prosrc like '%reporting_period_year%'` returned only app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change, app.prevent_declaration_fact_change, app.declaration_predecessor_matches, public.record_declaration_filed — none of which compares a member shipment's period to the declaration's. Period filtering exists only in application code (src/application/declarations/compute-declaration-draft-facts.ts:104-134), which raw PostgREST bypasses.

(3) Live reproduction in the fresh DB inside a real begin;...rollback;: setup as postgres (org with capabilities {IMPORTER_DECLARANT}, OWNER membership, shipment ADV-D-2035 reporting_period_year=2035 status READY, one line net_mass_tonnes '10', one calculation_results row quantity '10'/TONNES with matching determination and embedded_emissions_tco2e '999', DRAFT ANNUAL-2029 declaration). Then `set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims='{"sub":"1111...","role":"authenticated"}'`; UPDATE declarations SET member_shipment_ids=array['aaaaaaaa-...']::uuid[], completeness_report='{"blockers":[],"forged":true}', status='READY' -> UPDATE 1; select * from public.record_declaration_filed('4444...','REF-CROSS-PERIOD') -> result_status OK. Resulting row: status FILED_RECORDED, filed_snapshot->'reporting_period' = {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2029, "quarter": null}, totals.embedded_emissions_tco2e "999", per_shipment[0].reference "ADV-D-2035", actual shipment reporting_period_year 2035. After ROLLBACK: 'AFTER ROLLBACK: declarations=0'.

(4) I additionally confirmed the stronger path the finder only asserted, which the finder did not prove: shipments_update_own_org_not_terminal is USING (org_id IN (select app.user_org_ids()) AND status <> ALL(ARRAY['LOCKED','VOID'])) and nothing freezes a shipment's reporting period. Second live probe (fresh DB, begin;...rollback;): honest ANNUAL-2029 shipment already in a READY ANNUAL-2029 declaration; a plain MEMBER (role MEMBER, not admin/owner) ran `update public.shipments set reporting_period_year=2035, release_date='2035-06-01', reference='ADV-DRIFTED-2035'` -> UPDATE 1; then the OWNER called record_declaration_filed -> OK, with filed_snapshot->'reporting_period' = {"kind":"ANNUAL","year":2029} while the member shipment's period is 2035. AFTER ROLLBACK decls=0 ships=0. So the defect is reachable with no forged column, no raw member-set edit, and no elevated role — an ordinary post-READY edit silently produces a mis-periodised filed snapshot.

(5) Fresh-environment claim holds: this is a missing clause in the SQL body, unaffected by grants/seed/ordering — I proved it on a database built from the repo's migrations plus seed in a brand-new database, and it reproduced identically.

Severity kept at HIGH (not lowered): the no-forgery drift path makes this reachable by ordinary use, and filed_snapshot is the archived legally meaningful artifact. It is bounded to the acting org's own data (RLS pins ids, s.org_id = v_decl.org_id enforced), so it is a self-inflicted misstatement, not cross-tenant — which is the same blast radius as 20260903110000, the migration the project itself wrote to close the analogous quantity gap. Cleanup: drop database advrev_period_opus -> DROP DATABASE; no repo file was modified.

title: The same shipment and the same calculation_results row can be frozen into two different FILED declarations for two different reporting periods
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260903110000_...sql: `and s.status in ('READY', 'LOCKED')`. The header comment justifies accepting LOCKED only for amendments ('an amendment (supersedes_declaration_id) covers shipments the superseded version already locked'), but the SQL applies no such restriction -- v_decl.supersedes_declaration_id is never consulted in the lockability test, and nothing anywhere asks whether another FILED_RECORDED declaration already lists this shipment.

LIVE (begin;...rollback;), org 00af0704-c2d8-4ea8-a9d8-c6bb3eee1252, role authenticated, jwt sub = owner af56decf-ff01-4972-adda-97fa4c298d98:
  one shipment 11111111-..., one line, one calculation row 33333333-... at 139 tCO2e;
  two READY declarations: 44444444-... (ANNUAL 2029) and 55555555-... (ANNUAL 2030), both member_shipment_ids = {11111111-...}
    select * from public.record_declaration_filed('44444444-...','REF-2029');  -> OK
    shipment now LOCKED, reporting_period_year 2029
    select * from public.record_declaration_filed('55555555-...','REF-2030');  -> OK
  resulting rows:
    55555555-... | 2030 | total 139 | calc_ids ["33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333"]
    44444444-... | 2029 | total 139 | calc_ids ["33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333"]
Two independent FILED_RECORDED declarations, different periods, citing the identical calculation_result_id as provenance for both.
exploit: Ordering that needs no raw member-set edit: (1) shipment S is in period P1, READY; declaration D(P1) is drafted and marked READY by the normal service, freezing members=[S]. (2) S's reporting-period columns are changed to P2 -- any MEMBER can do this via PostgREST and the RLS policy explicitly permits it. (3) D(P2) is generated by generateOrRefreshDeclarationDraft, which picks S up because it queries shipments by their CURRENT period columns, and is marked READY. (4) File D(P1) -> OK, S becomes LOCKED. (5) File D(P2) -> OK, because LOCKED is accepted unconditionally. Both filed snapshots carry S's emissions. Alternatively an admin sets member_shipment_ids directly, as in the probe.
impact: The same goods, the same tonnes, the same calculation are declared twice across two reporting periods. Both artifacts are immutable and both cite the same provenance id, so the duplication is discoverable only by cross-reading calculation_result_ids across periods, which nothing in the product does. Own-organization scope; no cross-tenant reach.
