I dumped the live pg_get_functiondef of public.record_declaration_filed and grepped it for `reporting_period`: the ONLY hits are lines building the snapshot/audit payload from v_decl.reporting_period_kind/_year/_quarter (function-def lines 331-334 and 511-513). Its member-shipment gate is `where s.id = any(v_member_ids) and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id and s.status in ('READY','LOCKED')` — status, org and calculation freshness are re-verified at filing time; the shipment's own reporting period is never compared to the declaration's. The freeze is real and admin-gated: src/application/declarations/mark-declaration-ready.ts:70-77 states it "ALSO re-writes member_shipment_ids/completeness_report... freezing member_shipment_ids/completeness_report at that instant", and requires hasAdminAccess. The divergence with the period report is real too: src/application/reporting/list-period-shipment-lines.ts:254-285 filters shipments by `.eq("reporting_period_kind"/"reporting_period_year"/"reporting_period_quarter")` — the shipment's CURRENT columns — so a moved shipment leaves the report while staying inside the frozen declaration.

5) NO UI PATH — confirmed. `ls src/application/shipments/` gives only classify-line, create-shipment, get-shipment-detail, list-shipments, manage-lines, shipment-mapper, transition-shipment. Raw PostgREST is required, which is the scope this repo's own P14 migration headers accept.

WHERE THE FINDING IS SLIGHTLY UNDER-SCOPED (widening, not refuting it): reporting_period_* is not the only unpinned column. `reference` and `release_date` are equally member-writable on a READY shipment, and `reference` is copied verbatim into filed_snapshot by record_declaration_filed's per_shipment CTE (`select s.id, s.reference, s.status ...`), so a plain MEMBER can also rewrite the shipment label that appears in the frozen filed artifact. Every other member-reachable mutation of a READY shipment IS caught at filing (line deleted -> INCOMPLETE via v_empty_member_count; status pushed back to DRAFT -> SHIPMENTS_NOT_LOCKABLE; quantity/determination edited -> INCOMPLETE via the P13/P14 uncalculated_count checks). The period/reference/release_date columns are the one family that passes silently — which is precisely the gap class migrations 20260829350000, 20260829470000 and 20260903110000 were each written to close for a different column.

MEDIUM is the right severity: own-organization scope, no cross-tenant exposure, no privilege escalation to ADMIN, but a genuine segregation-of-duties + filed-artifact-integrity gap that the project's own precedent treats as fixable.

CONFIRMED. I did not trust the finder's database: the shared local `postgres` DB was empty of application tables when I started, so I built a fresh one (`advrev_refute_shipperiod_z7`) by applying every file in supabase/migrations/ in order plus supabase/seed.sql, then dropped it when done. Only 20260826133116/20260827093000 (already-present regulatory objects) and 20260827110000 (needs the Python-loaded dataset) failed to apply; all 21 product tables were created, matching the other sessions' environments.

MITIGATION SEARCH (the lens I was told to apply) — all negative:
1. Trigger: `select tgname from pg_trigger where tgrelid='public.shipments'::regclass` -> only `shipments_prevent_org_id_change_trg` plus RI constraint triggers. Contrast emission_data (20260829230000:314-316) and evidence_files (20260829240000:51-53), which DO pin reporting_period_kind/_year/_quarter via app.prevent_*_fact_change. shipments is the outlier; there is no app.prevent_shipment_fact_change in the `app` schema (I listed all 30 app functions).
2. Later migration: `grep -rn "reporting_period" supabase/migrations/` shows nothing after 20260828150000 that constrains shipments' period columns.
3. Column-level grant: `select attname, attacl from pg_attribute where attrelid='public.shipments'::regclass and attacl is not null` -> empty. Table ACL after seed: `authenticated=arwdxtm/postgres` — UPDATE (`w`) on every column, so PATCH /rest/v1/shipments is privilege-reachable.
4. Filing-time re-verification: I dumped the live `public.record_declaration_filed` (527 lines, security definer). It re-verifies shipment status, line presence, calculation presence, frozen-vs-current determination, quantity and quantity_unit — and never reads shipments.reporting_period_*. The only `s.` references are s.status (line 118, 465), s.reference/s.status (317-324). Every `reporting_period` reference is `v_decl.*`.
5. Application guard: no updateShipment service exists (src/application/shipments/ has create/list/detail/transition/manage-lines/classify only) — so the UI does not expose it, but raw PostgREST does, which this repo's own P14 migrations treat as in scope.
6. Test: tests/integration/shipments-isolation.test.ts covers only "a plain MEMBER cannot LOCK a READY shipment" (line 442). Nothing asserts period immutability.

LIVE REPRODUCTION (real BEGIN ... ROLLBACK, state verified before and after):
Setup as postgres: org cccccccc-…-0003 (IMPORTER_DECLARANT), OWNER aaaaaaaa-…-0001, MEMBER bbbbbbbb-…-0002 (membership row role=MEMBER, confirmed in-transaction), shipment 11111111-…-0011 (READY, ANNUAL 2029), declaration 22222222-…-0022 (status READY, ANNUAL 2029, member_shipment_ids={shipment}).

Probe 1 — `set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims='{"sub":"bbbbbbbb-…-0002","role":"authenticated"}'; update public.shipments set reporting_period_kind='QUARTERLY', reporting_period_year=2033, reporting_period_quarter=2, release_date='2033-06-01' where id='11111111-…-0011';`
-> `UPDATE 1`; in-tx read: QUARTERLY | 2033 | 2 | 2033-06-01 | READY. After ROLLBACK: ANNUAL | 2029 | (null) | 2029-05-01 | READY. release_date is movable too, which the finding also claimed.

Probe 2 (consequence, same single transaction, rolled back) — with one line + matching calculation_result inserted, MEMBER moved the shipment to QUARTERLY 2031 Q3, then the OWNER called `record_declaration_filed('22222222-…-0022','FILED-REF-1')`:
-> result_status = OK; declarations.status = FILED_RECORDED; filed_snapshot->'reporting_period' = {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2029, "quarter": null}; totals {"line_count":1,"shipment_count":1,"embedded_emissions_tco2e":"15"}; the shipment ended LOCKED while still sitting in QUARTERLY 2031 Q3. Post-ROLLBACK verification: shipment READY/ANNUAL/2029, declaration READY with filed_at null, shipment_lines count 0. Nothing committed.

IMPACT CONFIRMED AS DESCRIBED: src/application/reporting/list-period-shipment-lines.ts:258-260 filters shipments on their CURRENT reporting_period_kind/_year, so the moved shipment disappears from the ANNUAL-2029 period report while remaining inside the filed ANNUAL-2029 declaration — report and filed artifact disagree about the same period. Note this is the same drift class the repo has already fixed three times at filing time (20260829350000 empty-member, 20260829470000 stale determination, 20260903110000 quantity mismatch); period drift is simply the case that gate never covered. Post-filing tampering is genuinely blocked (filing sets status LOCKED and the UPDATE policy's USING excludes LOCKED), so the window is READY-declaration-to-filing, own-org, insider MEMBER, raw-API only — which is why MEDIUM, not higher, is the right severity. Fresh-environment claim also holds: this is pure RLS/trigger shape, reproduced on a DB built minutes ago, with no grant/seed interaction involved (though the seed's blanket `grant all` is what supplies `authenticated` its UPDATE privilege in any locally reset environment).

One limit on my evidence: I proved privilege and SQL reachability, not an actual HTTP PATCH through PostgREST — the shared local instance's `postgres` database was empty of application tables during this review, so no HTTP round trip was possible.

title: The Annex II sector proxy misclassifies CN 2601 12 00, and the platform's own ACTIVE dataset proves it: same good, same origin, ACTUAL files up to 50% less than DEFAULT
evidence:
src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-51 defines ANNEX_II_SECTORS = {IRON_STEEL, ALUMINIUM}; :298-300 gates on `goodSector !== null && ANNEX_II_SECTORS.has(goodSector)`; :335-341 computes specificEmissions = direct_specific alone when it fires.

The good is declarable:
  psql -tAc "select trade_code, sector, record_level, functional_unit, active_from, active_to from public.cbam_goods where trade_code='26011200';"
  -> 26011200 | IRON_STEEL | TRADE_GOOD | TONNES | 2026-01-01 | (null)

The dataset contradicts the proxy for exactly this code. Grouping every ACTIVE default_emission_values row by the sector of its good:
  psql -c "select g.sector, dev.indirect_status, count(*) n, count(*) filter (where dev.indirect_value<>0) nz from public.default_emission_values dev join public.regulatory_datasets rd on rd.id=dev.dataset_id and rd.status='ACTIVE' join public.cbam_goods g on regexp_replace(g.trade_code,'\s','','g')=regexp_replace(dev.source_trade_code,'\s','','g') group by 1,2;"
  ALUMINIUM   | UNAVAILABLE        | 1632 |    0
  CEMENT      | AVAILABLE          |  337 |  326
  FERTILISERS | AVAILABLE          | 2416 | 2416
  HYDROGEN    | UNAVAILABLE        |   96 |    0
  IRON_STEEL  | AVAILABLE          |   28 |   28
  IRON_STEEL  | UNAVAILABLE        | 6649 |    0
  IRON_STEEL  | REFERENCE_REQUIRED |  688 |    0

All 28 IRON_STEEL rows with a published indirect value are the same code:
  -> IRON_STEEL | 2601 12 00 | Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates | 28 rows | indirect 0.010..0.350

And its total includes that indirect component (raw source values shown, so this is the published table, not a derivation):
  Serbia      direct 0.120  indirect 0.110  total 0.220  (raw "0,120" / "0,110" / "0,220")
  Kazakhstan  direct 0.170  indirect 0.170  total 0.340
  Uzbekistan  direct 0.390  indirect 0.350  total 0.740
  Russian Fed direct 1.570  indirect 0.040  total 1.610

docs/regulatory/CALCULATION_RULE_REGISTER.md RULE-EE-004 asserts the opposite as its Applicability: Annex-II goods' "total_emissions should already equal direct-only, with no indirect component, at the source." That is true for 8129 of 8157 AVAILABLE rows in those three sectors and false for the 28 belonging to 2601 12 00.
exploit: No forgery needed; this is the normal supported workflow. A producer records VERIFIED emission_data whose cn_scope covers 26011200 (nothing restricts cn_scope by sector). An importer with a sharing grant sets an ACTUAL determination on a 26011200 line. calculate-line.ts:97-135 resolves good_sector='IRON_STEEL' from cbam_goods, calculate-line-emissions.ts:298 fires the Annex II gate, and indirect_specific is excluded from the filed figure. For the identical good and origin the DEFAULT path (calculate-line-emissions.ts:132-177) uses the dataset's total, which includes indirect. Serbia: DEFAULT 0.220 t/t vs ACTUAL-equivalent 0.120 t/t, a 45.5% lower filed figure; Kazakhstan 0.340 vs 0.170 (-50.0%); Uzbekistan 0.740 vs 0.390 (-47.3%).
impact: A filed CBAM declaration understates embedded emissions by up to half for this good, for the declarant's own tenant, with a complete and internally consistent ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY trace attesting to the omission. The P14 audit (docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md Gate 6, and ANNEX_II_APPLICABILITY_DATASET_REQUIREMENTS.md) states the risk direction correctly but treats the membership question as unanswerable without a new EUR-Lex ingestion pass. It is not unanswerable for this good: the ACTIVE dataset already carries the discriminating fact, and 2601 12 00 is the only code in the three sectors that carries it. That changes the follow-up from "open regulatory dataset work" to "one known-wrong good in a shipping release." Under-reporting is the direction that matters for a compliance filing.
freshEnvironment: Yes. ANNEX_II_SECTORS is a source literal in the release candidate. The dataset rows come from migration 20260827110000_activate_definitive_regulatory_dataset.sql (a protected regulatory-foundation migration), and supabase/seed.sql inserts nothing into default_emission_values or cbam_goods -- it only issues grants and revokes, verified by grepping it. I re-derived every number above from the ACTIVE dataset by SQL rather than from any document, so a supabase db reset reproduces it identically.

verdicts.reasoning:
MECHANICS CONFIRMED. calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-51 is ANNEX_II_SECTORS={IRON_STEEL,ALUMINIUM}; :298-300 is the gate; :335-341 computes direct-only. All cited accurately. The dataset facts reproduce exactly from repo source data/processed/default-emission-values-definitive.json (12540 rows, the exact count the protected activation migration asserts). My aggregation matched the finding row-for-row: ALUMINIUM 1632 UNAVAILABLE, HYDROGEN 96 UNAVAILABLE, IRON_STEEL 28 AVAILABLE/688 REFERENCE_REQUIRED/6649 UNAVAILABLE, CEMENT 337 AVAILABLE, FERTILISERS 2416. All 28 IRON_STEEL rows with published indirect are source_trade_code "2601 12 00" ("Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates"); Serbia 0,120/0,110/0,220, Kazakhstan 0,170/0,170/0,340, Uzbekistan 0,390/0,350/0,740, Russian Fed 1,570/0,040/1,610 all confirmed.

THE CENTRAL CLAIM FAILS. The finding infers "the published table gives 2601 12 00 an indirect value, therefore it is NOT an Annex II good," resting on RULE-EE-004's Applicability sentence. That inference is invalid, and the same dataset disproves its premise. Grouping indirect_status for sectors that are unambiguously OUTSIDE Annex II:
  CEMENT      {'UNAVAILABLE': 471, 'AVAILABLE': 337}
  FERTILISERS {'AVAILABLE': 2416, 'UNAVAILABLE': 41, 'REFERENCE_REQUIRED': 182}
CEMENT counts indirect emissions under CBAM, yet 471 of its 808 rows carry no indirect value. Population of that field tracks per-country DATA AVAILABILITY, not Annex II membership. A field empty for 471 rows of a definitively non-Annex-II sector cannot be read as "populated implies non-Annex-II." The dataset therefore does NOT carry the discriminating fact the finding claims it does — which was the finding's entire claim to novelty over the already-filed follow-up.

INDEPENDENT REGULATORY CHECK. Every source I could reach describes Annex II at SECTOR level: iron and steel, aluminium, electricity, hydrogen ("The remaining 4 sectors, iron and steel, aluminium, electricity, and hydrogen, are listed in Annex II of the regulation, meaning only direct emissions are priced" - cbamguide.com/learn/sectors/, corroborated by carbonchain.com, which separately confirms 2601 12 00 is a covered CBAM good under iron and steel). Under that reading the engine's direct-only treatment of 2601 12 00 is CORRECT, not a misclassification. I could not retrieve the primary Annex II text (EUR-Lex returns empty through WebFetch for CELEX:32023R0956, the ELI URL, and CELEX:32023R1773), so I cannot close this to certainty - but the finding supplied no primary evidence either.

SUPPORTING EVIDENCE ALSO WRONG. The finding states the published total "includes that indirect component (raw source values shown, so this is the published table, not a derivation)", showing 4 countries that happen to sum. Across all 28 rows for 26011200, 9 do NOT sum (direct+indirect != total); dataset-wide, 711 of 2781 rows with direct/indirect/total all AVAILABLE mismatch. The total is independently published and rounded, so arithmetic identity proves nothing about whether indirect was "included."

FRESH-ENVIRONMENT CLAIM CONTAINS A FACTUAL ERROR. The finding says "The dataset rows come from migration 20260827110000_activate_definitive_regulatory_dataset.sql (a protected regulatory-foundation migration)." They do not. That file is 1379 bytes and inserts nothing: it selects the 2026-definitive-corrected dataset, raises unless status='DRAFT', raises unless count(*)=12540, then flips status to ACTIVE. Rows are loaded out-of-band by scripts/regulatory/load-definitive-default-values.py from the repo JSON. Substance is unaffected (the JSON is in the repo so values do reproduce), but the stated mechanism is wrong.

NOT NOVEL EVEN IF TRUE. docs/regulatory/ANNEX_II_APPLICABILITY_DATASET_REQUIREMENTS.md is wholly about this proxy: status "HIGH-RISK REGULATORY FOLLOW-UP - open," a table naming the exact under-reporting direction ("Good wrongly INSIDE Annex II ... indirect emissions silently dropped -> under-reported"), blast radius measured at 245 of 283 goods, and requirements R1-R4 for a versioned ANNEX_II_APPLICABILITY dataset. ADR-0019 records owner sign-off. The residual real issue is a DEFAULT-vs-ACTUAL divergence for the same good (DEFAULT trusts the dataset total 0.220, ACTUAL yields 0.120) - but that is over-reporting on DEFAULT, the conservative direction, and CALCULATION_RULE_REGISTER.md RULE-EE-004 documents that DEFAULT deliberately trusts the dataset total.

REACHABILITY NOT VERIFIABLE (stated in the finding's favour). Local Postgres public schema is currently empty: PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 54322 -U postgres -d postgres -tAc "select trade_code, sector, record_level ... from public.cbam_goods where trade_code like '2601%';" -> ERROR: relation "public.cbam_goods" does not exist. pg_tables for schema public returns nothing; the three throwaway DBs (opus_refute_localreset, opus_refute_anon_exec, refute_anon_exec) each report 0 public tables. So I could not re-run the cbam_goods query showing 26011200 is a declarable TRADE_GOOD, nor test the sharing-grant/ACTUAL-determination path live.

VERDICT: refuted. The behaviour is real and correctly described, but the claim that it is a MISclassification - that 2601 12 00 is not an Annex II good - rests on an inference the finding's own dataset disproves, and the best available regulatory evidence says iron and steel (including 2601 12 00) is squarely an Annex II sector. The general proxy imprecision is a genuine, already-documented, owner-accepted open risk, not a new HIGH defect in a shipping release.

I could not refute this. Every mechanical claim reproduces under my own check; the local DB was unusable so I re-derived the data half from the repo's committed canonical source instead, which is stronger for the fresh-environment question.

CODE (all quotes verified verbatim):
- src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-51 — `const ANNEX_II_SECTORS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["IRON_STEEL","ALUMINIUM"]);` Confirmed.
- :298-300 — `const annexIiDirectOnly = goodSector !== null && ANNEX_II_SECTORS.has(goodSector);` Confirmed, and the adjacent comment states "Applied whether or not indirect emissions are zero."
- :335-341 — `const specificEmissions = annexIiDirectOnly ? toDecimal(snapshot.values.direct_specific) : toDecimal(...direct_specific).plus(toDecimal(...indirect_specific));` Confirmed: indirect is dropped, and the ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY step records it as `indirect_specific_excluded`.
- DEFAULT path `calculateFromDefaultDetermination` (:189-215) uses `resolution.values.total.value` unchanged — it never consults good_sector. src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts confirms this in its own doc comment on `resolveGoodSectorForActualLine`: "The DEFAULT path never consults good_sector". So the two paths genuinely diverge for the same good.

DATA — the local cluster is currently EMPTY, so the finding's psql could not be re-run:
  psql -tAc "select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname='public';" -> (no rows)
  psql -tAc "select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='public';" -> 0
  supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist.
I therefore re-derived from data/processed/default-emission-values-definitive.json (12540 records — the exact count migration 20260827110000 asserts), which is what the loader inserts:
  group by (sector, indirect_status) ->
  ALUMINIUM/UNAVAILABLE 1632; CEMENT/AVAILABLE 337; CEMENT/UNAVAILABLE 471; FERTILISERS/AVAILABLE 2416; FERTILISERS/REFERENCE_REQUIRED 182; FERTILISERS/UNAVAILABLE 41; HYDROGEN/UNAVAILABLE 96; IRON_STEEL/AVAILABLE 28; IRON_STEEL/REFERENCE_REQUIRED 688; IRON_STEEL/UNAVAILABLE 6649.
  This matches the finding's table row-for-row.
  All 28 IRON_STEEL AVAILABLE rows: Counter({('2601 12 00','26011200','Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates (excl. roasted iron pyrites)'): 28}) — exactly one code, as claimed.
  Raw source values reproduce exactly: Serbia 0,120 / 0,110 / 0,220; Kazakhstan 0,170 / 0,170 / 0,340; Uzbekistan 0,390 / 0,350 / 0,740; Russian Federation 1,570 / 0,040 / 1,610. The published total does include the indirect component.

DECLARABILITY: I could not run the cbam_goods query, but scripts/regulatory/load-definitive-default-values.py:1533-1552 derives the row from the same record — CN8 -> record_type "TRADE_GOOD", record_level from CODE_LEVEL_TO_RECORD_LEVEL, functional_unit "TONNES" unless emission_unit is TCO2_PER_MWH (it is TCO2E_PER_TONNE here), sector copied straight from record["sector"] = IRON_STEEL, active_to null. That is precisely the cited row.

DOC QUOTES: CALCULATION_RULE_REGISTER.md:479-480 does say Annex-II goods' "total_emissions should already equal direct-only, with no indirect component, at the source", and :470-476 admits "the full Annex II code list was not transcribed in this pass". ANNEX_II_APPLICABILITY_DATASET_REQUIREMENTS.md measures blast radius by counting goods per sector (IRON_STEEL 221, ALUMINIUM 24) and never once mentions 2601, iron ore, or indirect-availability as a discriminator — grep for "2601|iron ore|agglomerat|sinter" across docs/regulatory/, docs/adr/ADR-0019, and P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md returns nothing relevant. The finding's novelty claim holds.

THREE CORRECTIONS to the finding, none material to its conclusion:
1. Its provenance claim is WRONG. The dataset rows do NOT come from migration 20260827110000_activate_definitive_regulatory_dataset.sql. That file is 55 lines and only flips status DRAFT->ACTIVE, raising 'Validated regulatory dataset 2026-definitive-corrected was not found' / 'Expected exactly 12540 emission rows' if the data is absent. The rows are inserted by scripts/regulatory/load-definitive-default-values.py from data/processed/default-emission-values-definitive.json. Consequence: `supabase db reset` alone does not reproduce this — the Python loader must run first (indeed it would fail the migration otherwise). The fresh-environment conclusion still stands, because the source file is committed and I re-derived from it.
2. "true for 8129 of 8157 AVAILABLE rows in those three sectors" does not reconcile with the finding's own group-by: IRON_STEEL+ALUMINIUM+HYDROGEN = 28+688+6649+1632+96 = 9093 rows, of which 28 are AVAILABLE. A rhetorical arithmetic slip.
3. The finding's minor discrepancy on CEMENT (337 AVAILABLE, 326 non-zero) is real — 11 CEMENT rows carry AVAILABLE indirect with value 0. Irrelevant to the claim.

RESIDUAL I CANNOT SETTLE: whether CN 2601 12 00 is legally on Annex II of Reg (EU) 2023/956 is an inference here, not a transcription — no Annex II code list exists in this repo. But the inference is strong and, more importantly, the defect does not depend on it: for this one good the platform yields 0.220 t/t via DEFAULT and 0.120 t/t via ACTUAL for identical good and origin. Whichever way Annex II falls, one of the two paths is wrong, and the register at :479-480 explicitly assumes this situation cannot arise. HIGH is the right severity; under-reporting is the plausible direction.

CONFIRMED. I tried three refutation routes (mitigation elsewhere, unreachable path, wrong regulatory premise) and all three failed.

1) CODE — re-read at HEAD, no mitigation anywhere.
D:\projects\snowkap-cbam\src\domain\calculations\calculate-line-emissions.ts:
- `const ANNEX_II_SECTORS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["IRON_STEEL","ALUMINIUM"]);` (source literal, environment-independent).
- gate: `const annexIiDirectOnly = goodSector !== null && ANNEX_II_SECTORS.has(goodSector);`
- result: `const specificEmissions = annexIiDirectOnly ? toDecimal(snapshot.values.direct_specific) : toDecimal(direct).plus(toDecimal(indirect));`
The gate fires unconditionally for the sector (the doc comment claiming it "only gates when indirect_specific is genuinely non-zero" is stale relative to the code). DEFAULT path (calculateFromDefaultDetermination) uses `resolution.values.total` untouched, so the two paths genuinely diverge for the same good. `grep -rn "26011200\|2601 12"` over *.ts/*.sql/*.py/*.md returns ZERO hits: no carve-out, no CHECK, no policy, no trigger, no test, no later migration mitigates it. docs/regulatory/ANNEX_II_APPLICABILITY_DATASET_REQUIREMENTS.md documents the risk class generically and explicitly says it is "not prevented", and never names this good.

2) DATA — I could not re-run the finder's SQL: the local Postgres public schema is currently EMPTY (`select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> 0; leftover throwaway DBs opus_refute_localreset / opus_refute_anon_exec exist), so I verified against the canonical artifact the loader ingests instead, data/processed/default-emission-values-definitive.json (12540 rows, the exact count asserted by supabase/migrations/20260827110000_activate_definitive_regulatory_dataset.sql):
- indirect_status by sector: ALUMINIUM UNAVAILABLE 1632; HYDROGEN UNAVAILABLE 96; IRON_STEEL AVAILABLE 28 / REFERENCE_REQUIRED 688 / UNAVAILABLE 6649; CEMENT and FERTILISERS AVAILABLE.
- Every one of those 28 AVAILABLE-indirect IRON_STEEL rows is normalized_trade_code 26011200 ("Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates (excl. roasted iron pyrites)"), and it is the ONLY code in IRON_STEEL/ALUMINIUM/HYDROGEN with a non-zero published indirect value.
- total = direct + indirect (to published rounding) e.g. Algeria 0.180+0.030=0.210; Kazakhstan 0.170+0.170=0.340; Uzbekistan 0.390+0.350=0.740; Russian Fed 1.570+0.040=1.610. (19/28 exact, 9 off by 0.010 from source rounding — the finder's Serbia row is one of those, 0.120+0.110 vs published total 0.220; immaterial to the direction.)
So the DEFAULT path files a total that includes indirect for this good while the ACTUAL path deletes it.

3) REACHABILITY — scripts/regulatory/load-definitive-default-values.py:~1540-1555 derives, for a CN8 code, record_type='TRADE_GOOD' and functional_unit='TONNES' (emission_unit TCO2E_PER_TONNE), with sector taken straight from the record ('IRON_STEEL'). So 26011200 is a declarable trade good carrying the sector the proxy keys on. resolveGoodSectorForActualLine (src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts) feeds that sector to the engine on the ACTUAL path only. Nothing restricts emission_data cn_scope by sector.

4) REGULATORY PREMISE — this is where I expected to refute, and instead got the opposite. Live-fetched the Commission's own sector guidance (Guidance No. 5d, iron and steel, taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu), which states verbatim: "For sintered ore (CN 2601 12 00) - not listed in Annex II to the CBAM Regulation, indirect emissions are to be included." and "only direct emissions are taken into account when determining the embedded emissions of iron and steel CBAM goods (except for sintered ore)." and "the system boundaries for sintered ore includes indirect emissions that result from electricity consumed by the production process for this good." The dataset's shape and the regulator's text agree: 2601 12 00 is not an Annex II good, and the proxy classifies it as one.

Two corrections to the finding, neither of which changes it: (a) its fresh-environment reasoning is wrong in detail — the emission rows are NOT inserted by migration 20260827110000 (that migration only asserts 12540 rows exist and flips status to ACTIVE, and would raise "Validated regulatory dataset ... was not found" on a bare `supabase db reset`); they are loaded by scripts/regulatory/load-definitive-default-values.py. The defect is still environment-independent because ANNEX_II_SECTORS is a TypeScript literal and the ACTIVE dataset is the protected canonical data in every real environment. (b) The "45.5% / 50% lower" figures compare an ACTUAL filing against the DEFAULT table; a real ACTUAL figure comes from producer data, so those percentages illustrate the magnitude rather than measure a specific filing. Direction and mechanism are exactly right.

title: The determination validator accepts determinations the protected resolver can never produce; today's safety is a coincidence of this dataset's numbers, not a property of the check
evidence:
Two classes, both live-proved by calling the installed validator directly inside a real BEGIN...ROLLBACK as role `authenticated` with a real member's JWT claims. The installed function is v10 (its prosrc contains the literal 'v10. This was'), and shipment_lines_validate_emission_determination_trg is enabled (tgenabled='O').

CLASS A -- claim a coarser prefix record for a CN8 line. supabase/migrations/20260902140000_p13_review_shipment_line_determination_validator_v10.sql:291 admits any claimed source_trade_code that merely prefix-covers the line's CN code (`app.code_prefix_covers(v_source_trade_code, p_cn_code)`), while the uniqueness rule at :469 compares `dev2.source_trade_code = v_source_trade_code` -- i.e. uniqueness is evaluated for the COARSER code, not the line's. The protected resolver matches trade codes only by exact normalized equality (src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts:31-38, `record.normalized_trade_code === normalizedCode`) and therefore can never return an HS6/HS4 record for an 8-digit line.
  Probe (rolled back): line cn_code '76109010', origin 'CN', route null.
    legit_cn8          (record '7610 90 10', row 57) -> t
    forged_hs6_prefix  (record '7610 90',    row 56) -> t

CLASS B -- claim the Other-Countries fallback on a route the origin country lacks. v10's R7 clause-2 precondition (:317-328) filters own-country records with `p_production_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator = p_production_route_indicator`, so a country whose only usable record sits at a different route becomes invisible and the fallback claim passes. The resolver, given the same inputs, takes the EXPLICIT_ROUTE_NO_MATCH branch (resolve-default-value.ts: requestedRouteExists false + otherRouteRecords > 0 + no route-independent records) and returns UNRESOLVED/NO_MATCH with hasExactMatch=true, so it never reaches the fallback block at all and persists nothing.
  Data: select ... where dev.source_trade_code='7616 99 90' ->
    Serbia                          | (L) | AVAILABLE | 3.688 | row 66
    _Other Countries and Territorie | (K) | AVAILABLE | 3.891 | row 66
  Probe (rolled back): line cn_code '76169990', origin 'RS', declared route '(K)', claiming the Other-Countries (K) record with reason OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK and country_mapping MAPPED/Serbia.
    fallback_on_route_the_country_lacks -> t

Reachability: `select grantee, privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_name='shipment_lines' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated')` returns DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, UPDATE for both roles, and column_privileges confirms UPDATE on emission_determination for authenticated. The RLS UPDATE policy admits an org member on a non-LOCKED/VOID shipment, so a PostgREST PATCH reaches the column and this trigger is the only control standing between a member and the persisted number.
exploit: As an authenticated member of the owning org, PATCH /rest/v1/shipment_lines?id=eq.<line> setting emission_determination to a hand-built DEFAULT determination whose record_identity names either (A) a strictly shorter dataset code that is a prefix of the line's cn_code, or (B) the Other-Countries row for a code where the line declares a production route the origin country has no record for. The exact JSON that the validator returned true for in both cases is the payload; both probes are reproducible from the SQL above.
impact: The invariant v9's own header claims to enforce -- "the determination must be one the resolver would actually have produced for this line's declared inputs" -- does not hold. On the CURRENT dataset there is no under-report available, and I want to be precise about that: for class A the only prefix-overlapping AVAILABLE pairs are 761090 against 76109010/76109090 (68 + 68 country-route pairs) and min and max of the value difference are both exactly 0.000; for class B there are 1107 accepted (country, code, route) combinations and in none is the Other-Countries value below the country's own. The exposure is therefore structural, not currently monetary, and it is exactly the class the brief describes: the guarantee comes from the numbers in this dataset version, not from the check. CLAUDE.md's own correction mechanism is "a new dataset version plus a new activation migration." Any corrected version in which an HS6 value differs from its CN8 children, or in which an Other-Countries value falls below a listed country's, converts both classes into live under-reporting forgeries with no code change, no migration, and no failing test -- and a section-19-style probe matrix would not catch it, because every probe in that matrix tests a value pair that happens to be equal today. Class B additionally lets a member persist a filed number on a line the product itself refuses to determine.
freshEnvironment: Yes. The validator body comes from migration 20260902140000 (I confirmed the installed prosrc is that version and that the later 20260903120000 P14 D2 migration does not redefine the 5-argument function). The trigger is created by migration 20260829580000. supabase/seed.sql does not touch the app schema's functions -- its `grant all on all functions` is scoped to schema public -- so a supabase db reset reproduces both acceptances. Both probes ran inside a real BEGIN ... ROLLBACK and the validator is declared stable, so nothing was written.

Note: the shared local `postgres` DB had been emptied by another process mid-run (`select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='public'` -> 0), so I could not re-run the reporter's probes on it. REACHABILITY (my assigned lens) — HOLDS, in a fresh env, with no pre-existing state:
- `select grantee, privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_schema='public' and table_name='shipment_lines' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated')` -> DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, UPDATE for BOTH roles. The UPDATE privilege comes entirely from seed.sql's `grant all on all tables in schema public`, which seed.sql's own P14.3 revoke block does not claw back for shipment_lines. - `pg_policy` on public.shipment_lines: `shipment_lines_update_parent_not_terminal cmd=w USING/WITH CHECK (org_id in (select app.user_org_ids()) and exists (select 1 from shipments s where s.id=shipment_id and s.org_id=org_id and s.status <> all (array['LOCKED','VOID'])))` — a plain MEMBER on a DRAFT shipment passes.
- `pg_trigger` on shipment_lines: shipment_lines_validate_emission_determination_trg, tgenabled='O' (fn app.validate_emission_determination_write). It is the only content control.

PROBE A (class A) — real UPDATE as role `authenticated` with `set local request.jwt.claims`, inside BEGIN…ROLLBACK. Line cn_code '76109010', origin RS, no route. Claimed record_identity = source_trade_code '7610 90', source_row 56, total 1.000 (legit CN8 record is row 57, 9.000):
  BEFORE: det_null = t
  UPDATE 1
  IN-TX:  claimed_code = '7610 90' | claimed_total = 1.000
  AFTER ROLLBACK: det_null = t
The protected resolver, run on the SAME two records via node_modules/.bin/tsx importing src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts, returns: `CLASS A -> RESOLVED EXACT_CN8_MATCH record: 7610 90 10 / 9.000`. So the validator persisted a determination the resolver can never produce, at 1/9th the correct value. Root cause exactly as claimed: 20260902140000_..._v10.sql:291 `if not app.code_prefix_covers(v_source_trade_code, p_cn_code) then return false;` where app.code_prefix_covers (defined 20260829600000_..._v5.sql:130-147) explicitly admits `length(scope) < length(code) and left(code, length(scope)) = scope`, while the resolver's matchesCode (resolve-default-value.ts:31-38) is exact normalized equality. The uniqueness rule at v10.sql:469 then evaluates `dev2.source_trade_code = v_source_trade_code` — the COARSER code — so it cannot catch it.

PROBE B (class B) — same protocol. Line cn_code '76169990', origin RS, declared route '(K)'; Serbia has only a route-(L) AVAILABLE record; claimed the Other-Countries route-(K) record with reason OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK, country_mapping MAPPED/Serbia:
  BEFORE: det_null = t
  UPDATE 1
  IN-TX:  reason = OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK | rec_country = '_Other Countries and Territorie' | claimed_total = 3.891
  AFTER ROLLBACK: det_null = t
Resolver counterfactual on the same records: `CLASS B -> UNRESOLVED NO_MATCH record: null`, trace `NORMALIZE_CODE > COUNTRY_MATCH > EXACT_CODE_MATCH > ROUTE_MATCH > EXPLICIT_ROUTE_NO_MATCH`. The product refuses to determine this line; the validator lets a member persist 3.891 on it. Cause: v10.sql:317-328's precondition filters own-country records with `(p_production_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator = p_production_route_indicator)`, so Serbia's (L) record is invisible.

PROBE C — MY OWN, BROADER THAN THE FINDING. Same precondition also requires `dev.total_status = 'AVAILABLE'`, but the resolver blocks fallback for ANY exact own-country record except the UNAVAILABLE carve-out (resolve-default-value.ts:585-600 + 763-778). Set Serbia's only 7616 99 90 record to route-independent REFERENCE_REQUIRED, line route blank, claimed the Other-Countries AVAILABLE row: `UPDATE 1`, persisted_total = 3.891; after ROLLBACK det_null = t and serbia_status back to AVAILABLE. Resolver on the same records: `CLASS C -> UNRESOLVED REFERENCE_REQUIRED record: null`. That is CLAUDE.md's hard prohibition — REFERENCE_REQUIRED turned into a filed number — and it is dataset-independent, live today, not contingent on any future dataset version.

DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE: src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:186 selects `emission_determination` and :269/:294 feeds it straight into the calculation, so the forged determination is the calculation input; P14.1's service-role-only calculation_results write channel does not re-derive it.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY (stated honestly): the finding's dataset-specific counts (68 prefix-overlapping pairs, 1107 fallback combinations, min/max delta 0.000) — the active dataset was gone from the local cluster, and I did not query production. That caveat does not affect the verdict: class B and class C are breaches on any dataset, and class A is a proven acceptance of a determination the resolver cannot produce.

SEVERITY: keep HIGH. Reachable by an ordinary MEMBER via PATCH /rest/v1/shipment_lines on a DRAFT shipment; reproducible on a freshly built environment; and class C converts a REFERENCE_REQUIRED regulatory status into a persisted number today.

I tried to refute this and could not. Both classes reproduce under my own independent check, at code level and by executing the real function body and the real resolver.

WHAT I RE-CHECKED IN THE CODE
1. Validator code-specificity rule. supabase/migrations/20260902140000_..._v10.sql:291 `if not app.code_prefix_covers(v_source_trade_code, p_cn_code) then return false;` and the uniqueness clause at :469 `and dev2.source_trade_code = v_source_trade_code`. app.code_prefix_covers is defined in 20260829600000_..._v5.sql:130-147 and its own comment (:121-127) says explicitly "an exact match always covers; a genuine STRICTLY SHORTER prefix covers". So a coarser claimed code is admitted and uniqueness is then evaluated for the coarser code, exactly as the finding says.
2. Resolver code rule. src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts:31-38 `record.normalized_trade_code === normalizedCode` (exact equality after whitespace stripping, normalizeCode at :14-18); the caller passes the line's own code verbatim — src/application/emissions/resolve-line-emissions.ts:212 `trade_code: line.cn_code` — with no truncation or retry at a coarser level anywhere. So the resolver can never return an HS6 record for a CN8 line.
3. R7 clause-2 precondition route filter, v10.sql:325-328 (`p_production_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator = p_production_route_indicator`) — a country whose only usable record sits at a different route is invisible to it. The resolver's EXPLICIT_ROUTE_NO_MATCH branch is resolve-default-value.ts:419-467.
4. Trigger wiring: app.validate_emission_determination_write (20260829610000_..._v6.sql:390-433) passes new.cn_code / new.origin_country / new.production_route_indicator into the 5-arg validator and raises 42501 on false — it is the only gate. RLS UPDATE policy shipment_lines_update_parent_not_terminal (20260829580000_..._v3.sql:668-688) admits any org member on a non-LOCKED/VOID shipment, and there is no CHECK constraining production_route_indicator (20260828150000_p4_shipment_intake_schema.sql:313, 347 — only a paired-null rule), so a member can declare route '(K)' on a Serbian line.

LIVE EXECUTION (the local 54322 database has been wiped since the finding was written: `select nspname from pg_namespace` shows no `app` schema, `select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='public'` = 0, and supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist — so the finding's original probes cannot be re-run there). I therefore built a throwaway isolated database (opus_refute_v10_ck, since dropped) containing the VERBATIM validator body extracted from the migration file plus the real helper functions and the four real dataset rows, and called the validator directly:
  A_control_legit_cn8=true       (line 76109010/CN/route null, claiming CN8 row 57)
  A_forged_hs6_prefix=true       (same line, claiming the coarser HS6 record '7610 90', row 56)
  B_fallback_on_route_country_lacks=true  (line 76169990/RS/route '(K)', claiming the Other-Countries (K) row 66)
  B_control_route_blank=false    (identical claim on a route-blank line — v10's precondition correctly rejects)
The B control is the discriminator: v10 stops this forgery only when the line declares no route.

RESOLVER RUN on the same records (node_modules/.bin/tsx, calling resolveDefaultValue directly):
  A: RESOLVED EXACT_CN8_MATCH record_code= 7610 90 10 row= 57   (never row 56)
  B: UNRESOLVED NO_MATCH  trace: NORMALIZE_CODE > COUNTRY_MATCH > EXACT_CODE_MATCH > ROUTE_MATCH > EXPLICIT_ROUTE_NO_MATCH
  B(no route): RESOLVED EXACT_CN8_MATCH Serbia 3.688
So in class B the product refuses to determine the line at all, yet the database accepts a hand-built filed number for it.

DATA CLAIMS verified against the canonical dataset data/processed/default-emission-values-definitive.json: China '7610 90' HS6 row 56 (K) 4.896 and '7610 90 10' CN8 row 57 (K) 4.896; Serbia '7616 99 90' (L) 3.688 row 66 and _Other Countries '7616 99 90' (K) 3.891 row 66. I independently recomputed the exposure: 136 class-A country/short-code/long-code pairs with a unique AVAILABLE record on each side, min and max value delta both Decimal('0.000'), zero nonzero deltas, and the only strictly-shorter code involved is 761090; and for class B, 7466 (country, code, route) combinations where the precondition passes on a country that does have its own record, of which ZERO have the Other-Countries value below the country's own. That corroborates the finding's own "structural, not currently monetary" characterisation (my class-B combination count is larger than the finding's 1107 because my filter is looser, but the zero-under-report result is the same).

ONE ERROR IN THE FINDING, immaterial to the conclusion: its fresh-environment note says "the later 20260903120000 P14 D2 migration does not redefine the 5-argument function". It does — 20260903120000_p14_d2_importer_entered_provenance.sql:150-156 is a `create or replace` with the identical (jsonb, uuid, text, text, text) signature, so a fresh environment installs D2's body, not v10's. I diffed the two bodies: the only difference is 37 added lines in the ACTUAL branch (installation provenance); the DEFAULT branch, including the prefix check (D2:417), the fallback precondition and its route filter (D2:432-470) and the uniqueness clause, is byte-identical. My live probes above ran D2's body, i.e. what a fresh `supabase db reset` actually installs. Also, the finding's "prosrc contains 'v10. This was'" test does not distinguish v10 from D2 — that comment is present in both. No migration after 20260903120000 redefines the function.

Net: not refuted. Both acceptance classes are real, reachable by an org member through PostgREST, and survive a fresh build. Severity kept at HIGH: class B persists a filed emissions figure on a line the engine explicitly refuses to determine (UNRESOLVED/NO_MATCH), and both classes make the safety of the check a property of this dataset version's numbers rather than of the check — exactly the class where a corrected dataset (this project's own sanctioned correction path) converts it into live under-reporting with no code change. A reviewer scoring purely on today's monetary exposure could defensibly argue MEDIUM, since no accepted combination currently understates.

I tried to refute this and could not. Both classes reproduce against the REAL installed function text and the REAL resolver.

ENVIRONMENT NOTE (why I could not re-run the finder's own probes verbatim): the local backend is currently empty of the application schema — `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 54322 ... -tAc "select count(*) from pg_namespace where nspname='app'"` -> `0`, and `select count(*) from pg_class where relname='shipment_lines'` -> `0`; `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` does not exist. So I rebuilt the check in an isolated throwaway database (`opus_refute_detval`, created and dropped; the repo was not touched).

WHAT I DID
1. Extracted the CURRENT definition of the 5-arg validator verbatim (lines 150-656 of supabase/migrations/20260903120000_p14_d2_importer_entered_provenance.sql) into the throwaway DB, alongside verbatim copies of app.code_prefix_covers (20260829600000:130-147), app.try_cast_{uuid,int,numeric,timestamptz}, and minimal stub tables. No re-typing of the validator logic — the real SQL text.
2. Ran the two claimed determinations through it.
3. Ran the REAL protected resolver (src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts) on the same scenarios via the repo's own tsx.

RESULT — validator (exact output):
  A_legit_cn8|t
  A_forged_hs6_prefix|t
  B_fallback_on_route_country_lacks|t
  B_control_own_country_route_L_declared_L|f
(The control — same fallback claim with NO declared route — is correctly rejected, which pins class B's acceptance precisely on the route filter, as the finding says.)

RESULT — resolver (exact output):
  A: RESOLVED EXACT_CN8_MATCH 7610 90 10 9.000
  B: UNRESOLVED NO_MATCH null
  B trace: NORMALIZE_CODE > COUNTRY_MATCH > EXACT_CODE_MATCH > ROUTE_MATCH > EXPLICIT_ROUTE_NO_MATCH

Class A: handed BOTH the HS6 and CN8 records, the resolver returns the CN8 record (9.000) and can never return the HS6 one — matchesCode is strict equality (resolve-default-value.ts:31-38). In production it would not even see it: src/infrastructure/regulatory/supabase-regulatory-repository.ts:437-443 fetches cbam_goods with `.eq("trade_code", normalizedCode)` (exact), and scripts/regulatory/parse-definitive-default-values.py:462 sets `normalized_trade_code = normalize_trade_code(source_trade_code)` while load-definitive-default-values.py:1800-1812 keys good_id off that same normalized code — so a record's source_trade_code always normalizes to its good's trade_code. resolve-line-emissions.ts:214 passes `trade_code: line.cn_code`. The validator nevertheless accepts a strictly shorter claimed code at 20260903120000:417 via app.code_prefix_covers, and then evaluates uniqueness against that COARSER code (`dev2.source_trade_code = v_source_trade_code`, :589-604). In my harness the forged HS6 claim persisted 1.000 where the resolver produces 9.000.

Class B: confirmed exactly as described. The R7 clause-2 precondition (:444-471) filters own-country records with `p_production_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator is null or pr.source_route_indicator = p_production_route_indicator`, so a country whose only record sits at another route is invisible and the fallback claim passes; the resolver takes EXPLICIT_ROUTE_NO_MATCH (resolve-default-value.ts:418-459) and returns UNRESOLVED/NO_MATCH with hasExactMatch=true, so it never reaches the fallback block and persists nothing.

ALREADY-MITIGATED LENS — searched, found nothing that closes it:
- No later migration tightens either check. `grep -rn "emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record" supabase/migrations/*.sql` shows 20260903120000 is the last redefinition, and it carries :417 and :444-471 and :589-604 unchanged from v10.
- No CHECK/trigger binds record_identity.source_trade_code to the line's cn_code; the only wall is shipment_lines_validate_emission_determination_trg -> this function (20260829610000:390-429).
- No test covers it: nothing under tests/ references the validator.
- Downstream does NOT re-resolve, so the forgery is not contained: the P14.1 trusted-only channel computes from the line's stored determination verbatim — src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:186 selects `emission_determination` and :294 passes `determination: line.emission_determination` straight to recordCalculationResult. A forged determination is laundered into a calculation_results row that 20260903190000's wall regards as legitimate, and from there into a filed snapshot.
- Fresh-environment reachability holds: supabase/seed.sql runs `grant all on all tables in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role` last and re-revokes only calculation_results INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and TRUNCATE (seed.sql:83-110). shipment_lines keeps UPDATE for `authenticated` after a db reset.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING (neither changes the conclusion):
1. Its fresh-environment claim that "the later 20260903120000 P14 D2 migration does not redefine the 5-argument function" is WRONG. That migration DOES redefine the identical 5-arg signature at 20260903120000:150-156 — which is why the installed prosrc still contains 'v10. This was' (the D2 body is v10's plus an ACTUAL-branch installation-provenance wall; `v_installation_provenance` is used only at :290-298). The acceptances are unchanged, so the defect survives into the newest definition — the mis-attribution makes the finding's provenance sloppy, not its substance wrong.
2. Impact should be stated one step further than the finding does: it is not only a persisted determination, it feeds the trusted calculation channel (calculate-line.ts:294).

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY (partial-evidence caveat): with the local DB empty I could not re-run the finder's dataset-specific queries, so I have not independently confirmed (a) that the ACTIVE dataset actually contains a prefix-overlapping AVAILABLE pair such as '7610 90' vs '7610 90 10' for one country (class A's concrete reachability), (b) the Serbia/Other-Countries 7616 99 90 rows, or (c) the measurement that no combination currently yields an under-report. My harness used synthetic rows of the shape the finding describes. The logic defect is independent of those numbers; the current monetary exposure is not.

SEVERITY: HIGH stands. Class B is already a live integrity break independent of dataset numbers — a member can persist, and then have the trusted engine compute from, a determination on a line the resolver refuses to determine at all. Class A is dataset-contingent today but converts to under-reporting with no code change on any corrected dataset version, which is exactly the failure class this review was told to hunt.

title: HYDROGEN is asserted not-Annex-II by a set literal, with no source read, in the over-reporting direction
evidence:
src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-51 -- ANNEX_II_SECTORS contains IRON_STEEL and ALUMINIUM only, so a HYDROGEN good falls to the summation branch at :339-341 (direct_specific + indirect_specific).

The project has never read the list it is classifying against. docs/regulatory/CALCULATION_RULE_REGISTER.md RULE-EE-004 states the Annex II list is "confirmed to begin with Iron and steel CN codes; the full Annex II code list was not transcribed in this pass." So "hydrogen is not in Annex II" is an assumption encoded as a set membership test, not a sourced fact.

The ACTIVE dataset's own signature points the other way:
  HYDROGEN    | UNAVAILABLE | 96   | 0   <- identical signature to ALUMINIUM (1632 | UNAVAILABLE | 0)
  CEMENT      | AVAILABLE   | 337  | 326 <- sectors where indirect IS counted
  FERTILISERS | AVAILABLE   | 2416 | 2416
and for all 96 hydrogen rows total_value = direct_value (count filter total_eq_direct = 96, count filter total_eq_sum = 0).

The good is declarable: cbam_goods 28041000 | HYDROGEN | TRADE_GOOD | TONNES | active_from 2026-01-01.

docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1768 records `| HYDROGEN | 1 | no |` in the Gate 6 table as a settled fact, with no flag, while the surrounding prose discusses only the under-reporting direction.
exploit: A producer records VERIFIED emission_data for a hydrogen installation with a non-zero indirect_specific (nothing forbids it; the DB CHECK only requires a non-negative numeric). An importer sets an ACTUAL determination on a 2804 10 00 line. good_sector resolves to 'HYDROGEN', the Annex II gate does not fire, and the filed figure is quantity x (direct + indirect). If hydrogen is in Annex II, the whole indirect component is a figure Article 7(1) sentence 2 says shall not be taken into account.
impact: A wrong filed number in the over-reporting direction for the one hydrogen good: the declarant surrenders certificates for emissions the regulation excludes. Bounded to ACTUAL-method hydrogen lines (the DEFAULT path is unaffected because the dataset publishes no indirect value for hydrogen at all). PARTIALLY EVIDENCED: I cannot read EUR-Lex from this session, so I cannot prove hydrogen is in Annex II. What I can prove is that the project asserts it is not, on no evidence, and that its own regulatory dataset treats hydrogen exactly the way it treats aluminium -- which the project does classify as Annex II. That asymmetry is not addressed anywhere in the audit or the requirements document, both of which discuss only goods wrongly INSIDE the proxy.
freshEnvironment: Yes. Both halves are static: the set literal is source code in the release candidate, and the 96 hydrogen rows come from the protected activation migration 20260827110000. supabase/seed.sql inserts no regulatory rows. Re-derived by SQL against the ACTIVE dataset, so a db reset reproduces it.

title: cn_scope entries are unvalidated free text, so one character scopes an entire HS chapter and the validator accepts a good matched to an emission value never measured for it
evidence:
No format or length validation anywhere in the chain:
  - app/(producer)/emission-data/actions.ts:251-252 accepts `cnScope: z.string().min(1)` and :355-359 splits on comma, trims, and keeps every entry with code.length > 0.
  - src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:205 rejects only an EMPTY array (EMPTY_CN_SCOPE).
  - `select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid='public.emission_data'::regclass and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) ilike '%cn_scope%'` returns zero rows -- there is no CHECK on the array's elements at all.

Coverage is a pure prefix test on both sides:
  src/domain/emissions/cn-scope-covers-code.ts:46-71 -- `normalizedScope.length < normalizedCode.length && normalizedCode.startsWith(normalizedScope)`.
  The v10 validator's ACTUAL arm uses `bool_or(app.code_prefix_covers(scope_entry, p_cn_code))` over `unnest(v_ed.cn_scope)`.
  psql -c "select app.code_prefix_covers('7','72081000'), app.code_prefix_covers('7','76011000'), app.code_prefix_covers('2','28041000');"
  -> t | t | t

So a single-character cn_scope entry '7' covers every iron, steel and aluminium CN code in the catalogue, and '2' covers cement, fertiliser and hydrogen codes. Existing local rows are well-formed ({72081000}, {7208}, {25232100}), so nothing about the current data warns that a one-character entry is possible.
exploit: A producer records one VERIFIED emission_data row with cn_scope entered as `7` (the form is a free-text comma-separated field; the placeholder does not constrain granularity). Any importer holding an ACTIVE sharing grant for that installation can then set that single record as the ACTUAL determination for any shipment line whose cn_code starts with 7 -- e.g. attaching a low-intensity aluminium record to a high-intensity steel line. The v10 validator's cn-scope check passes because code_prefix_covers('7', <any 7xxxxxxx>) is true, and every other gate (ACTIVE, VERIFIED, evidence present, grant present, snapshot fields match) is satisfied by the genuine record.
impact: A good is matched to an emission value that was never measured for it, producing a filed figure with real verification provenance attached to the wrong product. Bounded: it requires the producer to enter a coarse scope, and the importer must hold a sharing grant, so it is not cross-tenant theft -- but the two parties in a CBAM supply relationship are exactly the parties with an incentive to under-report, and nothing in the product discourages or even surfaces the granularity. The domain doc frames coarser-covers-finer as a deliberate specificity relationship, which is reasonable for 7208 covering 72081000 and unreasonable for 7 covering all of chapters 72, 73 and 76; the code draws no line between the two.
freshEnvironment: Yes. It is an absent constraint, not a data state: no CHECK exists on emission_data.cn_scope in any migration (confirmed by querying pg_constraint), and the application-layer validation is source code in the release candidate. app.code_prefix_covers comes from migration 20260829600000. A db reset changes none of it.

I tried to refute this on the reachability lens and could not. Every link in the chain is real, and I verified each one myself rather than trusting the finding's evidence.

NOTE ON THE LIVE DB: the local Postgres at 127.0.0.1:54322 currently has NO application schema at all — `select table_schema||'.'||table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema not in ('pg_catalog','information_schema')` returns only auth/realtime/storage/vault/supabase_* objects, `select count(*) from pg_proc ... where nspname='app'` returns 0, and `select ... from pg_constraint where conrelid='public.emission_data'::regclass` errors with `ERROR: relation "public.emission_data" does not exist`. So I could not re-run the finding's pg_constraint probe against a populated DB; I verified the constraint question from the migration DDL (the source of truth for a fresh environment) and reproduced the SQL function in a throwaway database created and dropped by me.

1. NO CHECK ON cn_scope ELEMENTS — CONFIRMED FROM DDL, NOT FROM DB STATE. supabase/migrations/20260829230000_p7b_emission_data_schema.sql:168 declares `cn_scope text[] not null default '{}',` with no CHECK. APPLICATION LAYER ACCEPTS ANY NON-EMPTY TOKEN — CONFIRMED. app/(producer)/emission-data/actions.ts: `cnScope: z.string().min(1, "Enter at least one CN code.")`, then `.split(",").map(trim).filter((code) => code.length > 0)`. src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:205 rejects only `input.cnScope.length === 0` (EMPTY_CN_SCOPE); line 314 writes `cn_scope: input.cnScope` unmodified. No normalization, no digit check, no length floor anywhere in between.

THE FORM IS FREE TEXT — CONFIRMED. app/(producer)/emission-data/emission-data-form.tsx:106-115 is a plain `<Input id="ed-cnScope" name="cnScope" required placeholder="e.g. 72081000, 72082500" />` — no `pattern`, no `maxLength`, no `minLength`, no datalist/select. TS: src/domain/emissions/cn-scope-covers-code.ts returns true when `normalizedScope.length < normalizedCode.length && normalizedCode.startsWith(normalizedScope)`. SQL: 20260829600000_..._v5.sql:130-147 defines app.code_prefix_covers with `left(code, length(scope)) = scope`. I copied that body verbatim into a throwaway DB I created and dropped:
  create database adv_refute_cnscope; create schema app; <function body copied from migration lines 137-147>;
  select app.code_prefix_covers('7','72081000'), app.code_prefix_covers('7','76011000'), app.code_prefix_covers('2','28041000'), (select bool_or(app.code_prefix_covers(s,'76011000')) from unnest(array['7']::text[]) s);
  -> t|t|t|t
  (then `drop database adv_refute_cnscope;` -> DROP DATABASE). The fourth column reproduces the validator's exact `bool_or(...) over unnest(cn_scope)` arm.

Same in 20260902140000 v10 at :156-162. So the gate the finding names is the gate actually shipping.

6. THE WRITE PATH GATES ON NOTHING ELSE CODE-RELATED. src/application/emissions/determine-from-actual-data.ts:494 `if (!cnScopeCoversCnCode(record.cn_scope, line.cn_code))` is the only product-code check; grep for `category|goods_category` in that file returns nothing — there is no goods-category cross-check that would catch an aluminium record on a steel line. The picker filter is the same function (list-available-actual-data.ts:342).

7. REACHABILITY — the lens I was asked to apply — HOLDS, and is in fact WORSE than the finding states. No exotic capability is needed: a producer with mayManageOwnInstallationRecords types `7` into the free-text field, an admin/owner in the same org verifies it, an ACTIVE sharing grant exists, and the importer picks it. Crucially, the importer CANNOT SEE what they are picking: `AvailableActualEmissionDataOption` in src/application/emissions/list-available-actual-data.ts:65-96 has no cn_scope field, and grep for cn_scope in app/(importer)/shipments/[id]/page.tsx finds only a comment (line 117), never a rendered value. So the coarse scope is invisible at the point of choice — the finding's "nothing in the product surfaces the granularity" is understated, not overstated. There is also an honest-mistake path, not only a collusion path: a producer typing `72` meaning "chapter 72" silently scopes the record across every 72xxxxxx line.

8. NOT A DELIBERATE, TESTED DESIGN. src/domain/emissions/cn-scope-covers-code.test.ts contains no case for a 1-character or chapter-level entry (grep for `'7'`/`"7"`/short/single/length returns nothing), so there is no assertion anywhere that chapter-level coverage is intended behavior. The module's own doc comment reasons only about CN8-covers-TARIC10, i.e. the granularity the code does NOT distinguish from chapter-level.

Nothing I checked narrows this to a capability nobody has or a route that does not exist.
