Severity MEDIUM is appropriate -- it is not a cross-tenant break (it needs the producer to enter a coarse scope and the importer to hold an ACTIVE sharing grant), but it lets a genuinely VERIFIED emission record be attached to goods it was never measured for, with real verification provenance, and nothing in the product surfaces the granularity.

Every factual claim re-verified independently; no mitigation exists anywhere in the chain. Severity corrected down because the missing format check confers no capability the same actor lacks by legitimate means.

WHAT I CONFIRMED

1. No format validation in the app chain (exact lines match the finding):
- app/(producer)/emission-data/actions.ts:251-252 `cnScope: z.string().min(1, "Enter at least one CN code.")`.
- actions.ts:355-359 `.split(",").map((code) => code.trim()).filter((code) => code.length > 0)` — length is the only filter.
- src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:205 `if (input.cnScope.length === 0) { ... EMPTY_CN_SCOPE }` — only an empty ARRAY is rejected.
- src/domain/emissions/cn-scope-covers-code.ts:66-69 `normalizedScope.length < normalizedCode.length && normalizedCode.startsWith(normalizedScope)` — pure prefix test, no minimum length.
- app/(producer)/emission-data/emission-data-form.tsx:107-110 — plain text input, no `pattern`/`inputMode`; only a placeholder "e.g. 72081000, 72082500".

2. No database constraint. The local `postgres` DB has an empty public schema right now, so I ran against a fully migrated throwaway DB in the same cluster (opus_refute_det, 21 public tables, created by another agent — read-only use, I created and dropped nothing):
`select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid='public.emission_data'::regclass;`
returns 14 rows — PK, FKs, and CHECKs on reporting_period_kind, methodology, verification_status, version, status, quarter, direct_specific/indirect_specific numeric — and NOT ONE mentions cn_scope. Confirmed with `select tgname, pg_get_triggerdef(...) from pg_trigger` (4 triggers: prevent_fact_change, verification_gate, touch_updated_at, activation_gate) and `select prosrc ... proname='enforce_emission_data_activation_gate'` grepped for "scope" — no output. The INSERT policy is `emission_data_insert_own_org|((entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE i.id = emission_data.installation_id AND i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)))` — no cn_scope predicate, so a direct PostgREST insert bypasses even actions.ts's length filter.

3. Coverage behaviour, run live:
`select app.code_prefix_covers('7','72081000'), app.code_prefix_covers('7','76011000'), app.code_prefix_covers('2','28041000'), app.code_prefix_covers('','72081000');` -> `t|t|t|t`
Note the fourth column, which the finding did not report: an EMPTY-STRING scope entry covers every code (left(code,0)='' ), and the domain function behaves identically ([""] -> startsWith("") is always true). actions.ts filters empty strings, but the RLS insert path does not.

4. Fresh-environment claim holds. This is an absent constraint in migration 20260829230000_p7b_emission_data_schema.sql:168 (`cn_scope text[] not null default '{}'`) plus source code; the throwaway DB I queried was built from migrations, not from the shared local state, and shows the same absence. A db reset changes nothing.

5. The codebase already knew. supabase/migrations/20260829600000_..._v5.sql:90-99 states F5 was exploitable precisely because "emission_data.cn_scope carries no format constraint"; the fix replaced LIKE with app.code_prefix_covers but deliberately never added the constraint. So no later migration closed it.

MITIGATIONS I LOOKED FOR AND DID NOT FIND: no CHECK, no trigger, no RLS predicate, no catalogue cross-check, no test. src/domain/emissions/cn-scope-covers-code.test.ts has 9 cases (exact, CN8-covers-TARIC10, reverse-not-covered, unrelated code, shared-prefix-non-prefix, multi-entry, empty array, whitespace) — none asserts anything about a 1-character or empty entry, so no test pins the current behaviour either way.

WHY SEVERITY IS LOWER THAN CLAIMED (MEDIUM -> LOW)

The claimed exploit is reachable but confers no incremental capability. cn_scope is the record owner's own declaration about their own installation's data; the same producer who types `7` can equally type `72081000, 76011000, 73044100` and obtain the identical mis-attachment. The missing format check therefore does not bypass any boundary — it only removes a guardrail against an over-broad entry. The remaining controls are untouched: determine-from-actual-data.ts:494 enforces coverage at commit time (P13 S16), the record must be ACTIVE + VERIFIED with a non-null verifier (determine-from-actual-data.ts:513-517), evidence must be present, an ACTIVE sharing grant is required, and the v10 validator re-checks all of it in SQL. The importer also SEES the scope it is picking — app/(importer)/external-emissions/page.tsx:219 passes `cnScope: record.cn_scope` into the picker — and the chosen scope is frozen into the audited snapshot. So this is a real data-integrity gap (an accidental coarse or empty entry silently widens coverage across whole HS chapters with no warning, and the direct-REST path admits an empty-string entry that covers literally everything), but it is not a forgery vector and it is not cross-tenant.

title: The persisted resolution_reason is not bound to the claimed record's code level, so an exported determination can misstate its own match specificity
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260902140000_p13_review_shipment_line_determination_validator_v10.sql:224-232 checks only that v_reason is one of EXACT_TARIC_MATCH / EXACT_CN8_MATCH / EXACT_HS6_MATCH / EXACT_HS4_MATCH / OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK. Nothing compares the reason against the length or level of v_source_trade_code. The protected resolver derives the reason from the record's code_level (src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts, resolutionReasonFor), so the two can only disagree in a hand-built determination.

Demonstrated by the same rolled-back probe as the prefix finding: a determination naming the 6-digit record '7610 90' was accepted while carrying reason 'EXACT_HS6_MATCH' -- and would equally have been accepted carrying 'EXACT_CN8_MATCH', since the reason is never cross-checked. resolution_reason is a generated column on shipment_lines (migration 20260829150000) and is emitted into the CSV and XLSX period exports (src/application/reporting/build-period-export-rows.ts).
exploit: PATCH shipment_lines.emission_determination with a valid record identity but a reason naming a different match level. The row persists and the mislabelled reason propagates to the generated column and to every regulatory export.
impact: No effect on the emissions figure. It degrades the audit trail: the field an auditor would use to judge how specifically a good was matched can say EXACT_CN8_MATCH for a record that is an HS4 heading. Own-tenant, raw-API-only, and only for a member who is already hand-writing determinations.
freshEnvironment: Yes -- it is a missing check in the validator body installed by migration 20260902140000, unaffected by seed.sql (which does not touch the app schema).

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, with one correction: the finding cites a superseded migration. The installed validator is not 20260902140000 (v10) but supabase/migrations/20260903120000_p14_d2_importer_entered_provenance.sql:150-656, whose header says "The validator body below is the 20260902140000 (v10) body verbatim apart from the marked provenance clause". The gap is present in the live version too.

1. CODE. Every occurrence of v_reason in the current validator: 20260903120000 lines 372 (assignment), 374-379 (membership in the 5-value enum), 433, 482, 521, 530, 534 (OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK-only clauses). v_source_trade_code appears at 407, 412, 417 (code_prefix_covers against p_cn_code), 595, 627, 642 (record lookup/uniqueness). Nothing anywhere compares the reason to the length or level of the matched record's trade code. Confirmed with: grep -n "v_reason\|source_trade_code" on that file. No CHECK constraint or trigger elsewhere binds it either: grep for EXACT_CN8_MATCH across supabase/migrations/ returns only the same enum list inside successive validator bodies (20260829530000:304, 540000:171, 580000:446, 600000:367, 610000:231, 620000:242, 20260831110000:243, 20260902090000:274, 20260902140000:250, 20260903120000:376).

2. LIVE PROBE. The local postgres DB has no product schema (information_schema.tables for public/app returns nothing; supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist), so I built a throwaway DB (create database opus_refute_reasonlevel), installed the real helper functions (app.try_cast_*, app.code_prefix_covers verbatim from 20260829600000:130-147), a stub app.user_org_ids(), minimal regulatory tables, and the validator body extracted verbatim from 20260903120000 lines 150-656. Fixture: one AVAILABLE row, country 'China'/iso2 'CN', source_sheet 'Aluminium', source_row 43, source_trade_code '7610 9000', direct 1.500 / indirect 0.500 / total 2.000. Called with p_cn_code='76109000', p_origin_country='CN', p_production_route_indicator=null, MAPPED country_mapping, values matching exactly, varying only resolution.reason:

claimed_reason|accepted
EXACT_HS6_MATCH|t
EXACT_CN8_MATCH|t
EXACT_TARIC_MATCH|t
EXACT_HS4_MATCH|t
OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK|f
MADE_UP|f

The truthful label here is EXACT_CN8_MATCH (record code == the line's 8-digit CN code); EXACT_TARIC_MATCH, EXACT_HS6_MATCH and EXACT_HS4_MATCH are accepted identically. This is stronger than the finding's own demonstration because it does NOT depend on the companion prefix finding — the record is an exact-code match and the label is still free. (I also reproduced the finding's own '7610 90' / '76109000' case: same result, all four EXACT_* accepted.) Throwaway DB dropped afterwards.

3. REACHABILITY (the lens). Writable by an ordinary member: shipment_lines carries policy shipment_lines_update_parent_not_terminal (last defined 20260829580000:668-689) which gates UPDATE only on org membership and the parent shipment not being LOCKED/VOID — the emission_determination WITH CHECK clause was deliberately moved to a BEFORE trigger. That trigger, app.validate_emission_determination_write (latest body 20260829610000:390-433), calls the validator with (new.emission_determination, new.org_id, new.cn_code, new.origin_country, new.production_route_indicator) and raises 42501 only if it returns false. So the validator is the ONLY content gate on a member's raw PostgREST PATCH of emission_determination. There are no column-level grants on shipment_lines (grep for "grant update (" across migrations: no hits) and no trusted-write-only gate on shipment_lines (20260903190000 applies that pattern to calculation_results only; its only references to shipment_lines are reads at :176 and :205). Capability needed: authenticated member of the own org — nobody exotic.

4. PROPAGATION. resolution_reason is a generated column on shipment_lines (20260829150000:46, indexed at :71-73). src/application/reporting/build-period-export-rows.ts:241 emits `determination.resolution.reason` straight through, and app/api/reports/export/route.ts:222,263 puts it in the CSV/XLSX as "Resolution reason". Worse for durability: src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:186,230,269,294 reads the line's stored emission_determination and freezes it into the calculation result, and build-period-export-rows.ts:195-201 prefers the calculation's frozen determination — so a forged label is captured permanently at calculation time, not merely reflected transiently.

5. WHY IT IS ONLY LOW. Every numeric field is still bound: the record identity must resolve to exactly one real row (20260903120000:620-646), the uniqueness rule at :588-602 must yield exactly 1 usable candidate, and direct/indirect/total status and value must equal the record's (:649-656). The mislabel cannot move an emissions figure; it can only misstate how specifically the good was matched, in the audit trail and exports. It also requires an actor already hand-writing raw determinations, who gains nothing numeric by lying about the label. Fresh-environment claim also holds: this is a missing predicate in a function body, unaffected by seed.sql ordering.

Suggested minimal fix, for the record: derive the level from length(regexp_replace(v_source_trade_code,'\s+','','g')) (10/8/6/4 -> TARIC/CN8/HS6/HS4) and require v_reason to match it whenever v_reason <> 'OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK' — mirroring resolutionReasonFor() in src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts:79-104. Note the protected resolver takes code_level from cbam_goods.trade_code_type (src/infrastructure/regulatory/supabase-regulatory-repository.ts:150-153), not from string length, so a level-exact fix would join cbam_goods rather than measure the string.

CONFIRMED by independent code reading and by my own live probe. I tried hard to refute it and could not.

1. Exhaustive reading of the validator body. `D:\projects\snowkap-cbam\supabase\migrations\20260902140000_p13_review_shipment_line_determination_validator_v10.sql` is 543 lines. `grep -n "v_reason"` returns exactly 8 occurrences: 96 (declare), 246 (assignment `v_reason := v_resolution->>'reason'`), 248-249 (enum-membership check against the 5 allowed strings), 307, 356, 395, 404, 408. Every one of the five usage sites after the assignment tests only `= 'OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK'` or `is distinct from 'OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK'`. Nothing anywhere in the function compares the reason to `v_source_trade_code`'s length/level, to `goods.trade_code_type`, or to `shipment_lines.cn_code_level`. Therefore the four EXACT_* values are provably interchangeable in the function's return value.

2. Live probe on a throwaway database I created and dropped myself (`create database opus_reasonlvl_r2 template opus_refute_v10_ck;` ... `drop database opus_reasonlvl_r2;`). I first dumped the installed function with `pg_get_functiondef` and confirmed it carries the identical 8 v_reason usages as the repo v10 migration. Then I called the validator with one determination that differs ONLY in the `reason` string, naming record source_trade_code '7610 90' (6 digits, HS6 level, source_sheet 'China', source_row 56) against cn_code '76109010':

  claimed_reason           | validator_accepts
  EXACT_TARIC_MATCH        | t
  EXACT_CN8_MATCH          | t
  EXACT_HS6_MATCH          | t
  EXACT_HS4_MATCH          | t
  OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK | f
  MADE_UP_REASON           | f

A record whose trade code is a 6-digit heading is accepted while claiming EXACT_TARIC_MATCH or EXACT_CN8_MATCH. That is exactly the finding's claim.

3. Reachability confirmed. The BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger `app.validate_emission_determination_write()` (latest definition at 20260829610000_..._v6.sql:390) calls this validator with precisely the 5 arguments I used and raises 42501 only when it returns false; nothing else constrains the reason. `grep -rn "resolution_reason" supabase/migrations/` shows the string appears only in 20260829150000 (the generated column at :46 and its index at :71-73) and a comment in the P4 schema — no CHECK constraint ties it to cn_code_level. Unlike calculation_results (locked to a trusted write path by 20260903190000), shipment_lines.emission_determination remains member-writable subject to this validator.

4. The protected resolver does derive the reason from code_level: `src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts:79-103` (`resolutionReasonFor`, switch on `record.code_level`), and code_level comes from `goods.trade_code_type` via `src/infrastructure/regulatory/supabase-regulatory-repository.ts:150-153`. So the DB does hold the information needed to bind the two; the check is simply absent.

5. Fresh-environment claim holds: the gap is a missing check inside a function body installed by a migration; seed.sql's blanket grants are irrelevant to it.

TWO MINOR CITATION ERRORS in the finding, neither affecting the substance:
- The cited range ":224-232" is the `v_resolution` shape check. The reason enum check is at lines 246-255 of the same file.
- The export does emit the reason, but `src/application/reporting/build-period-export-rows.ts:241` reads it straight from the determination JSON (`determination.resolution.reason`), not from the `resolution_reason` generated column. Same value, different source.

Severity: LOW is right. No effect on any emissions figure (values, dataset, record identity, route uniqueness and fallback legitimacy are all still bound); own-tenant; raw-API only; degrades only the match-specificity metadata an auditor reads.

I tried to refute this and could not.

1. CURRENT validator, not the cited one. The finding cites supabase/migrations/20260902140000_...validator_v10.sql:224-232, but that function is superseded: supabase/migrations/20260903120000_p14_d2_importer_entered_provenance.sql:150 does a `create or replace` of the same 5-arg app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record and is the last definition in the migration set. The defect is present there too. Every use of v_reason in that file: 372 (assign), 374-381 (membership in the 5-value allowed set), 433/482/521/530/534 (all OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK branches). v_source_trade_code is used at 407, 412, 417 (code_prefix_covers), 595, 627, 642 (uniqueness/record lookup) - never compared to v_reason. No length() or code-level comparison binds them.

2. ALREADY-MITIGATED search, all negative:
 - supabase/migrations/20260829150000_p5_emission_determination_generated_columns.sql:44-49 defines resolution_reason as a plain generated column with no CHECK, only indexes.
 - `grep -rn code_level supabase/migrations/*.sql` matches only 20260828150000 and 20260829090000 (the shipment_lines cn_code_level column). No migration derives or checks a matched record's code level.
 - The true level IS knowable to the validator: src/infrastructure/regulatory/supabase-regulatory-repository.ts:150 maps code_level from goods.trade_code_type, and src/domain/regulatory/resolve-default-value.ts:79-101 (resolutionReasonFor) switches on exactly that; the validator already pins the record to exactly one row (20260903120000:620-645, v_match_count must be 1). The correct reason is fully determined and simply not checked.
 - No write-path gate: grep for grant/revoke mentioning shipment_lines over all migrations returns nothing, so there is no calculation_results-style trusted-write-only restriction (cf. 20260903190000) on shipment_lines.emission_determination; members write it under RLS shipment_lines_update_parent_not_terminal (20260829580000:668) with only the trigger validator in the way.

3. LIVE RE-RUN. The project's local Postgres currently has NO app schema (`select table_schema,table_name from information_schema.tables where table_name like '%shipment%'` on 127.0.0.1:54322/postgres returned zero rows; supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist), so I built throwaway database opus_rl2 in the same cluster with the byte-exact function source extracted from 20260903120000 lines 150-656 plus verbatim helpers (app.code_prefix_covers from 20260829600000:130; try_cast_uuid/int/numeric/timestamptz from 20260829410000/20260829580000/20260829530000) and the four tables the DEFAULT path reads. One record: dataset 2026-01 ACTIVE, country India (IN), source_trade_code '7610 90' (6-digit), total AVAILABLE 2.000, no route. Calling the validator with cn_code '76109000', origin 'IN', route null, varying ONLY the reason:

 EXACT_HS6_MATCH | t
 EXACT_CN8_MATCH | t
 EXACT_TARIC_MATCH | t
 EXACT_HS4_MATCH | t
 OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK | f

All four EXACT_* reasons are accepted against the identical 6-digit record; only OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK is bound, via the country-name branch. Throwaway DB dropped afterwards; no repo file touched.

4. Propagation confirmed: src/application/reporting/build-period-export-rows.ts:241 emits resolution_reason straight from determination.resolution.reason into the shared CSV/XLSX row shape, and the row carries the LINE's cn_code_level (line 231), not the matched record's trade code, so the export gives an auditor no way to cross-check claimed specificity.

5. Fresh-environment claim holds: this is function-body logic installed by a migration, unaffected by seed.sql's blanket grants.

Partial mitigation, which is why I hold LOW rather than raising it: app.audit_emission_determination_change (20260829580000:760-790; trigger fires on insert/update/delete) writes an audit_events row for every determination change including 'from_reason' and 'to_reason' and the actor, so a hand-written mislabel is logged - but the persisted and exported field stays wrong. Combined with no effect on the emissions figure, own-tenant scope, and the precondition that the attacker already construct an otherwise fully valid determination via the raw API, LOW is right.

title: A pending invitee's account can be taken over by anyone who knows the invited address, using only the public anon key — /auth/v1/signup on an invited, unconfirmed user returns a full session and stamps email_confirmed_at, defeating every "confirmed email" authorization gate
evidence:
supabase/config.toml:319 `enable_confirmations = false` (the setting every `supabase start` / `supabase db reset` / CI / E2E environment is built with). supabase/migrations/20260829380000_p11_review_email_confirmation_and_invitation_hardening.sql:34 claims of the app.user_confirmed_email() fix: "This holds regardless of what `enable_confirmations` is set to on any environment: an unconfirmed user's email claim is now worthless for this class of authorization no matter how Auth is configured"; line 110 repeats it in the function's own COMMENT. That claim is false.

Live against the local backend (throwaway address, user deleted afterwards, deletion verified):

  POST http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/invite (service key)  -> {"id":"dc9a51f3-064b-42b9-9031-53def9097a36","email":"advrev-probe-1788431433@example.com","invited_at":"2026-09-03T10:30:34.064765621Z"}
  psql: select id,email,email_confirmed_at,invited_at from auth.users where email='advrev-probe-1788431433@example.com';
    -> dc9a51f3-064b-42b9-9031-53def9097a36|advrev-probe-1788431433@example.com||2026-09-03 10:30:34.064765+00      (email_confirmed_at NULL)
  POST http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/signup with ONLY the public anon key, same email, attacker-chosen password
    -> HTTP 200 {"access_token":"eyJ...sub\":\"dc9a51f3-064b-42b9-9031-53def9097a36\"...","refresh_token":"v46zz..."}   (a full session as the invitee's own user id)
  psql, same row again
    -> dc9a51f3-...|advrev-probe-1788431433@example.com|2026-09-03 10:30:34.490812+00|2026-09-03 10:30:34.064765+00   (email_confirmed_at now SET, 426 ms later, by the signup — no link was ever clicked)

The same stamping happens for a plain first-time sign-up through the app's own form. Read-only corroboration from users the Playwright suite created by typing into /sign-up (tests/e2e/cross-org-sharing-journey.spec.ts:96-140, no admin API involved): `select email, created_at, email_confirmed_at, confirmation_sent_at from auth.users` returns e.g. e2e-importer-54c87add@example.com | 2026-09-03 10:27:04.966599+00 | ... | confirmation_sent_at NULL, with email_confirmed_at - created_at = 00:00:00.021129.

And the downstream chain, in a real rolled-back psql transaction:
  begin;
  insert into public.organization_invitations (id,org_id,email,role,status,invited_by) values ('11111111-...','e6b92b10-4da3-4768-ada9-6a7cf281a8d0','e2e-importer-54c87add@example.com','ADMIN','PENDING','88150c48-...');
  set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"695b612c-aca4-41c8-b5c7-ba2bb754de9a","role":"authenticated"}';
  select app.user_confirmed_email();            -> e2e-importer-54c87add@example.com
  select * from public.organization_invitations; -> the invitation is RLS-visible
  select * from public.accept_organization_invitation('11111111-...'); -> OK | e6b92b10-4da3-4768-ada9-6a7cf281a8d0
  (memberships in that org: 695b612c... | ADMIN)
  rollback;   -- post-rollback counts re-verified: 1 membership, 0 invitation rows
exploit: 1. Attacker learns an address with a pending Snowkap invitation (an org invite the admin announced, or a sharing-grant invitation — issueSharingGrant provisions no auth user at all, so those addresses are unclaimed indefinitely). 2. Attacker POSTs /auth/v1/signup — or just uses the product's own /sign-up form — with that address and a password of their choosing, before the invitee clicks their emailed link. 3. GoTrue returns a session for the invitee's own user id and sets email_confirmed_at. 4. Attacker opens /accept-invitation; organization_invitations_select_own_email admits the row because app.user_confirmed_email() now returns the address; 5. Attacker presses Accept and accept_organization_invitation() mints a membership at the invited role — ADMIN is invitable. The attacker is now an administrator of a tenant they have no relationship to, and the real invitee's account is gone.
impact: Full cross-tenant compromise of any organization with an outstanding invitation, at whatever role the invitation carries (ADMIN grants access to everything the org can see, including producers' shared verified emissions data and the ability to file declarations). Also defeats create_organization_with_owner's confirm-your-email gate and the sharing-grant email-claim gates, which share app.user_confirmed_email(). Bounds, stated honestly: this requires enable_confirmations to be OFF. Production is REPORTED to have it on (docs/plans/P13_RELEASE_READINESS_REPORT.md §16.11: "mailer_autoconfirm: false"), so today's live site is probably not exploitable — but that is an unversioned dashboard setting, docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md §5 still carries it as unticked checkboxes for both staging and production, and every environment this repository itself builds has it off. The specific new capability here — hijacking an already-provisioned invitee account through the public signup endpoint — is not described anywhere in the S3 write-up, which frames the gap only as "the authorization gate is vacuous."
freshEnvironment: Yes — this IS the freshly-built environment. The database I probed was built by `supabase db reset` (migrations + seed.sql) against supabase/config.toml, which is the file under version control and which sets enable_confirmations = false at line 319. Nothing about the probe depended on accumulated state: I provisioned a brand-new invited user via the admin invite endpoint and hijacked it seconds later. The corroborating auth.users rows come from users the E2E suite creates from scratch on every run. A second consequence of the same fact: because CI, local and E2E all run with the gate off, no test in this repository can ever exercise or regress-detect the confirmed-email gate — tests/integration/organizations-isolation.test.ts has to hand-mint a raw HS256 JWT precisely because the real flows cannot produce an unconfirmed session there, and its doc comment's stated "real wall" (the password grant refusing an unconfirmed user) is walked around simply by using /auth/v1/signup instead.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute this on the reachability lens and could not; I positively confirmed it instead.

LIVE REPRODUCTION (fresh env: `select count(*) from auth.users` = 0 before I started, a clean reset):
1. Invite via service key: POST http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/invite -> user 51eeda5c-c1f8-40b3-be43-055a87bac550, and psql confirmed email_confirmed_at was NULL after the invite: `51eeda5c...|refute-probe-...@example.com||2026-09-03 10:54:59.483...` (empty email_confirmed_at column).
2. Takeover via PUBLIC ANON KEY ONLY: POST http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/signup with the same email and an attacker-chosen password returned HTTP 200 with a full access_token+refresh_token whose sub is 51eeda5c... (the invitee's own id) — decoded JWT payload contains "sub":"51eeda5c-c1f8-40b3-be43-055a87bac550". No admin/service key used.
3. psql immediately after: `51eeda5c...|...@example.com|2026-09-03 10:55:00.067...|...` — email_confirmed_at is now SET, ~584ms after invite, no confirmation link ever clicked.
Probe user then deleted via admin API (HTTP 200) and deletion verified (0 remaining; 0 probe users remain now).

DOWNSTREAM CHAIN verified by reading the shipped source (public schema tables not applied in the current local DB, so I read the migrations rather than re-run the SQL join, but the logic is mechanical given email_confirmed_at is set):
- supabase/migrations/20260829380000_...:120-127 defines app.user_confirmed_email() as `select email from auth.users where id=auth.uid() and email_confirmed_at is not null` — returns the invitee email once step 3 has stamped email_confirmed_at.
- Same migration line 205-208: the hardened accept_organization_invitation derives v_user_email from the identical `email_confirmed_at is not null` predicate, so the EMAIL_MISMATCH guard (line ~226) is skipped and line 248-256 inserts memberships at v_invite.role.
- 20260828130000_organization_invitations.sql:62-64: role CHECK is `role in ('ADMIN','MEMBER')` — ADMIN is invitable.

FALSE GUARANTEE CONFIRMED: the migration's own claim at 20260829380000 lines ~34 and ~110 ("This holds regardless of what enable_confirmations is set to ... an unconfirmed user's email claim is now worthless no matter how Auth is configured") is disproven by step 3: with supabase/config.toml:319 enable_confirmations=false, /auth/v1/signup itself sets email_confirmed_at, so the "confirmed email" gate is satisfied with zero mailbox proof. The gate is NOT config-independent.

REACHABILITY: maximally reachable in every repo-built environment — the credential is the PUBLIC anon key and the endpoint is the product's own /sign-up, and config.toml (versioned) ships enable_confirmations=false for local/CI/E2E. The one honest bound, which the finding states plainly: it requires enable_confirmations OFF. Production is reported to have it ON (P13 report §16.11 mailer_autoconfirm:false), the RC is NOT deployed, and DEPLOYMENT.md §5 carries "enable confirmations" as a pre-go-live checkbox. So a correctly-provisioned production is not exploitable — but that mitigation is an unversioned dashboard setting the repo cannot enforce, and the P11 migration that was supposed to remove the dependency demonstrably does not.

Kept at HIGH: a confirmed cross-tenant account-takeover to ADMIN using only a public key, live in every environment this repo builds, whose remediation migration falsely claims to have closed it config-independently. Not downgraded to a documentation nit because I executed a working exploit; not raised to BLOCKER because a correctly-configured production (reportedly the live state, and not this build) blocks it.

I reproduced the core claim myself against the live local backend. config.toml:319 (and a duplicate at :378) `enable_confirmations = false` confirmed. Sequence with real keys from .env.local: (1) service-key POST /auth/v1/invite created auth.users row with email_confirmed_at NULL (verified in psql); (2) anon-key-ONLY POST /auth/v1/signup with same email returned HTTP 200 {access_token, refresh_token, user} bound to the invitee's user id — verified the token authenticates as the invitee via GET /auth/v1/user (returns invitee id/email and a SET email_confirmed_at); (3) psql before/after shows email_confirmed_at NULL -> 2026-09-03T10:56:32 stamped purely by the anon signup, no link clicked. The final applied accept_organization_invitation is the P11 create-or-replace (migration 20260829380000) gating on `email_confirmed_at is not null`, and app.user_confirmed_email() = `select email from auth.users where id=auth.uid() and email_confirmed_at is not null` — both satisfied because GoTrue auto-stamps email_confirmed_at when confirmations are off. So the migration comment at lines 34 and 110 ("holds regardless of what enable_confirmations is set to") is demonstrably false. role check `in ('ADMIN','MEMBER')` confirms ADMIN is invitable. Two caveats that do not refute: the finding's "attacker-chosen password"/"account is gone" is imprecise — step 5 showed encrypted_password stays empty after signup and step 6's password grant returned invalid_credentials, so the password is NOT durably set; but the attacker holds the live session+refresh token returned by signup, which suffices. And I could not live-run the ADMIN-grant leg because the local public schema was absent (another agent mid-reset; only auth schema present), so that leg rests on the applied migration source plus the finding's rolled-back transaction rather than my own live grant. I deleted both probe users via admin API and verified 0 remaining. The central technical claim — anon-key signup on an invited unconfirmed user yields a confirmed session and defeats the email-confirmation gate — is correct.

I reproduced the GoTrue half exactly, then found that three of the finding's load-bearing claims are false and that the root cause is an already-tracked, already-documented item that this release candidate does not touch.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (the mechanism is real, on a confirmations-off stack):
Live against local, throwaway address, user deleted and deletion verified afterwards.
- POST /auth/v1/invite (service key) -> id bbb35c76-cb68-4d7b-8dad-cfd203e75964; psql `select id,email,email_confirmed_at,invited_at from auth.users where email='refute-probe-973@example.com'` -> `bbb35c76-...|refute-probe-973@example.com||2026-09-03 10:56:01.491214+00` (email_confirmed_at NULL).
- POST /auth/v1/signup with ONLY the anon key, attacker password -> `HTTP/1.1 200`, `Sb-Auth-User-Id: bbb35c76-cb68-4d7b-8dad-cfd203e75964`, a full access_token/refresh_token, and `"email_confirmed_at":"2026-09-03T10:56:10.001087641Z"` — 9 s after the invite, no link clicked.
- Cleanup: DELETE /auth/v1/admin/users/bbb35c76-... -> 200; `select count(*) from auth.users where id='bbb35c76-...'` -> 0.
So yes: with `enable_confirmations = false` (supabase/config.toml:319, unchanged since commit 9766997), the public signup endpoint hands back a session on a pending invitee's own user id and stamps email_confirmed_at.

CAVEAT ON WHAT I COULD NOT RE-RUN: the local database's application schema is currently empty — `select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> 0, and `select count(*) from information_schema.routines where routine_schema='app'` -> 0 (another agent appears to be mid-reset; `public.organizations` does not exist). I therefore could not re-execute the downstream accept_organization_invitation chain live. I read it instead: supabase/migrations/20260829380000_...sql:131 (`lower(email) = lower(coalesce(app.user_confirmed_email(), ''))`) and :205-215 (the RPC's `where auth.users.id = auth.uid() and email_confirmed_at is not null`). The chain does follow logically once email_confirmed_at is set, so I am not disputing that half.

WHY THE FINDING DOES NOT SURVIVE AS STATED:

1. "That claim is false" (migration:34 / :110) — it is not. The literal statement is that *an unconfirmed user's* email claim is worthless for this authorization no matter how Auth is configured, and that is exactly what app.user_confirmed_email() enforces. What the finder actually demonstrated is a different proposition (confirmations-off makes users confirmed cheaply), which the repository states plainly itself, in the authoritative release document: docs/plans/P13_RELEASE_READINESS_REPORT.md:577 — "GoTrue stamps it at signup with zero verification when confirmations are disabled."

2. "not described anywhere in the S3 write-up" — S3 is not just described, it is triaged. P13_RELEASE_READINESS_REPORT.md:724 carries it inside **Bucket B — HIGH, must fix before release**, status "Documented, not code-fixed (`d4dd505`)", and docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md §5 (lines 269-303) carries it as four checkbox-tracked pre-go-live requirements plus an explicit instruction not to "fix" config.toml because "it was never the actual gap." The org-takeover consequence is inherent in that finding: to exploit a vacuous confirmed-email gate you must hold a session bearing the invitee's address, which is the takeover. The only increment here is that it also works when an auth.users row already exists.

3. "no test in this repository can ever exercise or regress-detect the confirmed-email gate" — false, and this is the mitigation the finder looked at and misread. tests/integration/organizations-isolation.test.ts:748-900 ("the onboarding RPC rejects a caller whose email was never confirmed, and accepts the same caller once it is") creates a genuinely unconfirmed user via the admin API, mints a raw session JWT precisely so the gate is exercised at the Postgres layer independent of any grant flow, asserts rejection with no organization/membership/audit row left behind (`expect(orgAfterRejection).toHaveLength(0)`), then confirms the same user and asserts `membership?.role === "OWNER"`. Both sides, on every run, regardless of enable_confirmations. That test's own comment (lines 731-736) already records the exact GoTrue fact the finder presents as new: the flag "only auto-confirms the ordinary public signUp flow; it does not relax the login check for a user left unconfirmed any other way."

4. Not exploitable where it would matter, and not new in this RC. Production is verified confirmations-on: P13_RELEASE_READINESS_REPORT.md:2687 and :2984 (`mailer_autoconfirm: false` — "not weakened"), corroborated behaviourally at :1570-1578 by a live `over_email_send_rate_limit` on the hosted Auth API, and :1597 states no production Auth setting was weakened for the verification users. `git log -1 -- supabase/migrations/20260829380000_...` -> `4930269 fix(p11): mandatory security review...` — the gate is P11 code already deployed; config.toml's last touch is `9766997`. This branch introduces nothing here.

Net: the mechanism is real on a dev/CI stack, the finding's three supporting claims are wrong, and the root cause is an already-open, already-HIGH, checkbox-tracked owner item rather than a newly discovered release blocker. The one residual worth keeping is small: the migration's COMMENT at :110 reads as though the Auth setting no longer matters at all, which is materially misleading next to what P13 §16.6 says — a documentation overclaim, not a HIGH vulnerability in this candidate.

title: Offboarding or demoting an administrator does not revoke the invitations they issued — a removed admin's pending ADMIN invitation stays acceptable and mints a fresh ADMIN membership
exploit: A departing or compromised ADMIN, before losing access, invites an address they control (or a confederate's) at role ADMIN. The organization then removes or deactivates them, or demotes them to MEMBER — every action the product offers for offboarding. None of those touches organization_invitations. Up to seven days later (or forever, see the expires_at finding), the invitation is accepted and the attacker holds a fresh ADMIN membership in an organization that believes it has revoked their access.
impact: Offboarding is not complete. The organization's own Team screen does list pending invitations, so an attentive admin can spot and revoke the planted row — but nothing forces that, nothing warns, and no audit event links the removal to the orphaned invitation. The re-entered account is ADMIN: full read of the org's shipments, emissions, producers' shared verified data, and the ability to file declarations. Own-tenant scope, but it is precisely the boundary the removal action exists to enforce.
freshEnvironment: Yes. This is a property of the migration-defined schema and the application service, with no dependency on grants, seeds, restores or accumulated data — accept_organization_invitation()'s body carries no inviter re-check in the source file, and I confirmed the live function definition matches. The probe built the entire scenario (org, memberships, invitation) from scratch inside its own transaction, so it reproduces identically on a database built by db reset, restore or CI.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by my own independent reproduction. I could not use the shared local `postgres` DB (another agent had left `public` with 0 tables: `select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> 0, and `accept_organization_invitation` did not exist). So I built a fresh database, which made this a stronger fresh-environment test than the original: `create database advrev_refute_inv`, minimal auth/storage stubs, then all 74 `supabase/migrations/*.sql` applied in order (only failure: `20260827110000_activate_definitive_regulatory_dataset.sql`, needs the regulatory seed data — irrelevant here), then `supabase/seed.sql` applied in full so the `authenticated` role had exactly the grants a real environment has. Database dropped afterwards; repo untouched.

SOURCE CHECKS (all re-done, not taken on trust):
1. `supabase/migrations/20260828130000_organization_invitations.sql:73-76` — `invited_by uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete restrict`. The invitation has NO foreign key to `memberships`, so deleting a membership cannot cascade it. Only `org_id` cascades (from `organizations`).
2. `grep -rn "invited_by" supabase/migrations/*.sql` returns exactly two non-comment hits: the column definition (`:73`) and `and invited_by = auth.uid()` in the INSERT policy (`:148`). `invited_by` is never read again anywhere in the schema.
3. `accept_organization_invitation()`'s current body is `supabase/migrations/20260829380000_p11_review_email_confirmation_and_invitation_hardening.sql:178-330`. I read it in full. It checks: auth.uid() present; caller's email confirmed and matching; not ACCEPTED; PENDING; `expires_at >= now()`; no existing membership (deactivated -> MEMBERSHIP_DEACTIVATED). Then `insert into public.memberships (org_id, user_id, role) values (v_invite.org_id, auth.uid(), v_invite.role)`. No re-check of the inviter. No migration after `20260829380000` redefines it (I listed all 41 later files; the only later mentions, in `20260903130000` and `20260903190000`, are comments). Live confirmation in my fresh DB: `select prosrc ... where proname='accept_organization_invitation' | grep -c invited_by` -> 0.
4. No trigger: `select ... from pg_trigger t join pg_class c ... where c.relname='organization_invitations' and not tgisinternal` -> `(none)`.
5. Application layer: `src/application/organizations/manage-membership.ts` exports `changeMemberRole` (:85), `removeMember` (:193), `deactivateMember` (:292), `reactivateMember` (:424); `grep -n "organization_invitations\|invitation"` on that file returns one unrelated comment at :339. `app/team/actions.ts`'s `removeMemberAction` (:332) and `deactivateMemberAction` (:416) call only `removeMember`/`deactivateMember` — never `revokeInvitation`, which exists and is only wired to `revokeInvitationAction` (:695).
6. Reachability of the ADMIN-role invite: `app/team/actions.ts:566` `role: z.enum(["ADMIN","MEMBER"])`, and the RLS insert policy (`20260828130000:139-151`) requires only `app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(org_id) and invited_by = auth.uid() and status='PENDING'` — no restriction on the invited role, no check that the address isn't the inviter's own or an existing member's.

LIVE PROBE A (remove path), inside `begin; ... rollback;`, with the invitation created THROUGH RLS as the rogue ADMIN (`set local role authenticated`, claims sub=2222...):
  STEP1 ADMIN invite via RLS as ADMIN | 1
  STEP2 rogue memberships left | 0        (deactivated, then deleted)
  STEP2 invitation | PENDING | unexpired=true
  STEP3 accept (as attacker 3333..., confirmed email) | OK | aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000aa
  STEP4 | 33333333-... | ADMIN   <- new ADMIN minted by a non-member's invitation
  STEP4 | 11111111-... | OWNER
  POST-ROLLBACK org / attacker memberships / invitations -> 0 / 0 / 0

LIVE PROBE B (deactivate-only — the path `deactivateMember`'s own doc comment calls "what master plan §14 actually calls offboarding"):
  inviter deactivated? | true
  inviter still admin_or_owner? | false      (app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of -> false)
  accept after DEACTIVATE-only | OK | aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ab
  final memberships: 3333... ADMIN, 1111... OWNER (plus the deactivated inviter row)
So even when the inviter is provably no longer an admin by the schema's own predicate, their invitation still mints ADMIN.

SEVERITY: I am downgrading HIGH -> MEDIUM. The mechanism is real and reachable end-to-end through the sanctioned UI, but the exploit requires pre-meditation by an already-trusted ADMIN/OWNER (planting the invitation before offboarding) plus a second mailbox they control; the accept-time `expires_at < now()` check is genuinely enforced (I saw the EXPIRED branch at `20260829380000:252-258`), bounding the window to the 7-day default absent the separate expiry finding; the pending invitation is listed and revocable on /team; and the outcome is persistence at a privilege the actor already held, not escalation or a cross-tenant break. It is a genuine incomplete-offboarding defect, not a HIGH-severity boundary break.

I tried to refute this and could not; every technical claim checks out against the source of truth.

1. The quoted grep is accurate. `grep -rn "organization_invitations\|invitation" src/application/organizations/manage-membership.ts` returns exactly one line — `339:  // domain refuses. Same reasoning as accept_sharing_grant_invitation's` — an unrelated comment. The four mutators in that file are `changeMemberRole` (src/application/organizations/manage-membership.ts:85), `removeMember` (:193), `deactivateMember` (:292), `reactivateMember` (:424); I read removeMember's full body (:193-282) — fetch memberships, run `removeMembership` invariant, DELETE ... .select("id"), record `membership.removed` audit event, return OK. Nothing touches organization_invitations.

2. The server-action layer does not compensate. `app/team/actions.ts:332` `removeMemberAction` (read in full, :332-395) does rate limit -> parse -> getCurrentOrgSummary -> `removeMember` -> revalidatePath("/team"). `revokeInvitation` is imported at app/team/actions.ts:30 but only ever called from `revokeInvitationAction` (:746). Same for `deactivateMemberAction` (:416) — grep for "invitation" in that file hits only the invite/revoke actions (:594 onward), never the removal/deactivation/role-change paths. The accept UI does not gate either: app/accept-invitation/actions.ts calls `acceptInvitation` with no inviter check, and `acceptInvitation` (src/application/organizations/invitations.ts:362) is a bare `supabase.rpc("accept_organization_invitation", ...)` passthrough (:366-380).

3. The RPC body claim is correct, and 20260829380000 is genuinely the last definition. `grep -rn "create or replace function public.accept_organization_invitation" supabase/migrations/*.sql` returns only three hits: 20260828130000:173, 20260829360000:728, 20260829380000:178 — no later migration redefines it (the hits in 20260829460000, 20260831100000 and 20260903130000 are comments only, lines 33/45/30). I read the whole 20260829380000 §4 body: it checks auth.uid() non-null, `email_confirmed_at is not null` on the caller, invitation exists, email match, status ACCEPTED/non-PENDING, `expires_at < now()`, existing/deactivated membership — then unconditionally `insert into public.memberships (org_id, user_id, role) values (v_invite.org_id, auth.uid(), v_invite.role)`. `invited_by` is never read anywhere in the function. It is SECURITY DEFINER, so memberships RLS does not intervene.

4. No trigger compensates. `grep -rn "create trigger" supabase/migrations/*.sql` returns 24 triggers; none is on organization_invitations, and the two on memberships (memberships_prevent_user_id_change_trg 20260829370000:92, memberships_prevent_org_id_change_trg 20260829420000:49, plus memberships_enforce_last_active_owner_trg 20260829570000:126) are immutability/last-owner guards that never look at invitations.

Live re-run of the probe was not possible right now: the local cluster is currently unmigrated. `PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 54322 -U postgres -d postgres -tAc "select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public';"` -> `0`; `select pg_get_functiondef('public.accept_organization_invitation(uuid)'::regprocedure)` -> `ERROR: function "public.accept_organization_invitation(uuid)" does not exist`; `select version ... from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` -> `ERROR: relation "supabase_migrations.schema_migrations" does not exist`. I did not reset or otherwise modify anything (checked three times over several minutes; it is another session's state, presumably mid-reset). This does not weaken the finding — its mechanism is entirely in migration-defined DDL and application source, both of which I read directly, and the finding's own fresh-environment claim is therefore sound.

One correction to the finding's framing, not its substance: severity. The precondition is an actor who was already ADMIN and acted maliciously before offboarding — someone who could already read and exfiltrate everything the re-entered ADMIN account can. The incremental harm is persistence past removal, bounded by the default 7-day expiry, in-tenant only, and the planted row is visible and revocable on the Team screen (invitations.ts:251 revokeInvitation). That is a real offboarding-completeness defect but reads as MEDIUM rather than HIGH; the "forever" framing depends on the separate expires_at finding, which I did not evaluate here.

I could not refute it. I searched for a mitigation everywhere the finder did not look (later migrations, triggers, FK cascades, RLS, application layer, tests, audit docs) and then reproduced it from scratch in a freshly built database.

MITIGATION SEARCH (all negative):
1. Later redefinitions: `grep -rn "create or replace function public.accept_organization_invitation" supabase/migrations/` -> only 20260828130000:173, 20260829360000:728, 20260829380000:178. The last is the live body (supabase/migrations/20260829380000_p11_review_email_confirmation_and_invitation_hardening.sql lines 178-329): it validates auth.uid() not null, confirmed-email match, ACCEPTED/NOT_PENDING, `expires_at < now()`, existing/deactivated membership, then `insert into public.memberships (org_id,user_id,role) values (v_invite.org_id, auth.uid(), v_invite.role)` at lines 288-297. `invited_by` is never read.

LIVE RE-RUN ON A FRESH SCHEMA. The local dev DB at 54322 was empty when I started (`select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> 0; supabase_migrations.schema_migrations did not exist -- another session had it mid-reset), so I built my own throwaway: `create database advrev_refute`, minimal auth stub (auth.users, auth.uid/jwt/role), then applied all 74 supabase/migrations/*.sql in order. Probe A (deactivate, then hard-remove the inviter), real psql transaction, rolled back:
  inviter memberships remaining | 0
  invitation after offboarding  | PENDING expires 2026-09-10 11:00:19.544304+00
  set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims sub=695b612c-...-03 (attacker@example.com, email_confirmed_at set)
  accept RPC | OK | aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-000000000001
  membership minted | 695b612c-...-03 | ADMIN
  membership minted | 88150c48-...-01 | OWNER
  POST-ROLLBACK probe org rows | 0

Probe B (demotion only, ADMIN -> MEMBER, no removal):

  accept after inviter demoted | OK | aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-000000000002
  membership minted | 695b612c-...-13 | ADMIN

Expiry IS enforced at accept time (20260829380000 lines 249-256), so the persistence window is the 7-day default, not unbounded. title: /reset-password changes the account password for ANY live session with no re-authentication and no current password, then signs the victim's other sessions out
evidence:
app/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx is a plain page under app/(auth)/, whose layout (app/(auth)/layout.tsx) contains no session or recovery-scope guard of any kind. app/(auth)/reset-password/actions.ts:157 reads `await supabase.auth.getUser()` and, on any non-null user, calls `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password })` at line 168 — there is no old-password field in reset-password-form.tsx, no AAL/AMR check, no recovery-session check, and no reauthentication nonce. Line 213 then calls `supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: "others" })`. supabase/config.toml:321 `secure_password_change = false`.

Live against the local Auth service (throwaway user, deleted afterwards, deletion verified as 0 leftover):
  POST /auth/v1/signup  -> access_token (939 chars) for advrev-pw-1788431566@example.com
  PUT  /auth/v1/user  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that token>"  -d '{"password":"AttackerPass456"}'
    -> HTTP 200 {"id":"1e99e76d-a27c-4dd6-8d7d-460ec3874d3d","email":"advrev-pw-1788431566@example.com",...}
  POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with the NEW password
    -> HTTP 200, access_token returned
No current password and no recent-login proof was supplied at any point.
exploit: Attacker obtains a live session cookie (borrowed/unlocked browser, a shared machine where someone did not sign out, an exfiltrated cookie). They navigate to /reset-password on the real origin, type a new password twice, submit. updatePasswordAction sees a non-null getUser() and changes the password; it then calls signOut({scope:"others"}), terminating the genuine owner's sessions. The owner's old password no longer works and the attacker now holds the credential.
impact: Elevates transient session possession into permanent account takeover plus immediate lockout of the legitimate owner, with the product's own signOut({scope:"others"}) doing the locking-out. Scope is one account, but that account may be an org OWNER. Honest bound: the GoTrue half depends on secure_password_change, which is false in the config this repo ships and is a dashboard setting in production that I did not and must not probe. The application half — a /reset-password screen reachable by any authenticated session with no old-password field — is unconditional and would additionally break the invite→set-password flow if secure_password_change were ever turned on, since the app never sends a reauthentication nonce.
freshEnvironment: Yes for the application half: app/(auth)/layout.tsx and reset-password/actions.ts have no guard in any build, and the route is statically part of the app. The GoTrue half survives any environment built from supabase/config.toml (line 321), which is what db reset / supabase start use; on a hosted project it depends on that project's own setting, which I deliberately did not touch or query.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent re-check; could not refute on the reachability lens.

REACHABILITY (the lens): the route is statically part of the app and nothing guards it.
- app/(auth)/layout.tsx: renders only <Wordmark/> and {children}. No session/recovery/AAL guard. Confirmed by reading the whole file.
- The strongest refutation candidate was middleware. There is no middleware.ts source (find returns only .next build artifacts). This Next.js version renames it to proxy.ts (proxy.ts:10-14 doc comment: "Named `proxy.ts` per Next.js 16 (the `middleware.ts` file convention is deprecated as of v16.0.0 and renamed to `proxy`)"). proxy.ts:126-133 matcher "/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)" DOES cover /reset-password, but the body (proxy.ts:30-124) only builds a cookie-adapter client and calls `await supabase.auth.getUser();` (line 121) to refresh the session, then `return response`. It is a session refresher, not an authorization gate. Refutation path fails.
- app/(auth)/reset-password/actions.ts:155-165 gates ONLY on getUser() being non-null; :167-172 calls supabase.auth.updateUser({password}); :212-215 calls supabase.auth.signOut({scope:"others"}). All three cited line numbers are exact.
- No old-password input in reset-password-form.tsx (read in full: only `password` and `confirmPassword`). `grep -rni "currentPassword|oldPassword|current password|old password" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx app components src` returns ZERO non-test hits, so there is no alternative properly-guarded change-password screen; /reset-password is the product's only password-setting surface. Capability required = "hold a live session", the ordinary state of every logged-in user. Reachable.

LIVE HALF re-run independently (throwaway user refute-n6-1479@example.com, deleted afterwards, `select count(*) ... = 0` verified; other agents' rows untouched):
  POST /auth/v1/signup -> access_token (923 chars)
  PUT /auth/v1/user -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"password":"AttackerPass456"}' -> HTTP=200, body returns the user id/email. No current password, no reauth nonce supplied.
  POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password (NEW password) -> HTTP=200
  POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password (ORIGINAL password) -> HTTP=400 {"code":400,"error_code":"invalid_credentials","msg":"Invalid login credentials"}
Confirms the password genuinely changed, not merely a 200.

Verified at the RUNNING SERVICE, not just the config file:
  docker inspect supabase_auth_snowkap-cbam -> GOTRUE_SECURITY_UPDATE_PASSWORD_REQUIRE_REAUTHENTICATION=false
matching supabase/config.toml:321 `secure_password_change = false`.

FRESH-ENVIRONMENT DURABILITY (this review's core failure class): holds. The application half depends on no database state at all - layout.tsx, proxy.ts and actions.ts have no guard in any build. The GoTrue half derives from supabase/config.toml:321, which is in-repo and applied by `supabase start`/`db reset`, so every freshly built environment has it false. Unlike the seed/grant class, this is not an artifact of this particular database.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING'S FRAMING (both reduce novelty, not validity):
1. Already disclosed by the implementer: docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:968 lists N.6 "/reset-password accepts any live session without re-authentication", classed HIGH RISK, "No; mitigated by enabling secure_password_change hosted", and owner decision #8 names hosted Auth config. The implementer never claimed this was safe, so this contradicts no audit claim.
2. The stated mitigation is only PARTIAL, which the finding under-weights in its favour: supabase/config.toml:320's own comment reads "users need to reauthenticate OR HAVE LOGGED IN RECENTLY to change their password". The borrowed-unlocked-browser case (victim signed in minutes ago) still satisfies "logged in recently", so enabling the hosted setting does not fully close the primary exploit path. The finding's separate caveat is also correct: the app sends no reauthentication nonce anywhere, so enabling it would risk the invite/recovery set-password flow.

SEVERITY: MEDIUM as claimed is right. Downward pressure: requires the attacker to already hold a live session, at which point they already have full in-app access to that account's org data; the marginal gain is persistence past session expiry. Upward pressure: the product's own signOut({scope:"others"}) at actions.ts:213 actively converts session possession into owner lockout, and the account may be an org OWNER. Not HIGH because prior session compromise is a real precondition; not LOW because the app amplifies the consequence itself.

Production hosted setting not probed (correctly out of bounds); the local/fresh-environment finding stands without it.

I tried to refute this on four independent fronts and failed on all four. Every cited line is exact and the live behavior reproduces.

CODE CITATIONS — all verified line-exact (cat -n):
- app/(auth)/layout.tsx: read in full (35 lines). It is a presentational flex container rendering `<Wordmark/>` + `{children}`. No session check, no recovery-scope check, no redirect. Confirmed.
- app/(auth)/reset-password/actions.ts:157 `} = await supabase.auth.getUser();` (destructuring opens at 155). :159 `if (!user)` returns an error; ANY non-null user proceeds. Confirmed.

MY BEST REFUTATION ATTEMPT — a middleware guard redirecting signed-in users away from (auth) routes. There is no middleware.ts (Glob: "No files found"). This Next.js version renames it to proxy.ts, which exists at the repo root. I read all 134 lines: it constructs a server client and calls `await supabase.auth.getUser()` at :121 solely to refresh the cookie, then `return response`. There is zero redirect or branching logic, and config.matcher :132 matches everything. No guard exists. Refutation failed.

Second attempt — a reauth/AAL check elsewhere: `grep -rni "reauthenticat|aal2?|amr|nonce"` across app/ src/ components/ lib/ (excluding tests) returned nothing. Refutation failed.

LIVE REPRODUCTION (my own, local GoTrue at 127.0.0.1:54321; /auth/v1/settings confirmed disable_signup:false, mailer_autoconfirm:true):
1. POST /auth/v1/signup, password OrigPass123 -> access_token, 923 chars.
2. PUT /auth/v1/user -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"password":"AttackerPass456"}' -> HTTP 200, body `{"id":"d3540c4b-fe7b-44c8-ab9a-6611113125c2","aud":"authenticated","role":"authenticated","email":"refute-pw-1406@example.com",...}`. No current password, no recent-login proof supplied.
3. POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with AttackerPass456 -> HTTP 200, access_token present.
4. STEP THE ORIGINAL FINDING DID NOT RUN — sign in with the ORIGINAL password -> HTTP 400 `{"code":400,"error_code":"invalid_credentials","msg":"Invalid login credentials"}`. The legitimate owner's credential is dead. This confirms the lockout half concretely, and actions.ts:213's `signOut({scope:"others"})` kills their live sessions on top of it, so the product itself completes the takeover.

THE PROJECT ALREADY KNOWS. This is not a novel discovery, which strengthens rather than weakens it:
- docs/plans/P13_RELEASE_READINESS_REPORT.md §45.4: "Confirmed real and upgraded from LOW to MEDIUM: /reset-password is the product's only password-write path, so it doubles as the change-password flow, and it requires no current password while gating on any session rather than specifically a recovery session." It records the fix as "specified and ready" but "Deliberately not fixed in this round" because the owner was mid-test on that exact flow.
- docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:968 lists it as N.6, class HIGH RISK, unfixed, mitigation "enabling secure_password_change hosted".
So the finding independently rediscovered an issue the release audit itself carries as open. MEDIUM matches the project's own considered rating in P13 §45.4; I keep it there rather than raising it, because exploitation requires prior possession of a live session and crosses no tenancy boundary — the incremental harm is durable persistence plus owner lockout, not new data access.

FRESH-ENVIRONMENT LENS (the seed/grant failure class I was told to hunt): this finding is immune to it. Nothing here depends on database state, migration ordering, or grants. The app half is source code (layout.tsx, actions.ts, reset-password-form.tsx) present in every build; the GoTrue half comes from supabase/config.toml:321, which `supabase start` applies to any freshly built local or CI environment. The finding's own bound is honest and correct: the hosted production setting is a dashboard value it did not probe, and I did not probe it either.

CLEANUP / DISCLOSURE. I created one throwaway local auth user and deleted it via the admin API (DELETE HTTP 200), scoped to exactly the UUID d3540c4b-fe7b-44c8-ab9a-6611113125c2 returned by my own signup. Verified: `select count(*) from auth.users where email like 'refute-pw-%'` -> 0, and `where id='d3540c4b-...'` -> 0. Separately and transparently: total auth.users read 2 before my probe and 1 immediately after, then 0 on three samples two seconds apart. I issued no delete other than my own UUID; the two pre-existing rows were removed concurrently by another process in this workspace (E2E runs, consistent with the .next-e2e and test-results directories). I am flagging the discrepancy rather than burying it, but it is not attributable to my probe. No production system was touched and no repo file was modified.

I could not refute it; every element re-verified independently.

LIVE RE-RUN (local GoTrue v2.195.0; `select count(*) from auth.users` = 0 before):
  POST /auth/v1/signup -> access_token, 923 chars, user b07d43c6-a264-4856-8b99-fa5c9b2b3010
  PUT /auth/v1/user -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"password":"AttackerPass456"}' -> HTTP 200
