The same old file maps insertError.code === "42501" to reason "SHIPMENT_NOT_EDITABLE", and app/(importer)/shipments/[id]/actions.ts renders that as "This shipment is locked or void and can no longer be recalculated." A revoked table privilege raises 42501, so the failure presents as a plausible-but-false domain message rather than an error -- it would not read as an outage to a user or to whoever is watching the window.

RUNBOOKS CONFIRMED. docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md step 4 is "Dry run, then push" (supabase db push) and step 6 is "Only then deploy the application" -- the mandated order does put the new schema in front of the old code. ROLLBACK.md:163 scopes the safe case as "a new RLS policy that doesn't remove a capability the old code relies on" and :171 defines destructive as "(dropped or renamed a column/table the old code reads or writes, tightened a constraint the old code's writes would now violate)". A dropped policy plus a revoked grant is named in neither list.

PARTIAL MITIGATION THE FINDING DOES NOT CREDIT (why I downgrade rather than confirm at HIGH). Two pieces of existing guidance cover this class generically. (1) DEPLOYMENT.md's "Promoting a migration to production" preamble states outright: "'The migration is inert until the code lands' is not true in general and must never be assumed," and its step 3 requires rehearsing the rollback before anything is pushed. (2) ROLLBACK.md's destructive bullet ends with the operative instruction: "Before rolling back application code past a destructive migration, explicitly confirm the target commit's code is still compatible with the current schema, not the schema as it existed when that commit was written," and its third bullet supplies the remedy mechanism (a new forward corrective migration). So "the runbook offers no compensating step" is overstated: the general check and the general remedy both exist; what is missing is the specific classification (grant revocation / policy drop as destructive) and any per-migration flag. grep -rn "not additive|deploy order|old code|removes a capability" over docs/ returns only ROLLBACK.md:163; 20260903190000 appears in no runbook, and the audit's section C pending-migration table (P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:537-549) lists nine migrations and omits both P14.1 ones, so nothing in the release record flags this migration as capability-removing.

SCOPE OF HARM. Bounded: a manually supervised, owner-gated promotion window of minutes between steps 4 and 6, on one feature (Calculate), with no data loss and no security exposure -- the direction of the change is strictly tightening. The rollback trap is conditional on a rollback actually being taken, and is escapable by a forward re-grant migration (at the cost of reopening the P14.1 hole). That is a real operations/documentation gap worth fixing before promotion, not a HIGH.

WHAT I COULD NOT RE-RUN. No live probe: the local Postgres at 127.0.0.1:54322 currently has an empty public schema ("select schemaname||'.'||tablename from pg_tables where schemaname not in ('pg_catalog','information_schema')" returns only auth/realtime/storage/vault rows, and supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist), so another agent has reset it and I did not rebuild it. The finding is a property of the migration text, the pre-P14.1 source in git, and the two runbooks, all of which I read directly -- no database state was needed to confirm it.

title: The comparator is the sole programmatic acceptance test for recovery and is itself covered by nothing: no CI job, no npm script, no test
evidence:
`grep -rn "compare-database-posture" --include=*.yml --include=*.yaml --include=*.json --include=*.ts --include=*.mjs` over the repository returns exactly one file: scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs itself. It appears in prose in BACKUP_RESTORE.md:520-530 and DEPLOYMENT.md:574 and nowhere in .github/workflows/ci.yml or package.json's scripts.

Its self-checks have now been wrong three times: the `auth.users` FK check that counted Supabase's internal FKs (fixed in aa394ba), the self-checks that passed on an empty project, and the three independent holes in this report (findings 1, 3, 4). BACKUP_RESTORE.md:642 nevertheless states 'the acceptance test is now programmatic and demonstrably catches the exact failure the old one missed.'
exploit: NONE -- structural. There is no fixture database, no expected-output snapshot, and no negative test that deliberately breaks a posture and asserts the tool notices. Every one of its 24 queries is validated only by having been run once, by hand, against one database.
impact: A tool whose entire job is to be right during a recovery, when nobody has time to audit it, and whose correctness is asserted in the runbook rather than tested. Each of its checks encodes a lesson from a real incident; nothing stops the next edit from re-introducing an exact-zero threshold or a `relkind='r'` filter, and nothing would notice.
freshEnvironment: Yes -- repository-level fact, verified by grep at the release-candidate commit.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by my own checks; I could not refute it.

(1) Repo-wide grep for "compare-database-posture" across ALL file types (excluding node_modules/.git) returns exactly: ./scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs, ./docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md, ./docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md, ./docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md, and one Turbopack cache blob (./.next-e2e/cache/...). No test, no workflow, no package script.

(2) package.json scripts block is: dev, build, postbuild, start, test, test:watch, test:e2e, typecheck, regulatory:verify. No ops entry.

(3) .github/workflows/ci.yml: `grep -n "scripts/"` returns only lines 220, 228, 297, 301, 529, all scripts/regulatory/*.py. `grep -n "scripts/ops\|posture"` returns nothing. CI never invokes it.

(4) `find tests -path "*ops*"` -> empty. No test file in the 22 vitest suites references it.

(5) BACKUP_RESTORE.md:642 verbatim: "the acceptance test is now programmatic and demonstrably catches the exact failure the old one missed." Confirmed by sed -n '630,650p'.

(6) `git show aa394ba` confirms the third-wrongness claim in the tool's own words: "That is the same vacuous pass this file was written to stop, occurring in the file written to stop it."

NEW EVIDENCE strengthening the finding (not in the original report). I ran the tool read-only against the local backend:
  node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres"
Output: 3 CRITICAL failures (auth_user_foreign_keys_present, policy_functions_resolve, api_roles_hold_their_grants) but [OK] for tables_without_rls, rls_without_policies, tables_without_insert_policy, truncate_granted_to_api_roles, security_definer_without_search_path -- on a database with NO application schema at all. Verified independently: `select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='public'` -> 0, and `select count(*) from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` -> ERROR: relation does not exist. So 5 of the 9 "positive assertion" self-checks still pass vacuously on an empty database, which is precisely the defect class P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md section C.3 claims was eliminated by rewriting them as positive assertions. The aggregate verdict is still correct here (POSTURE DIFFERS) because the three genuinely-positive checks fail, so this is not a live false pass -- but it shows the vacuous surface is real, and nothing in the repository would detect its return.

REACHABILITY (the lens I was told to apply): both actor paths are real and require no capability nobody has. (a) An operator during recovery: BACKUP_RESTORE.md:520-530, 633, 645 and DEPLOYMENT.md:574 name this tool as THE acceptance test, and BACKUP_RESTORE.md:645 makes `POSTURE MATCHES` the outstanding proof-of-recovery criterion. (b) A future editor: no gate exists, so a regression to an exact-zero threshold or a relkind filter ships silently. The remediation is also demonstrably feasible, not theoretical: ci.yml already starts a disposable local Supabase stack for the isolation suites, so `--check` against that DSN would be a working gate. It simply does not exist.

Minor imprecisions in the finding, immaterial to its correctness: the tool has 23 checks (14 comparison in CHECKS at line 52, 9 in SELF_CHECKS at line 252), not 24; and it also appears at BACKUP_RESTORE.md:633 and :645 and at four places in P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md, not only the two lines cited.

Severity: MEDIUM is fair and I am leaving it. It is not a shipped-product defect and has no exploit, which argues for LOW; but it is the sole programmatic gate on disaster recovery of a regulatory compliance database, its own history shows two documented self-check failures, and its grant-related self-checks (api_roles_hold_their_grants, truncate_granted_to_api_roles) are exactly the detector for this review's headline failure class -- an untested detector for the class the release already got wrong once.

I re-ran every piece of evidence independently at HEAD = 0679e60d6ffdaec24718c584570dcedb9637aa46 (confirmed via git rev-parse). The finding's core structural claim is CORRECT.

1. The grep, re-run by me verbatim: `grep -rn "compare-database-posture" --include=*.yml --include=*.yaml --include=*.json --include=*.ts --include=*.mjs .` returns exactly 4 hits, all inside scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs itself (lines 22, 23, 515, 516 — its own usage/help strings). No .yml, .json, or .ts file anywhere references it. CONFIRMED.

2. No npm script: package.json's `scripts` block contains exactly dev, build, postbuild, start, test, test:watch, test:e2e, typecheck, regulatory:verify. None invoke the comparator. CONFIRMED.

3. No CI job: `.github/` contains only `workflows/ci.yml`. `grep -rn "scripts/ops" .github/` returns nothing. `grep -n "scripts/" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns only regulatory-pipeline invocations (lines 220, 228, 297, 301, 529 — scripts/regulatory/*.py). CONFIRMED.

4. No test: `scripts/ops/` contains exactly one file, the comparator. `grep -rn "scripts/ops\|posture" tests/` returns only three unrelated prose uses of the word "posture" in comments (calculation-reproduction.test.ts:667, organizations-isolation.test.ts:580 and :2366). vitest.config.ts defines no include glob covering scripts/. There is no fixture DB, no snapshot, no negative test. CONFIRMED.

5. Doc citations are accurate: BACKUP_RESTORE.md:520, 525, 530 and DEPLOYMENT.md:574 (file path is docs/runbooks/, which the finding abbreviated). The quoted runbook claim is real, at docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md:640-642: "the acceptance test is now programmatic and demonstrably catches the exact failure the old one missed." CONFIRMED.

6. The aa394ba history claim is real: `git show --stat aa394ba` = "fix(ops): the auth.users FK check passed on a database holding no schema", 13 insertions touching only compare-database-posture.mjs. CONFIRMED.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: (a) The script's `--check <dsn>` mode is not a self-test of the tool — it runs the 9 SELF_CHECKS against a database, so it validates a database's posture, not the comparator's own SQL. It cannot catch a regression in its own queries. (b) P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1449 claims the `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` self-check is "now enforced continuously," which would have refuted the coverage claim — but `grep -rn "truncate_granted\|has_table_privilege.*TRUNCATE\|'TRUNCATE'" tests/` returns zero hits, and the only case-insensitive "truncate" matches in tests/ are unrelated prose about numeric rounding. That audit claim does not correspond to any test.

ONE INACCURACY, immaterial: the finding says "24 queries." The actual count is 23 — 14 entries in CHECKS (schemas, tables, columns, rls_enabled, policy_definitions, effective_grants, schema_usage_grants, functions, function_grants, triggers, constraints, indexes, sequences, extensions) and 9 in SELF_CHECKS. Off by one; does not affect the substance.

SEVERITY CORRECTION to LOW. The structural gap is exactly as described, but MEDIUM overstates it: the comparator is an operator-run recovery aid, not shipped runtime code — it is in no product code path and has no exploit (the finding concedes this). Its failure mode is loud, not silent: it prints [DIFFER]/[FAIL] with the first twenty differing rows per check and exits non-zero. Critically, the finding quotes one clause out of a paragraph whose lead sentence (BACKUP_RESTORE.md:640) is "Recovery is **not proven**," and whose closing sentence records that a real restore returning POSTURE MATCHES "remains outstanding." The runbook is therefore substantially more honest than the finding's framing of "correctness asserted in the runbook rather than tested" implies — the overclaim is confined to the single word "demonstrably." The legitimate residue is real and worth fixing: 23 hand-validated queries guarding recovery, with nothing preventing a future edit from reintroducing an exact-zero threshold or a relkind filter.

CONFIRMED by independent re-verification at 0679e60 (clean tree). I could not find any mitigation.

1) Grep reproduced and widened. `git grep -n "compare-database-posture"` = 13 hits: scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:22,23,515,516 (its own usage strings); docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1388,1449,1717,2125; docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md:520,525,530,633,645; docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:574. All prose or self-reference. Zero invocations. The finder's extension filter was too narrow, so I re-ran without --include and against the git index; same result.

2) Not in CI. `.github/` contains exactly one tracked file, .github/workflows/ci.yml. `git grep -n "scripts/" -- .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns only scripts/regulatory lines (220, 228, 297, 301, 529). "scripts/ops" appears nowhere. CI runs pnpm typecheck, pnpm test (vitest), pnpm build, playwright, pnpm audit, secret scan.

3) Not in package.json. The scripts block has 9 entries (dev, build, postbuild, start, test, test:watch, test:e2e, typecheck, regulatory:verify); no ops entry. Notably postbuild DOES run scripts/build/assert-clean-production-artifact.mjs, so sibling scripts are wired into gates; this one uniquely is not.

4) MITIGATION LENS - searched and found nothing. (a) `git ls-files` shows zero *.test.ts/*.spec.ts under scripts/, while the repo colocates 100+ test files elsewhere (proxy.test.ts, lib/utils.test.ts, src/infrastructure/supabase/client.test.ts, app/**/actions.test.ts). vitest.config.ts uses the default include glob (it only sets `exclude: [...configDefaults.exclude, "tests/e2e/**"]`), so a colocated test under scripts/ would be picked up - none exists. (b) The underlying invariants are not independently covered either: `git grep -n "has_table_privilege\|relacl\|TRUNCATE"` over tests/ returns only unrelated string-truncation comments (tests/e2e/actual-data-determination.spec.ts:586, tests/integration/regulatory-resolution.test.ts:133,247, etc.). No test asserts grant or TRUNCATE posture. (c) No git hooks, husky, lefthook, Makefile, justfile, or any tracked .sh. (d) No self-test mode in the 614-line script: `process.argv` occurs once, at line 508, parsing only the two documented modes; no fixture, snapshot, or expected-output file.

5) Supporting claims verified. `git log -- scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs` shows exactly two commits, both self-check bug fixes: aa394ba "fix(ops): the auth.users FK check passed on a database holding no schema" (its own message: "That is the same vacuous pass this file was written to stop, occurring in the file written to stop it") and 06cea94. BACKUP_RESTORE.md ~641-643 does carry the quoted sentence "the acceptance test is now programmatic and demonstrably catches the exact failure the old one missed."

6) CORRECTION IN THE TOOL'S FAVOUR (does not refute). I ran it read-only: `node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres"` -> "RESULT: POSTURE DIFFERS -- 3 check(s) failed, 3 of them critical" (auth_user_foreign_keys_present, policy_functions_resolve, api_roles_hold_their_grants). This is NOT a tool bug: the local postgres DB is currently empty. `select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` -> 0; FKs in public/app -> 0; `select count(*) from information_schema.role_table_grants where grantee='anon' and table_schema='public'` -> 0; no app-schema functions. The rewritten positive checks correctly refused to pass vacuously on an empty database, i.e. aa394ba's fix demonstrably works. Also, the quoted BACKUP_RESTORE.md:642 sentence sits inside a section headed "Recovery is **not proven**", so the runbook overclaims less than the finding implies.

SEVERITY: lowered MEDIUM -> LOW. The structural gap is real and total, but: the script is an operator tool, not product code; it is not deployed, not on any runtime path, and reaches no user data; there is no exploit; its only consumer is a human running a documented drill who reads its output directly, so a regression surfaces at the next drill; and the runbook already labels recovery unproven and gates it behind an owner-authorised step. The legitimate concern that keeps it above INFO is the demonstrated recurrence of the vacuous-pass class in this very file (aa394ba), with nothing automated to catch the next instance.

title: seed.sql's revoke list is a hand-maintained mirror by its own admission, and it already fails to re-assert the narrowings it does not name: `anon` regains EXECUTE on seven SECURITY DEFINER RPCs migrations granted to `authenticated` alone
evidence:
supabase/seed.sql:21-23 does `grant all on all tables/sequences/functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role`, and :25-32 sets the matching default privileges. The 2026-09-03 (P14.3) block at :83-110 re-asserts exactly three things: calculation_results INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, `record_calculation_result` EXECUTE, and TRUNCATE. seed.sql:68-72 states the coupling plainly: 'These statements mirror the migrations named above and must be updated with them ... the alternative -- teaching this file which tables are special -- is a list that rots silently.'

It is already incomplete. Every one of these migrations grants EXECUTE to `authenticated` only:
  20260828080000:107  create_organization_with_owner -> authenticated
  20260828120000 / 20260829360000  list_org_members -> authenticated
  20260828130000 / 20260829380000  accept_organization_invitation -> authenticated
  20260829300000 / 20260829390000  accept_sharing_grant_invitation -> authenticated
  20260829310000  record_shared_data_consumption -> authenticated
  20260829330000  record_declaration_filed -> authenticated
  20260902150000  sharing_counterparty_org_names -> authenticated, service_role (deliberately not anon)

On the current local database, built by this repository's documented procedure:
  select proname, proacl from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='public' and proname in (...);
  -> accept_organization_invitation   ... authenticated=X/postgres anon=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  -> accept_sharing_grant_invitation  ... authenticated=X/postgres anon=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  -> create_organization_with_owner   ... authenticated=X/postgres anon=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  -> list_org_members                 ... authenticated=X/postgres anon=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  -> record_declaration_filed         ... authenticated=X/postgres anon=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  -> record_shared_data_consumption   ... authenticated=X/postgres anon=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres
  -> sharing_counterparty_org_names   ... authenticated=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres anon=X/postgres
  -> record_calculation_result        ... postgres=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres   <- the one that was fixed
exploit: Partial, and I am marking it as such. I probed the two most promising as `anon` inside a rolled-back transaction on the live local database and found no disclosure: `public.list_org_members('1b635dfb-...')` raised 'Not a member of this organization.' and `public.sharing_counterparty_org_names()` returned zero rows -- both scope through `app.user_org_ids()`, which is empty without `auth.uid()`. So the widening is currently absorbed by each function's own internal checks rather than by the grant. That is defence-in-depth lost, not a breach demonstrated.
impact: Two things. First, the concrete state: seven SECURITY DEFINER functions, several of which write (accept an invitation, record a declaration as FILED, record shared-data consumption), are callable over PostgREST RPC by an unauthenticated `anon` request in every environment built by `supabase db reset` -- which is CI's environment and every developer's. Their safety rests entirely on each body's own membership logic; the grant boundary the migrations wrote is gone. Second, and more important: this is direct evidence that the P14.3 fix repaired the three instances CI happened to catch rather than the mechanism, and that seed.sql's own predicted rot has already happened. The next revoke-based control added to a migration will decay the same way, silently. I have not verified the hosted project's ACLs, so I cannot say whether production shares this state.
freshEnvironment: This finding IS the fresh-environment state -- it is produced by `supabase db reset` running seed.sql last. Read from the current local database, which was built that way. Not verified against the hosted production project (I made no production queries).

verdicts.reasoning:
MECHANISM: CONFIRMED by my own experiment. I built a throwaway database in the local cluster and reproduced the exact idiom in isolation:

  create function public.f_test() returns int language sql as 'select 1';
  revoke all on function public.f_test() from public;
  grant execute on function public.f_test() to authenticated;
  -> AFTER MIGRATION: anon=false authenticated=true acl={postgres=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres}
  -- then supabase/seed.sql:20-23 verbatim:
  grant all on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;
  -> AFTER SEED: anon=true acl={postgres=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres,anon=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}

So seed.sql's blanket grant does re-widen EXECUTE to `anon` on functions the migrations restricted to `authenticated`, and the finding's list of migration sites is accurate (verified: 20260828080000:107-108, 20260828120000:77-78, 20260828130000:302-303, 20260829300000:627-628, 20260829310000:331-332, 20260829330000:1030-1031, 20260829360000:320-321, 20260829380000:348-349, 20260829390000:282-283, 20260902150000:194-196 — every one is `revoke all ... from public; grant execute ... to authenticated;`, which never names anon, so the blanket grant is not re-narrowed by seed.sql:83-110).

I could NOT re-run the finding's own ACL query: the local `postgres` database was empty for the whole session (`select count(*) ... nspname='public' and relkind='r'` -> 0; same for pg_proc -> 0; supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist), evidently mid/failed reset by another agent, and I am forbidden to run `supabase db reset`. So my reachability verdict rests on reading all seven bodies, not on live RPC probes.

REACHABILITY (the lens): REFUTED. All seven functions are SECURITY DEFINER and each carries its own first-statement caller guard, so an `anon` (unauthenticated, auth.uid() = null) caller gains nothing:
  - create_organization_with_owner (20260828080000): body line 4 is `if auth.uid() is null then raise exception 'create_organization_with_owner requires an authenticated caller.'` — before the INSERT.
  - accept_organization_invitation (20260829380000): first statement after BEGIN is the same `auth.uid() is null` raise.
  - accept_sharing_grant_invitation (20260829390000): same, first statement.
  - record_shared_data_consumption (20260829310000): same, first statement ('record_shared_data_consumption requires an authenticated caller.').
  - record_declaration_filed (20260829330000): same, first statement — before the `select ... for update`, so no lock, no read, no write.
  - list_org_members (20260829360000:271-289): first statement is `if not exists (select 1 from app.user_org_ids() as caller_org_id where caller_org_id = p_org_id) then raise exception 'Not a member of this organization.'` — and the raise is identical whether or not the org exists, so it is not an existence oracle either.
  - sharing_counterparty_org_names (20260902150000:196): pure SQL, every branch scoped by `sg.grantee_org_id in (select app.user_org_ids())` / `sg.grantor_org_id in (select app.user_org_ids())`.
And app.user_org_ids() (20260828070000) is `select org_id from public.memberships where user_id = auth.uid()` — with auth.uid() null that is `user_id = null`, which returns zero rows, not all rows. No null-matches-everything hole.

Note also that seed.sql grants only `in schema public`; the `app.*` helper functions keep their narrow `to authenticated` grants untouched.

Two further corrections to the claimed impact: (1) "every environment built by supabase db reset" excludes hosted production — seed.sql:1-4 states, correctly, that the CLI runs it only against a local instance, so the one environment holding real data is not affected by this mechanism at all; (2) the finding's own probes already found no disclosure, and it concedes "defence-in-depth lost, not a breach demonstrated."

Net: the observation is real and worth recording as a hardening note (seed.sql:68-72's predicted rot is a fair characterization of the coupling), but there is no reachable capability gain for any actor, in any environment, through any route. Not a MEDIUM security defect.

I tried to refute this and could not. Every cited fact checks out, and I reproduced the mechanism independently.

FILE CLAIMS — all verified verbatim in D:/projects/snowkap-cbam/supabase/seed.sql (110 lines total):
- :21-23 `grant all on all tables|sequences|functions in schema public to anon, authenticated, service_role;` — present exactly.
- :25-32 the three matching `alter default privileges ... grant all on tables|sequences|functions` — present.
- :83-110 the P14.3 block re-asserts exactly three things: calculation_results INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE revoke, record_calculation_result revoke+service_role grant, and TRUNCATE. Nothing else.
- :68-72 quote is accurate: "These statements mirror the migrations named above and must be updated with them... the alternative -- teaching this file which tables are special -- is a list that rots silently."

MIGRATION CLAIMS — verified by grep; each is `revoke all on function ... from public;` followed by `grant execute ... to authenticated` (so anon genuinely has no EXECUTE post-migration; the revoke-from-PUBLIC strips the Postgres default, which was my main hoped-for refutation and it fails):
  20260828080000_organization_onboarding_rpc.sql:107-108 create_organization_with_owner
  20260828120000_list_org_members_rpc.sql:77-78 and 20260829360000:320-321 list_org_members
  20260828130000_organization_invitations.sql:302-303 and 20260829380000:348-349 accept_organization_invitation
  20260829300000:627-628 and 20260829390000:282-283 accept_sharing_grant_invitation
  20260829310000_p7d3_shared_data_consumption_audit.sql:331-332 record_shared_data_consumption
  20260829330000_p9_declarations_schema.sql:1030-1031 record_declaration_filed
  20260831100000:95-97 and 20260902150000:194-196 sharing_counterparty_org_names (authenticated + service_role, not anon)
That is seven functions, as claimed. No migration anywhere re-revokes from anon except 20260903170000 (truncate) and 20260903190000 (calculation_results / record_calculation_result) — confirmed by `grep -rn "from anon|from public, anon|from authenticated" supabase/migrations/*.sql | grep -i revoke`, which returns only 20260903170000:48,54,68.

RE-RUNNING THE EVIDENCE: I could NOT re-read the finding's ACL dump on the main local DB — it currently has zero tables in schema public (`select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname='public'` -> 0; `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` does not exist), i.e. another agent wiped/reset it after the finding was written. So I reproduced the mechanism deterministically in a throwaway DB (created, then dropped) using the repository's ACTUAL seed.sql file:

  create database refute_seed_acl;
  -- mimic the migration pattern exactly:
  create function public.list_org_members(p_org uuid) ... security definer;
  revoke all on function public.list_org_members(uuid) from public;
  grant execute on function public.list_org_members(uuid) to authenticated;
  (plus record_calculation_result with the seed guard's identity args, narrowed to service_role, and calculation_results with INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE revoked)

  AFTER MIGRATIONS, BEFORE SEED:
    list_org_members|postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres
    record_calculation_result|postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres
    anon exec list_org_members = false

  psql -f D:/projects/snowkap-cbam/supabase/seed.sql   (the real file, unmodified)

  AFTER SEED:
    list_org_members|postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres
    record_calculation_result|postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres
    anon exec list_org_members = true
    anon exec record_calculation_result = false
    authenticated INSERT calculation_results = false

So the blanket `grant all on all functions` does hand EXECUTE back to anon for every function the P14.3 block does not name, while the three named narrowings survive. The finding's mechanism, its list, and its conclusion are correct.

SEVERITY CORRECTION (down from MEDIUM to LOW). Two facts the finding did not weigh: (1) seed.sql:2-4 states it "is never applied to any hosted Supabase project — the CLI runs this exclusively as the final step of `supabase db reset`/`start` against a local instance", so the hosted production ACL boundary is untouched; the exposure is confined to local dev and CI. (2) Every one of the seven is SECURITY DEFINER with its own auth gate — e.g. record_declaration_filed's body opens `if auth.uid() is null then raise exception` and then `if not app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(v_decl.org_id)`, and the app.* helpers stay narrowed because seed.sql only grants across schema `public`. The finding itself concedes no disclosure or write was demonstrated. That leaves a genuine but non-production defence-in-depth loss plus the real systemic point — the P14.3 fix repaired three instances rather than the mechanism, and the file's own predicted rot has already occurred. Real defect, correctly evidenced, lower blast radius than MEDIUM implies.

Trivial inaccuracies, not material: the finding cites 20260828080000:107 for the grant (107 is the revoke, 108 the grant), and attributes sharing_counterparty_org_names only to 20260902150000, omitting its origin at 20260831100000:95-97.

I could not refute the ACL fact; I reproduced it from scratch. But I found a mitigation the finder under-credited and one environment claim that is wrong, so severity drops MEDIUM -> LOW.

WHAT I CONFIRMED

1. The migrations really do write an anon-excluding grant. Exact lines (D:/projects/snowkap-cbam/supabase/migrations/):
   20260828080000_organization_onboarding_rpc.sql:107-108
   20260828120000_list_org_members_rpc.sql:77-78 and 20260829360000_p10_membership_deactivation.sql:320-321
   20260828130000_organization_invitations.sql:302-303 and 20260829380000_...:348-349
   20260829300000_...:627-628 and 20260829390000_...:282-283
   20260829310000_p7d3_shared_data_consumption_audit.sql:331-332
   20260829330000_p9_declarations_schema.sql:1030-1031
   20260902150000_..._terminal_grants.sql:194-196
   Each is `revoke all on function public.X(...) from public;` then `grant execute ... to authenticated;`. A repo-wide grep for `revoke ... from (anon|authenticated)` in supabase/migrations returns ONLY 20260903170000_p14_revoke_truncate_from_api_roles.sql:48,54,68 (TRUNCATE). No migration revokes function EXECUTE from anon.

2. The widening is real. I built a throwaway DB (opus_refute_localreset, since dropped) and ran the exact statement shapes:
   create function public.list_org_members(p_org_id uuid) ...; revoke all ... from public; grant execute ... to authenticated;
     -> AFTER MIGRATION : {postgres=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres}      <- anon absent
   then seed.sql:19-32 verbatim
     -> AFTER seed.sql  : {postgres=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres,anon=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}
     -> has_function_privilege('anon','public.list_org_members(uuid)','execute') = true
   supabase/seed.sql:83-101 re-asserts only record_calculation_result; :104-110 only TRUNCATE. Confirmed the mirror is incomplete exactly as claimed.

3. It really runs after the migrations in the gating environment. .github/workflows/ci.yml:315 runs `psql ... -f supabase/seed.sql` explicitly, AFTER `pnpm exec supabase migration up --local` (line 303). So CI's database does hold anon=X on all seven.

4. No test covers it: grep for has_function_privilege|proacl|'anon' across tests/ returns zero hits.

I could NOT re-run the finder's own probe: the shared local DB's public schema is currently empty (0 tables, 0 functions; supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist) — wiped by another agent. So I proved the mechanism instead.

WHY THIS IS LOW, NOT MEDIUM

Already-mitigated, by the primary designed control. All seven fail closed for an unauthenticated caller, and it is deliberate, not incidental:
  20260828080000:66-67, 20260829380000:194-195, 20260829390000:173-174, 20260829310000:128-129, 20260829330000:628-629 — each begins `if auth.uid() is null then raise exception`.
  list_org_members (20260829360000:283-290): `if not exists (select 1 from app.user_org_ids() as caller_org_id where caller_org_id = p_org_id) then raise exception 'Not a member of this organization.'`
  sharing_counterparty_org_names (20260902150000:135+): every branch gated by `in (select app.user_org_ids())`, empty when auth.uid() is null.
The comment at 20260829360000:311-315 states the design rule outright: SECURITY DEFINER "bypasses RLS entirely and must not rely on the caller having already been authorized elsewhere." The grant was never the load-bearing control here. The finder concedes no breach (2 of 7 probed, both denied); I verified the remaining 5 by source.

ONE FINDING CLAIM IS WRONG. "callable ... in every environment built by `supabase db reset` -- which is CI's environment and every developer's." supabase/config.toml:73 sets `sql_paths = ["./seed/*.sql"]`, and `supabase/seed/` does not exist (ls: No such file or directory) — seed.sql is not in the configured seed path. git log -p on config.toml shows `-sql_paths = ["./seed.sql"]` / `+sql_paths = ["./seed/*.sql"]` at commit 827d3a7. So a developer's plain `supabase db reset` plausibly does not run seed.sql at all; CI reaches this state only because ci.yml:315 invokes it by hand. The blast radius is CI, not "every developer's".

UNRESOLVED CAVEAT, stated rather than asserted. seed.sql:2-16 says it replicates grants the hosted platform sets at provisioning that a local reset loses. Local pg_default_acl shows the platform bootstrap does set, for schema public, `FOR ROLE supabase_admin ... GRANT ALL ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, authenticated, service_role` ({postgres=X,anon=X,authenticated=X,service_role=X}/supabase_admin). If hosted carries an equivalent FOR ROLE postgres entry (migrations run as postgres, and production tables plainly are reachable by anon/authenticated), then production functions get anon=X at CREATE time and `revoke ... from public` never removes it — I demonstrated that in a second throwaway DB: with those default privileges present, after the identical migration statements the ACL is {postgres=X,anon=X,authenticated=X,service_role=X} and has_function_privilege('anon',...) = true with seed.sql never running. That would mean the anon boundary never existed anywhere and the "seed.sql rot" framing is mis-attributed. I could not settle it: my read-only production ACL query via supabase/.temp/pooler-url was blocked by the permission classifier, so I made no production queries.

NET: the mechanism observation is sound and is exactly the failure class under hunt — seed.sql's blanket grant is a hand-maintained mirror that has already drifted past the three items P14.3 named, and CI's database is weaker than what the migrations specify, so a future RPC that relies on its grant rather than an internal auth.uid() check would be silently unprotected in the environment that tests it. Worth fixing. But there is no reachable impact today, no production exposure demonstrated, and the exclusion the finding calls "lost" may never have existed. LOW.

title: The `sequences` check compares only names, not values, while its stated purpose is to detect a wrong restored value
evidence: scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:224-233. The `why` reads 'a sequence restored at the wrong value collides on the next insert' but the SQL is `select sequence_schema || '.' || sequence_name from information_schema.sequences` -- no `last_value`, no `pg_sequence_last_value()`. Two databases whose sequences are at wildly different positions report `[MATCH] sequences`. In my probe2 restore it printed `[MATCH] sequences (0 rows both sides)`.
exploit: NONE -- structural, and inert today: this schema currently has zero sequences (all keys are uuid). The defect is that the check reads in the report as coverage it does not provide, so the first `bigserial`/`identity` column added to the schema silently inherits an untested claim.
impact: Low today. It matters as a pattern: this is the third check in the file whose `why` string promises more than its SQL delivers (the other two are findings 3 and 4), which is what makes a green run of this tool hard to trust at a glance during a recovery.
freshEnvironment: Yes -- a property of the script. Verified by reading the SQL and by the `0 rows both sides` output on a real restore.

verdicts.reasoning:
Re-ran the finding's evidence rather than trusting it.

CONFIRMED (code/comment mismatch is real): scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:224-233 has why = "a sequence restored at the wrong value collides on the next insert" and SQL = `select sequence_schema || '.' || sequence_name from information_schema.sequences where sequence_schema in ('public','app') order by 1` -- no last_value, no pg_sequence_last_value(). Reproduced empirically: created throwaway DBs seqprobe_a (t_id_seq last_value=5, via 5 inserts) and seqprobe_b (setval 999999), ran the real script against both; output included `[MATCH] sequences (1 rows both sides)` alongside 5 critical failures on other checks. Both DBs dropped; `select datname from pg_database where datname like 'seqprobe%'` now returns empty.

REFUTED on the stated impact mechanism. The finding's whole claim of harm is "the defect is that the check reads in the report as coverage it does not provide." It does not. Line 547 is the only match-path print: `[MATCH] ${check.name} (${sourceRows.length} rows both sides)` -- the `why` string is emitted ONLY on failure, at line 557 ([DIFFER]) and line 592 ([FAIL]). An operator running a green drill never sees the sentence that overpromises. It is a source comment, not report text.

REFUTED on documented coverage claims. docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md:519-537 and docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1388-1395 both enumerate the checks as "... indexes, sequences and extensions" -- an object-level claim that the SQL satisfies exactly. `grep -rn -i "sequence" docs/` surfaces no claim anywhere that sequence VALUES are compared. So no artifact a human reads carries the overpromise.

REFUTED on reachability (the lens assigned). No actor, no path, no object:
- `select count(*) from information_schema.sequences where sequence_schema in ('public','app')` -> 0
- `select n.nspname||'.'||c.relname from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace where c.relkind='S' and n.nspname in ('public','app')` -> empty
- identity/serial column scan (`is_identity='YES' or column_default like 'nextval%'` over public/app) -> empty
- `grep -rn "bigserial\|serial\b\|generated always as identity\|generated by default as identity" supabase/migrations/` -> no matches
The only sequences in the cluster are auth(1), realtime(1), supabase_functions(1), all outside the check's schema filter.

Also worth noting against the premise: sequence last_value is data state, not security posture. The script's own header scopes it to "the SECURITY POSTURE of two Postgres databases, object by object." A source that kept taking writes after its dump would legitimately diverge in last_value, so adding that comparison as written would manufacture false failures in exactly the recovery scenario the tool exists for. The correct remedy is a one-word reword of a comment, not added coverage.

Net: the finding's factual observation about the SQL is accurate, but its harm, its "reads in the report" mechanism, and its reachability are all falsified. What survives is an inaccurate code comment on a check marked `critical: false` that currently matches zero objects and whose text never reaches a report. That is below a defect threshold -- INFO, a comment nit, not an operations finding. The forward-looking part ("the first bigserial added silently inherits an untested claim") depends on a schema change that does not exist and is contradicted by ADR-0009 identity policy / uuid keys throughout.

I re-ran every piece of the evidence and the finding's factual claims are all correct. Downgrading severity to INFO, with a caveat that partly defends the implementation.

1. The cited code is exactly as quoted. D:\projects\snowkap-cbam\scripts\ops\compare-database-posture.mjs:223-233:

  {
    name: "sequences",
    critical: false,
    why: "a sequence restored at the wrong value collides on the next insert",
    sql: `
      select sequence_schema || '.' || sequence_name
      from information_schema.sequences
      where sequence_schema in ('public', 'app')
      order by 1
    `,
  },

No `last_value`, no `pg_sequence_last_value()`. The `why` string does promise value-level detection that the SQL does not perform. Claim confirmed by reading the file.

2. The view it queries is structurally incapable of reporting position. SQL run:
  select string_agg(column_name, ', ' order by ordinal_position) from information_schema.columns where table_schema='information_schema' and table_name='sequences'
Output:
  sequence_catalog, sequence_schema, sequence_name, data_type, numeric_precision, numeric_precision_radix, numeric_scale, start_value, minimum_value, maximum_value, increment, cycle_option
There is no `last_value` column, so no rewrite of this query against this view could detect a wrong restored value. This strengthens the finding rather than refuting it.

3. The "inert today" claim is confirmed. SQL run:
  select sequence_schema || '.' || sequence_name from information_schema.sequences where sequence_schema in ('public','app') order by 1
Output: (zero rows, exit 0).
  select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema in ('public','app') and (column_default like 'nextval%' or is_identity='YES')
Output: 0
Cluster-wide, the only sequences are outside the check's schema filter entirely:
  auth.refresh_tokens_id_seq | last_value=10
  realtime.subscription_id_seq | last_value=NULL
  supabase_functions.hooks_id_seq | last_value=NULL
And `grep -rniE "bigserial|serial\b|generated (always|by default) as identity" supabase/migrations/` returns no matches. All keys are uuid, as the finding says.

4. The claimed output string is what the code emits. With zero rows on both sides, `diff()` returns two empty arrays and line 546-548 prints `[MATCH] ${check.name} (${sourceRows.length} rows both sides)` = `[MATCH] sequences (0 rows both sides)`. Exactly as reported.

Why I correct LOW to INFO. Two things the finding does not weigh:
(a) This is `critical: false`, so it can never contribute to `criticalFailures`, and the object class it covers has zero members with no roadmap item introducing one.
(b) More substantively, the SQL's choice is arguably correct and the prose is merely loose. `CHECKS` is a source-vs-target comparison between a live source and a restored target. A live source's sequences advance continuously; a restored target's do not. Comparing `last_value` across the two would report a difference on essentially every real restore of a healthy database — a false-positive generator in exactly the recovery situation the script exists for. The defensible check for this list is identity (a sequence missing from, or extra in, the target), which is what the SQL does. The genuine defect is therefore confined to the `why` string overstating the coverage; the behavior is not wrong. That is a documentation inaccuracy in a non-critical check, which is INFO, not LOW.

Not refuted: the mismatch between stated purpose and implemented SQL is real, reproduced, and I confirmed it independently. It simply does not rise to LOW.

CONFIRMED by independent code read plus a live empirical reproduction; I looked for a mitigation and found none.

1. Code, verbatim, at D:\projects\snowkap-cbam\scripts\ops\compare-database-posture.mjs:223-233 (line numbers exactly as the finding claims):

```
223:  {
224:    name: "sequences",
225:    critical: false,
226:    why: "a sequence restored at the wrong value collides on the next insert",
227:    sql: `
228:      select sequence_schema || '.' || sequence_name
229:      from information_schema.sequences
230:      where sequence_schema in ('public', 'app')
231:      order by 1
232:    `,
233:  },
```

The `why` at :226 is about the VALUE; the SQL at :228-230 projects only `sequence_schema || '.' || sequence_name`. No `last_value`, no `pg_sequence_last_value()`, no `pg_sequences`. This is inconsistent with the file's own pattern for its sibling checks, which do compare definition text, not just identity: `indexes` selects `|| indexdef` (:216-217), `constraints` selects `|| pg_get_constraintdef(con.oid)` (:200-201), `functions` selects a body hash (:154).

2. Live reproduction (not taken on trust from the finder). I created two throwaway databases in the local cluster, identical in schema, differing only in sequence position:

  psql -d seqprobe_a -tAc "create table t(id bigserial primary key, x text)"; insert 5 rows
  psql -d seqprobe_b -tAc "create table t(id bigserial primary key, x text)"; insert 90000 rows

  select 'A last_value=' || last_value from t_id_seq  ->  A last_value=5
  select 'B last_value=' || last_value from t_id_seq  ->  B last_value=90000

  node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs \
    "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/seqprobe_a" \
    "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/seqprobe_b"

  Output included, verbatim:
    [MATCH] sequences (1 rows both sides)

A 5-vs-90000 divergence — precisely the "restored at the wrong value collides on the next insert" scenario the `why` names — reports MATCH. (Both probe databases dropped afterward; `select datname from pg_database` confirms neither remains.)

3. The finding's "inert today" qualifier is also correct:
   select sequence_schema||'.'||sequence_name from information_schema.sequences where sequence_schema in ('public','app') order by 1;
   -> 0 rows (exit 0). The cluster has 3 sequences total (`select count(*) from pg_class where relkind='S'` -> 3), all outside public/app, i.e. outside this check's WHERE clause. So there is no exploit and no present impact.

4. ALREADY-MITIGATED lens — searched, nothing covers it:
   - grep for `last_value|pg_sequence|setval|nextval|bigserial|identity` across scripts/ and supabase/migrations/ returns no sequence-value assertion anywhere; the only hits in the ops script are the two lines above plus unrelated `pg_get_function_identity_arguments`.
   - scripts/ops/ contains only this one file. No trigger, CHECK, policy or later migration is relevant (a sequence value is not constrainable that way).
   - No test exercises the script: the only non-.git references to `compare-database-posture` are docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md, docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md, docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md and the script itself.
   - docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md:533-538 lists "...constraints, indexes, sequences and extensions" without claiming value comparison, so the runbook does not compound it — but it does not supply the missing check either.

Nuance that tempers, but does not refute, the finding: comparing `last_value` between a live source and a restored target would legitimately produce spurious mismatches, because the source keeps calling nextval after the dump is taken. So name-only SQL is a defensible implementation choice; the actual defect is that the `why` string states a purpose the SQL does not serve, in a tool whose entire reason for existing (per its own header, :6-18) is that the 2026-09-03 drill ran checks that passed while missing what mattered. Severity LOW stands: no exploit, no present impact, non-critical check, and the fix is either to reword :226 or to add a `pg_sequence_last_value()` projection guarded for the live-source case.

title: BACKUP_RESTORE.md's fidelity table says the target project supplies the `storage` schema, but the `evidence` bucket and the three `storage.objects` RLS policies are this application's own access control and are in neither the dump nor any check
evidence:
docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md:622 lists '`auth`, `storage`, `extensions`, `vault`, `realtime` schemas | NO | the target project provides them'. A fresh Supabase project provides `storage.buckets` and `storage.objects` as tables, but not:
  supabase/migrations/20260829240000_p7c_evidence_files_schema.sql:264  insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public) values ('evidence','evidence',false)
  :268 create policy evidence_storage_select_own_org on storage.objects ... to authenticated
  :277 create policy evidence_storage_insert_own_org on storage.objects ... to authenticated
  :286 create policy evidence_storage_delete_own_org on storage.objects ... to authenticated

The dump is `--schema=public --schema=app` (BACKUP_RESTORE.md:145-146), so none of these are in it. The comparator scopes every check to `('public','app')` -- `pg_policies where schemaname in ('public','app')` at scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:118, and the three storage-relevant self-checks all filter `n.nspname = 'public'` (lines 320, 334, 351). Nothing in the tool can see the storage schema.

Nor can it be verified locally at all: supabase/config.toml:170 has `[storage] enabled = false`, and
  select nspname, count(c.oid) from pg_namespace n left join pg_class c on c.relnamespace=n.oid group by 1;
  -> storage|0
The local `storage` schema holds zero relations, so the bucket and the three policies have never executed on this machine -- which config.toml:130-140 already documents honestly.
exploit: NONE -- structural. After a restore into a fresh project the `evidence` bucket row does not exist and `storage.objects` carries RLS with none of this application's policies, so every evidence upload and every signed-URL read fails until an operator notices and re-runs that migration's Part 5. The runbook's 'required post-restore steps' (BACKUP_RESTORE.md, section D.3) name auth.users, the revokes and the ledger, but not this.
impact: A recovery that completes with `POSTURE MATCHES` and a working application still has evidence upload and download entirely broken, with no gate that says so. The fidelity table's 'the target project provides them' is true for the storage tables and false for the three access-control policies and the bucket that this codebase created in them. Low severity because the failure mode is denial rather than disclosure, and because it surfaces on first use -- but it belongs in the post-restore step list.
freshEnvironment: Yes -- it is a property of the dump scope, the comparator's schema filters, and the runbook's table, all read at the release-candidate commit. The local-verifiability half is confirmed against the running local database (`storage` schema, 0 relations).

verdicts.reasoning:
I re-ran every citation and could not refute the substance.

VERIFIED FACTS (my own checks):

The restore path is also real -- BACKUP_RESTORE.md:685-690 names the logical dump as "the *only* path" for platform-level loss, i.e. restore into a fresh project where Part 5 never ran. No missing capability, no missing route.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG (why I downgrade rather than confirm at LOW):

Evidence files live in the `evidence` bucket... full recovery... depends on... whatever covers the Storage bucket", and :620 repeats it in the same table. :638 already declares "Recovery is **not proven**", and :618 tells the reader schema/policies are "also reproducible by re-running the migration set". 4. The local-verifiability half is pre-documented by the codebase itself (config.toml:124-167, P13_RELEASE_READINESS_REPORT.md:581, :4724), which record that the storage-touching migrations were tracked via `supabase migration repair` and are shim-verified only. That is disclosed, not concealed.

Net: the technical core is confirmed and I will not refute it, but it is a documentation-completeness note (add the bucket + 3 policies to the restore checklist) on a procedure the document already labels unproven and already flags storage as out of scope for -- no security consequence, denial-only, self-announcing on first use. INFO rather than LOW.

Every substantive claim re-verified independently. (1) docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md:622 quoted exactly: "| `auth`, `storage`, `extensions`, `vault`, `realtime` schemas | **NO** | the target project provides them |". (2) supabase/migrations/20260829240000_p7c_evidence_files_schema.sql:264-266 inserts the 'evidence' bucket and :268/:277/:286 create evidence_storage_select_own_org / _insert_own_org / _delete_own_org on storage.objects to authenticated; I read lines 220-300 and confirmed Part 5 is unconditional, with no existence guard.
